<!-- thm-1: body_md -->
\label{thm: main intro}
    Let $\pi: M \to B$ be a good compactified Prym fibration.\\
    (a) There is an isomorphism of complex mixed Hodge structures up to Tate twists $H^*(M; {\mathbb{C}}) \cong H^*(IM^\vee; {\mathbb{C}})$.\\
    (b) There is a motivic decomposition of $R\pi_* {\mathbb{Q}}_M$ into its shifted perverse components.\\
    (c) The perverse filtration $P_\bullet H^*(M; {\mathbb{C}})$ is multiplicative with respect to cup product.
<!-- end thm-1 -->
<!-- rmk-1: body_md -->
The Hitchin fibration for $M_{\operatorname{SL}_n}(C)$ is not a good compactified Prym fibration as defined above; it is a compactified Prym fibration for a family of curves including non-integral (both non-irreducible and non-reduced) members. In general it appears difficult to extend Arinkin's Poincar\'e sheaf, which plays a key role in the proof, to a family of curves with non-reduced members. In \cite[\S 5.4]{MSY}, for the case of $M_{\operatorname{GL}_n}(C)$, this difficulty is circumvented using Springer theory and suitable moduli spaces of parabolic Higgs bundles.
    This argument does not immediately generalize to $\operatorname{SL}_n$, but in upcoming work we will present a different proof of the multiplicativity of the perverse filtration on $H^*(M_{\operatorname{SL}_n}(C))$. It is also worth pointing out that in contrast to the case of $\operatorname{GL}_n$, the multiplicativity statement is not enough to complete the proof of the $P=W$ conjecture for $\operatorname{SL}_n$, which remains open in general.
    (Indeed, as far as the author is aware, there is currently no literature on the weight filtration on the non-$\Gamma$-fixed classes of the $\operatorname{SL}_n$ character variety when $n$ is composite, other than the $E$-polynomial computation in \cite{Mereb}.)
<!-- end rmk-1 -->
<!-- rmk-2: body_md -->
\label{rmk: LSV}
    Our use of the term \textit{compactified Prym fibration} for the situation of a family of (possibly singular) curves with a (not necessarily \'etale) degree $n$ morphism to a fixed smooth base curve should be contrasted with the compactified Prym fibrations discussed, e.g., in \cite{LSV}, for an \'etale double cover of a family of (possibly singular, non-fixed) base curves. The recent preprint \cite{Huishi} shows that an \'etale double cover-type compactified Prym is a dualizable abelian fibration, i.e., that the results of \cite{MSY} apply directly. (Although the two definitions of Prym variety are not entirely comparable except in the case of an \'etale double cover of a smooth base curve, an important difference is that the \cite{LSV} definition includes only the connected component of the identity, whereas ours takes the whole kernel of the norm map. Taking only the identity component has the effect of restricting the discussion to abelian schemes, rather than abelian scheme extensions of finite groups, so that the \cite{MSY} setup suffices for the purposes of \cite{Huishi}.)
<!-- end rmk-2 -->
<!-- defn-1: body_md -->
\label{defn: nice quotient}
    By \textit{nice quotient} we will mean a quotient stack $[X/G]$, where $X$ is a quasiprojective complex variety equipped with an action of a finite abelian group $G$. Given a stack $\mathcal X$, we use \textit{nice presentation} to mean a global quotient presentation $\mathcal X = [X/G]$ of this form.
<!-- end defn-1 -->
<!-- lem-1: body_md -->
\label{lemma: pushforward exterior product}
    If $i: X \to X'$, respectively $j: Y \to Y'$, is a proper and $G$-, respectively $H$-, equivariant morphism of quasiprojective varieties, then
    $$(i \times j)_*(\mathcal F \boxtimes \mathcal G) = (i_* \mathcal F) \boxtimes (j_* \mathcal G) \in K_0(\mathcal X' \times \mathcal Y')$$
    for $\mathcal F \in K_0(\mathcal X)$ and $\mathcal G \in K_0(\mathcal Y)$.
<!-- end lem-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
We start with the corresponding statement at the level of non-equivariant complexes of sheaves.
    Consider the Cartesian squares
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
	{X \times Y} & {X' \times Y} & Y \\
	{X \times Y'} & {X' \times Y'} & {Y'} \\
	X & {X'} & {\operatorname{Spec} {\mathbb{C}}}
	\arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow[from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow[from=1-2, to=1-3]
	\arrow[from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow[from=1-3, to=2-3, "a"]
	\arrow[from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow[from=2-1, to=3-1]
	\arrow[from=2-2, to=2-3]
	\arrow[from=2-2, to=3-2]
	\arrow[from=2-3, to=3-3, "b"]
	\arrow[from=3-1, to=3-2, "c"]
	\arrow[from=3-2, to=3-3, "d"]
\end{tikzcd}\]
    (where we use the same letter to denote all parallel arrows, and all functors are assumed derived). Then, for $\mathscr F \in D^b\mathrm{Coh}(X)$ and $\mathscr G \in D^b\mathrm{Coh}(Y)$, we have
    $$(i \times j)_*(\mathscr F \boxtimes \mathscr G) := c_* a_*((a^*b^*\mathscr F) \otimes (c^*d^* \mathscr G)) = c_*(b^* \mathscr F \otimes a_*c^*d^*\mathscr G)$$
    by the projection formula \cite[Tag 08EU]{stacks-project}. Next, note that $X \times Y'$ and $X' \times Y$ are $\operatorname{Tor}$-independent over $X' \times Y'$, and so we have the base change formula $a_* c^* = c^* a_*$ \cite[Tag 08IB]{stacks-project}. Thus
    $$ c_*(b^* \mathscr F \otimes a_*c^*d^*\mathscr G) = c_*(b^* \mathscr F \otimes c^*a_*d^*\mathscr G) = (c_*b^* \mathscr F) \otimes (a_*d^* \mathscr G)$$
    by another application of the projection formula. Now, as $d$ and $b$ are flat, by another application of base-change, we have
    $$(c_* b^* \mathscr F) \otimes (a_* d^* \mathscr G) = (b^* c_* \mathscr F) \otimes (d^* a_* \mathscr G) = c_* \mathscr F \boxtimes a_* \mathscr G =: i_* \mathscr F \boxtimes j_* \mathscr G.$$
    Finally, note that since all isomorphisms involved are canonical, they respect the $(G \times H)$-equivariant structure.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- prop-1: body_md -->
\label{prop: Thomason localization}
    \cite[Th\'eor\`eme 2.1]{Thomason} Given $g \in G$, the inclusion of the fixed locus $\iota: X^g \hookrightarrow X$ induces an isomorphism $\iota_*: K_0(\mathcal X^g)_{\mathfrak m_g} \xrightarrow{\sim} K_0(\mathcal X)_{\mathfrak m_g}$.
<!-- end prop-1 -->
<!-- lem-2: body_md -->
\label{lem: localization inverse}
    Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and $f: X \hookrightarrow Y$ a $G$-equivariant closed embedding of quasiprojective varieties, with $Y$ being smooth. Let $f_g: X^g \to Y^g$ be the restriction to the fixed loci and $\iota_Y: Y^g \hookrightarrow Y$ the inclusion. Then
    $$f_g^* (\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_{\iota_{\mathcal Y}})^{-1}) \cdot \iota_{\mathcal Y}^!: K_0(\mathcal X)_{\mathfrak m_g} \to K_0(\mathcal X^g)_{\mathfrak m_g}$$
    is inverse to the isomorphism $\iota_{\mathcal X*}$, where $\mathcal N_{\iota_{\mathcal Y}}^\vee \in K^0(\mathcal Y^g)$ is the class of the conormal bundle and $\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_{\iota_{\mathcal Y}})^{-1} \in K^0(\mathcal Y^g)_{\mathfrak m_g}$ is the unique class such that $\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_{\iota_{\mathcal Y}})^{-1} \cdot \lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_{\iota_{\mathcal Y}}) = 1 \in K^0(\mathcal Y^g)_{\mathfrak m_g}$ \cite[Lemme 3.3]{Thomason}.
<!-- end lem-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
First, since $Y$ is smooth, we see that $\mathscr O_{Y^g}$ is an $\iota_Y$-perfect complex, with $X \times_Y Y^g = X^g$, so that the above gives a well-defined morphism $K_0(\mathcal X) \to K_0(\mathcal X^g)$. Moreover, both the Gysin morphism and the $K^0(\mathcal X^g)$-action commute with the action of $K^0(BG)$, and we obtain a morphism of $\mathfrak m_g$-localizations.

    Also, since $\iota_{\mathcal X*}$ is an isomorphism and $\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_{\iota_{\mathcal Y}}) \in K^0(\mathcal Y^g)_{\mathfrak m_g}$ is invertible, it suffices to prove that
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: nonsmooth localization}
        \iota_{\mathcal X*}(\iota_{\mathcal Y}^!(\iota_{\mathcal X*}\mathcal F)) = \iota_{\mathcal X*}(f_g^* (\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_{\iota_{\mathcal Y}})) \cdot  \mathcal F)
    \end{equation}
    for any $\mathcal F \in K_0(\mathcal X^g)_{\mathfrak m_g}$.
    
    For any $F \in \mathrm{Coh}(X^g)$ we have (with all functors derived)
    \begin{multline} \label{eq: Thomason 3.3}
    \iota_{Y*} \iota_Y^* f_* \iota_{X*} F = \iota_{Y*} \iota_Y^*\iota_{Y*} f_{g*} F = \iota_{Y*} \mathscr O_{Y^g} \otimes \iota_{Y*} f_{g*} F = \iota_{Y*}(\iota_Y^* \iota_{Y*} \mathscr O_{Y^g} \otimes f_{g*} F) \\
    = \iota_{Y*} f_{g*}(f_g^*(\iota_Y^* \iota_{Y*} \mathscr O_{Y^g}) \otimes F) = f_* \iota_{X*}(f_g^*(\iota_Y^* \iota_{Y*} \mathscr O_{Y^g}) \otimes F)
    \end{multline}
    by repeated applications of the projection formula \cite[08EU]{stacks-project}. Now, viewing both sides of (\ref{eq: Thomason 3.3}) as sheaves on $X \subset Y$, we have
    $$[\iota_{Y*} \iota_Y^* f_* \iota_{X*} F ] = [\iota_{X*}(f_g^*(\iota_Y^* \iota_{Y*} \mathscr O_{Y^g}) \otimes F)] \in K_0(\mathcal X).$$
    On the left side, by definition
    $$ \iota_Y^!(\iota_{X*} [F]) = [\iota_Y^* f_* \iota_{X*} F] \in K_0(X^g),$$
    considering the right side as a complex supported on $X^g$, and so since pushing forward by closed immersions doesn't change this complex, we have
    $$\iota_{X*}(\iota_Y^!(\iota_{X*} [F]))) = [\iota_{Y*} \iota_Y^* f_* \iota_{X*} F].$$
    On the right side, we have
    $$[\iota_{X*}(f_g^*(\iota_Y^* \iota_{Y*} \mathscr O_{Y^g}) \otimes F)] = \iota_{X*}(f_g^*([\iota_Y^* \iota_{Y*} \mathscr O_{Y^g}] \cdot [F])) = \iota_{X*}(f_g^* (\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N_{\iota_Y}^\vee)) \cdot [F])$$
    by \cite[(3.3.3)]{Thomason}. Moreover, since all the isomorphisms involved are canonical, if $F \in \mathrm{Coh}(X^g)$ is $G$-equivariant, then the identities above hold for equivariant sheaves. Since $K_0(\mathcal X^g)_{\mathfrak m_g}$ is generated over $K^0(BG)_{\mathfrak m_g}$ by the classes of $G$-equivariant sheaves and equation (\ref{eq: nonsmooth localization}) is $K^0(BG)_{\mathfrak m_g}$-linear, this completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- defn-2: body_md -->
\label{defn: tauEG}
    If $\mathcal X = [X/G]$ is a nice quotient, the Edidin-Graham tau functor $\tau^{EG}$ is defined by
    $$\tau^{EG}: K_0(\mathcal X) \xrightarrow{p^*} K_0(X_G) \xrightarrow{\tau^F} \operatorname{CH}_*(X_G)_{\mathbb{Q}} \rightarrow \operatorname{CH}_{*-\dim V}(\mathcal X)_{\mathbb{Q}}$$
    where the first arrow is $G$-equivariant flat pullback along the map $X \times U \to X$, the second is Fulton's $\tau$ functor \cite[Theorem 18.2]{Fulton}, and the third is the identification in the definition of $\operatorname{CH}_*(\mathcal X)$ in degrees $* \ge \dim V$ and 0 otherwise.
<!-- end defn-2 -->
<!-- rmk-3: body_md -->
This appears to differ from the definition in \cite[\S 3.2]{EG-RRequivChow} by a factor of $\operatorname{td}^G(V)$. However, since $G$ is finite abelian, $V$ is a sum of irreducible 1-dimensional representations $V_i$, where ${\mathrm{ch}}_1^G(V_i) = 0 \in \operatorname{CH}_*(\mathcal X)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ since $V_i^{\otimes |G|}$ is the trivial representation.
<!-- end rmk-3 -->
<!-- rmk-4: body_md -->
\label{rmk: tauEG independent}
    Choosing two nice presentations $\mathcal X = [X/G] = [Y/H]$, by pulling back to $X_G \times_{\mathcal X} Y_H$ and using the compatibility of $\tau^F$ with smooth pullback \cite[Theorem 18.3(4)]{Fulton}, we see that $\tau^{EG}$ is in fact independent of the choice of nice presentation.
<!-- end rmk-4 -->
<!-- example-1: body_md -->
\label{ex: need stacky tau}
    Consider the nonrepresentable morphism $f: BG \to \operatorname{Spec} {\mathbb{C}}$, for $G$ a nontrivial finite abelian group. Let $p:U/G \to BG$ be an approximation scheme, and $V \in K_0(BG)$ the class of a nontrivial 1-dimensional representation. Then
    $$\tau^{EG}(V) = [BG] \in \operatorname{CH}_*(BG)_{\mathbb{Q}} = \operatorname{CH}_0(BG)_{{\mathbb{Q}}}$$ since
    $$\tau^F(p^* V) = \operatorname{td}(p^* V) \cap \operatorname{Td}(U/G) = [U/G] + \ldots $$
    so in particular
    $$f_* \tau^{EG}(V) = \frac{1}{|G|} [\operatorname{Spec} {\mathbb{C}}] \ne 0 \in \operatorname{CH}_*(\operatorname{Spec} {\mathbb{C}})_{\mathbb{Q}},$$
    whereas $f_* V = V^G = 0$ and so $\tau^{EG}(f_* V) = 0$.
<!-- end example-1 -->
<!-- prop-2: body_md -->
\label{prop: EG factors through m1}
    The functors ${\mathrm{ch}}^{EG}, \operatorname{td}^{EG}: K^0(\mathcal X) \to \operatorname{CH}^*(\mathcal X)_{\mathbb{Q}}$, respectively $\tau^{EG}: K_0(\mathcal X) \to \operatorname{CH}_*(\mathcal X)_{\mathbb{Q}}$, factor through the projection $K^0(\mathcal X) \to K^0(\mathcal X)_{\mathfrak m_1}$, respectively $K_0(\mathcal X) \to K_0(\mathcal X)_{\mathfrak m_1}$.
<!-- end prop-2 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Given $\mathcal F \in \ker(K^0(\mathcal X) \to K^0(\mathcal X)_{\mathfrak m_1})$, there must be some $r \in K^0(BG) \setminus \mathfrak m_1$ such that $r \cdot \mathcal F = 0$. Note that ${\mathrm{ch}}^{EG} = \mathrm{rk}: K^0(BG) \to \operatorname{CH}^*(BG) = \operatorname{CH}^0(BG) = {\mathbb{Z}}$ has kernel $\mathfrak m_1$. Now, letting $q: \mathcal X \to BG$ be given by the projection $X \to \operatorname{Spec} {\mathbb{C}}$, we have
    $$0 = {\mathrm{ch}}^{EG}(r \cdot \mathcal F) = q^*{\mathrm{ch}}^{EG}(r) \cap {\mathrm{ch}}^{EG}(\mathcal F) \in \operatorname{CH}^*(\mathcal X)$$
    and since $q^* {\mathrm{ch}}^{EG}(r)$ is given by multiplication by a nonzero integer, we conclude that ${\mathrm{ch}}^{EG}(\mathcal F) = 0$. Thus ${\mathrm{ch}}^{EG}$ factors through the projection to $K^0(\mathcal X)_{\mathfrak m_1}$, and since $\operatorname{td}^{EG}$ is defined in terms of ${\mathrm{ch}}^{EG}$, the same is true of $\operatorname{td}^{EG}$.

    Finally, the needed statement for $\tau^{EG}$ is \cite[Corollary 5.1]{EG-RRequivChow}.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- defn-3: body_md -->
\label{defn: stacky tau}
    Given a nice quotient $\mathcal X = [X/G]$,
    the stacky tau functor $\tau: K_0(\mathcal X)_{\mathbb{C}} \to \operatorname{CH}_*(I\mathcal X)_{\mathbb{C}}$ is defined by
    $$\tau: K_0(\mathcal X)_{\mathbb{C}} \xrightarrow{\pi} \oplus_{g \in G} K_0(\mathcal X)_{\mathfrak m_g, {\mathbb{C}}} \xrightarrow{\iota_*^{-1}} \oplus_{g \in G} K_0(\mathcal X^g)_{\mathfrak m_g, {\mathbb{C}}} \xrightarrow{\rho} \oplus_{g \in G} K_0(\mathcal X^g)_{\mathfrak m_1, {\mathbb{C}}}$$
    $$\xrightarrow{\tau^{EG}} \oplus_{g \in G} \operatorname{CH}_*(\mathcal X^g)_{\mathbb{C}} = \operatorname{CH}_*(I\mathcal X)_{\mathbb{C}}$$
    where the isomorphisms $\pi, (\iota_*)^{-1}, \rho, \tau^{EG}$ are defined in equations (\ref{eq: pi}), (\ref{eq: iota}), (\ref{eq: rho}), (\ref{eq: tauEG}), respectively, and the last identification comes from the description of $I\mathcal X$ in (\ref{eq: inertia stack description}).
<!-- end defn-3 -->
<!-- rmk-5: body_md -->
In the smooth case, this is the Edidin-Graham definition as found in, e.g., \cite[Theorem 5.1]{Edidin-RRforDM}, using Thomason's explicit description of $\iota_*^{-1}$ \cite[Lemme 3.3]{Thomason}. We will see in Corollary \ref{cor: agrees with Toen} that this $\tau$ also matches the functor constructed by To\"en in \cite[Th\'eor\`eme 4.10(3)]{Toen} (and thus in particular is independent of the choice of nice presentation). However, the author is not aware of a literature reference for Definition \ref{defn: stacky tau} in this form in the singular case; Edidin-Graham only work with smooth stacks, whereas To\"en uses smooth hyperresolutions to extend his tau functor in the singular case. In any case, this more concrete definition is useful in proving the needed properties of $\tau$.
<!-- end rmk-5 -->
<!-- defn-4: body_md -->
\label{defn: stacky ch}
    The stacky Chern character is the ring homomorphism
    $$\operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}: K^0(\mathcal X)_{\mathbb{C}} \xrightarrow{\iota^*} K^0(I\mathcal X)_{\mathbb{C}} \xrightarrow{\rho} K^0(I\mathcal X)_{\mathbb{C}} \xrightarrow{{\mathrm{ch}}^{EG}} \operatorname{CH}^*(I \mathcal X)_{\mathbb{C}}.$$
<!-- end defn-4 -->
<!-- prop-3: body_md -->
\label{prop: moving part of ttd}
    There is a group homomorphism $K^0(I \mathcal X)^{\operatorname{mov}} \to (\operatorname{CH}^*(I \mathcal X)_{\mathbb{C}})^\times$ uniquely defined by the property of extending ${\mathrm{ch}}^{EG} \circ \rho \circ \lambda_{-1}$ on classes $v \in K^0(I \mathcal X)^{\operatorname{mov}}$ for which $\lambda_{-1}(v)$ is well-defined. We again call this extended morphism ${\mathrm{ch}}^{EG} \circ \rho \circ \lambda_{-1}$.
<!-- end prop-3 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
We start by noting that $K^0(I \mathcal X)^{\operatorname{mov}}$ is generated by classes of equivariant vector bundles $V = V^{\operatorname{mov}}$, where $\lambda_{-1}([V])$ is well-defined and furthermore, on each component of $I\mathcal X$ we have that
    $$\rho \circ \lambda_{-1}([V]) = \sum_{i = 0}^{\mathrm{rk} V} (-1)^i \rho ([\wedge^i V])$$
    is of virtual rank
    $$\prod_{\zeta \ne 1} (1 - \zeta)^{\dim V_\zeta} \ne 0$$
    so that ${\mathrm{ch}}^{EG}(\rho \circ \lambda_{-1}(V))$ is invertible. It remains to note that given an identity $[V] = [V'] + [V'']$, we have $\lambda_{-1}([V]) = \lambda_{-1}([V']) \cdot \lambda_{-1}([V''])$ and thus also
    $${\mathrm{ch}}^{EG} \circ \rho \circ \lambda_{-1}([V]) = {\mathrm{ch}}^{EG} \circ \rho \circ \lambda_{-1}([V']) \cap {\mathrm{ch}}^{EG} \circ \rho \circ \lambda_{-1}([V'']).$$
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- defn-5: body_md -->
\label{defn: stacky td}
    We define an operation $\operatorname{td}^I: K^0(I\mathcal X) \to \operatorname{CH}^*(I\mathcal X)_{\mathbb{C}}$ by
    $$\operatorname{td}^I(\mathcal E) := ({\mathrm{ch}}^{EG} \circ \rho \circ \lambda_{-1})(( \mathcal E^{\operatorname{mov}})^{\vee})^{-1} \cap \operatorname{td}^{EG}(\mathcal E^{\operatorname{fix}}) \in \operatorname{CH}^*(I \mathcal X)_{\mathbb{C}},$$
    where the first term is defined in Proposition \ref{prop: moving part of ttd}.
    The stacky Todd class of $\mathcal F \in K^0(\mathcal X)$ is 
    defined by
    $$\operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(\mathcal F) := \operatorname{td}^I(\iota^*\mathcal F).$$
<!-- end defn-5 -->
<!-- prop-4: body_md -->
\label{prop: ttd properties}
    Let $f: \mathcal X \to \mathcal Y$ be a morphism of nice quotients.\\
    (a) We have
    $$If^* \operatorname{td}^I(\mathcal E) = \operatorname{td}^I(If^* \mathcal E) \in \operatorname{CH}^*(I \mathcal X)_{\mathbb{C}}$$
    for any $\mathcal E \in K^0(I\mathcal Y)$. In particular
    $$If^*\operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(\mathcal F) = \operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(f^* \mathcal F) \in \operatorname{CH}^*(I \mathcal X)$$
    for any $\mathcal F \in K^0(\mathcal Y)$. The respective statements also hold for ${\mathrm{ch}}^I := {\mathrm{ch}}^{EG} \circ \rho$ and $\operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}$.\\
    (b) If $f$ is in addition proper, we have
    $$If_*(\operatorname{td}^I(If^* \mathcal E) \cap \alpha) = \operatorname{td}^I(\mathcal E) \cap If_* \alpha \in \operatorname{CH}_*(I \mathcal Y)_{\mathbb{C}}$$
    for any $\mathcal E \in K^0(I\mathcal Y)$ and $\alpha \in \operatorname{CH}_*(I\mathcal X)$. In particular
    $$If_*(\operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(f^* \mathcal F) \cap \alpha) = \operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(\mathcal F) \cap If_* \alpha \in \operatorname{CH}_*(I \mathcal Y)_{\mathbb{C}}$$
    for any $\mathcal F \in K^0(\mathcal Y)$ and $\alpha \in \operatorname{CH}_*(I \mathcal X)$.
<!-- end prop-4 -->
<!-- thm-2: body_md -->
\label{thm: tau properties}
    Let $\mathcal X$ and $\mathcal Y$ be nice quotients.\\
                                      
                                                                                       
    (a) For any $\mathcal F \in K_0(\mathcal X)$ and $\mathcal E \in K^0(\mathcal X)$ we have
    $$\tau(\mathcal E \cdot \mathcal F) = \operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}(\mathcal E) \cap \tau(\mathcal F) \in \operatorname{CH}_*(I\mathcal X)_{\mathbb{C}}.$$
    (b) For $\mathcal F \in K_0(\mathcal X)$ and $\mathcal G \in K_0(\mathcal Y)$ we have
    $$\tau(\mathcal F \boxtimes \mathcal G) = \tau(\mathcal F) \times \tau(\mathcal G) \in \operatorname{CH}_*(I(\mathcal X \times \mathcal Y))_{\mathbb{C}} = \operatorname{CH}_*(I\mathcal X \times I\mathcal Y)_{\mathbb{C}}.$$
    (c) If $f: \mathcal X \to \mathcal Y$ is a proper morphism, we have
    $$If_* \tau(\mathcal F) = \tau(f_* \mathcal F) \in \operatorname{CH}_*(I\mathcal Y)_{\mathbb{C}}$$
    for any $\mathcal F \in K_0(\mathcal X)$.\\
    (d) If $f: \mathcal X \to \mathcal Y$ is a representable morphism and $\mathcal X$ and $\mathcal Y$ are smooth, then
    $$\tau(f^*\mathcal F) = \operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(T_f) \cap If^! \tau(\mathcal F) \in \operatorname{CH}_*(I\mathcal X)_{\mathbb{C}}$$
    for any $\mathcal F \in K_0(\mathcal Y)$. In particular, if $\mathcal X$ is smooth, then
    $$\tau(\mathcal E) = \operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}(\mathcal E) \cap \operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(T_{\mathcal X}) \cap [I\mathcal X] \in \operatorname{CH}_*(I\mathcal X)_{\mathbb{C}}$$
    for any $\mathcal E \in K^0(\mathcal X) = K_0(\mathcal X)$.\\
    (e) Suppose $f: \mathcal X \to \mathcal Y$ is a representable regular embedding fitting into a Cartesian square of equidimensional nice quotients
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        \mathcal X \arrow[r,hook, "f"] \arrow[d,hook, "c"] & \mathcal Y \arrow[d, hook]\\
        \mathcal Z \arrow[r,hook, "e"] & \mathcal W
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    such that all morphisms are representable and $\mathcal Z$ and $\mathcal W$ are smooth with $\dim \mathcal W - \dim \mathcal Z = \dim \mathcal Y - \dim \mathcal X$. Then
    $$\tau(f^* \mathcal F) = \operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(T_f) \cap (Ie)^! \tau(\mathcal F) \in \operatorname{CH}_*(I\mathcal X)_{\mathbb{C}}$$
    for any $\mathcal F \in K_0(\mathcal Y)$.
<!-- end thm-2 -->
<!-- rmk-6: body_md -->
The appearance of $(Ie)^!$ instead of $(If)^!$ in (e) may require some explanation. The issue is that $(If)^!$ is not always well-defined; for example, in Proposition \ref{prop: G and G-1 inverse} we will deal with a representable regular embedding $f: \mathcal X \to \mathcal Y$ such that $If$ is not regular (see Remark \ref{rmk: not reg}). The approach here with $\mathcal Z$ and $\mathcal W$ can be described as introducing a derived structure for which $If$ is quasismooth; then the corresponding Gysin pullback is exactly $(Ie)^!$.
<!-- end rmk-6 -->
<!-- cor-1: body_md -->
\label{cor: agrees with Toen}
    The functor $\tau$ of Definition \ref{defn: stacky tau} agrees with the one constructed in \cite[Th\'eor\`eme 4.10]{Toen} on nice quotients.
<!-- end cor-1 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
First, note that $\operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}$ and $\operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(T_{\mathcal X}) \cap [I \mathcal X]$ agree with $Ch$ and $Td(\mathcal X)$, respectively, as defined in \cite[D\'efinitions 4.5, 4.7]{Toen}. It follows from Theorem \ref{thm: tau properties}(d) and \cite[Th\'eor\`eme 4.10(4)]{Toen} that $\tau$ and To\"en's functor, which we call $\tau_T$, match for any smooth nice quotient $\mathcal X$.

    To show that $\tau$ and $\tau_T$ agree on all nice quotients, we proceed by induction on $\dim \mathcal X$. Note that by canonical (and thus $G$-equivariant) resolution of singularities, we can find a proper birational map $f: \widetilde{\mathcal X} \to \mathcal X$ where $\widetilde{\mathcal X}$ is a smooth nice quotient. Let $i: \mathcal Z \hookrightarrow \mathcal X$ be a closed substack of lower dimension such that $f$ is an isomorphism over the complement $\mathcal U\xhookrightarrow{j} \mathcal Z$. Then, using the localization exact sequence
    $$K_0(\mathcal Z) \xrightarrow{i_*} K_0(\mathcal X) \xrightarrow{j^*} K_0(\mathcal U) \to 0$$
    \cite[Theorem 2.7]{Thomason-foundations} and the fact that $j^* \circ f_* = j_{\widetilde{\mathcal X}}^*$ (using the canonical, thus $G$-equivariant, isomorphism of \cite[Tag 08IB]{stacks-project}), we have a surjection
    $$i_* \oplus f_*: K_0(\mathcal Z) \oplus K_0(\widetilde{\mathcal X}) \twoheadrightarrow K_0(\mathcal X).$$
    Now, $\tau$ and $\tau_T$ agree on $K_0(\mathcal Z)$ by the induction hypothesis, and on $K_0(\widetilde{\mathcal X})$ by the previous paragraph. Then it suffices to note that $\tau$ and $\tau_T$ both commute with proper pushforward (by Theorem \ref{thm: tau properties}(c) and \cite[Th\'eor\`eme 4.10(1)]{Toen}, respectively).
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- cor-2: body_md -->
\label{cor: part e}
    Let $B$ be a smooth variety, $\mathcal X$ a smooth nice quotient flat over $B$, and $\mathcal Y_i$ nice quotients flat over $B$ with representable embeddings into smooth nice quotients $\mathcal Y_i \hookrightarrow \mathcal Z_i$. Consider the morphism
    $$\delta_{\mathcal X}: \mathcal Y_1 \times_B \mathcal X \times_B \mathcal Y_3 \to \mathcal Y_1 \times_B \mathcal X \times \mathcal X \times_B \mathcal Y_2$$
    which is a flat base change of the diagonal $\Delta_{\mathcal X}: \mathcal X \to \mathcal X \times \mathcal X$. Then
    $$\tau(\delta_{\mathcal X}^* \mathcal F) = \operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(T_{\delta_{\mathcal X}}) \cap (I\Delta_{\mathcal X})^! \tau(\mathcal F) = \operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(-p_2^*T_{\mathcal X}) \cap (I\Delta_{\mathcal X})^! \tau(\mathcal F)$$
    for any $\mathcal F \in K_0(\mathcal Y_1 \times_B \mathcal X \times \mathcal X \times_B \mathcal Y_2)$.
<!-- end cor-2 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Choosing a nice presentation $\mathcal X = [X/G]$, recall that $\Delta_{\mathcal X}$ can be represented by $(\sigma, p_2): G \times X \to X \times X$, where $\sigma$ is the action map and $p_2$ the projection. Then consider the factorization
    $$\Delta_{\mathcal X}: \mathcal X \xrightarrow{a} [X \times X/G] \xrightarrow{b} \mathcal X \times \mathcal X$$
    obtained from the $(G \times G)$-equivariant morphisms
    $$G \times X \xrightarrow{(1,\sigma,p_2)} G \times X \times X \xrightarrow{p_{23}} X \times X.$$
    We note that $a$ is a regular embedding, and $b$ is \'etale; letting $\delta_a$ and $\delta_b$ be the corresponding base changes, the same is true of $\delta_a$ (by flatness) and $\delta_b$. Furthermore, note that $\delta_a$ fits into a Cartesian square of representable morphisms
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        \mathcal Y_1 \times_B \mathcal X \times_B \mathcal Y_2 \arrow[r, "\delta_a", hook] \arrow[d, hook] &  \mathcal Y_1 \times_{B,p_1} [X \times X/G] \times_{p_2,B} \mathcal Y_2\arrow[d, hook] \\
        \mathcal Z_1 \times \mathcal X \times \mathcal Z_2 \arrow[r, hook, "e"] & \mathcal Z_1 \times [X \times X/G] \times \mathcal Z_2
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    where the bottom terms are smooth, and both bottom and top arrows are flat base changes of $a$, thus of the same codimension.
    
    Then we have
    $$\tau(\delta_{\mathcal X}^* \mathcal F) = \tau(\delta_a^* \delta_b^* \mathcal F) = \operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(T_{\delta_a}) \cap (Ia)^!\tau(\delta_b^* \mathcal F)$$
    by Theorem \ref{thm: tau properties}(e) applied to the square above (for each component of $\mathcal X$ separately, if there are components of varying dimensions), since $Ie$ is a flat base change of $Ia$
    $$ = \operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(T_{\delta_a}) \cap (Ia)^!(I\delta_b)^*\tau( \mathcal F)$$
    since $\pi \circ \delta_b^* = I\delta_b^* \circ \pi$ because $\delta_b$ is representable; $\iota_*^{-1}$ commutes with $I\delta_b^*$ by Lemma \ref{lem: localization inverse}, using $\mathcal Z_1 \times [X \times X/G] \times \mathcal Z_2$ and $\mathcal Z_1 \times \mathcal X \times \mathcal X \times \mathcal Z_2$ as smooth embeddings; $\rho$ commutes because $\delta_b$ is representable; and $\tau^{EG}$ commutes by \cite[Theorem 3.1(d)(ii)]{EG-RRequivChow} (or alternatively by \cite[Th\'eor\`eme 4.10(2)]{Toen}, since by Corollary \ref{cor: agrees with Toen} the two $\tau$ functors agree)
    $$= \operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(T_{\delta_a}) \cap (Ia)^!(Ib)^!\tau( \mathcal F) = \operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(T_{\delta_a}) \cap (I\Delta_{\mathcal X})^!\tau( \mathcal F) = \operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(T_{\delta_{\mathcal X}}) \cap (I\Delta_{\mathcal X})^!\tau( \mathcal F)$$
    since $(I\delta_b)^* = (Ib)^!$ is flat pullback, and $T_{\delta_a} = T_{\delta_{\mathcal X}}$ since $\delta_b$ is \'etale.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- lem-3: body_md -->
\label{lemma: nonrepresentable presentation}
    If $f: \mathcal X \to \mathcal Y$ is a morphism of nice quotients, then there exist nice quotient representations $\mathcal X = [X/G]$ and $\mathcal Y = [Y/H]$, a group homomorphism $G \to H$, and a $G$-equivariant morphism $X \to Y$ (where $G$ acts on $Y$ through $H$) inducing the morphism $f$.
<!-- end lem-3 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Pick nice quotient representations $\mathcal X = [Z/J]$ and $\mathcal Y = [Y/H]$. Take $X := Z \times_{\mathcal Y} Y$ and $G := J \times H$. Note that $J$ acts on $X$ through the action on $Z$ over $\mathcal X$, and $H$ acts on $X$ through the action on $Y$; these actions commute and thus define an action of $G$ on $X$, compatible with the action of $J$ on $Z$, respectively of $H$ on $Y$, via the projection maps. We claim that the projection $X \to Z$ compatible with the projection of groups $G \to J$ induces an isomorphism of quotient stacks $a: [X/G] \cong [Z/J]$: indeed, it suffices to note that $[X/G] \times_{[Z/J]} Z = [X/H] = Z$, i.e., $a$ pulls back to an isomorphism under the cover $Z \to [Z/J]$ \cite[Tags 04XD, 041Y]{stacks-project}.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- lem-4: body_md -->
\label{lem: representable representation}
    If $f: \mathcal X \to \mathcal Y$ is representable morphism of nice quotients, there is a finite abelian group $G$, quasiprojective varieties $X$ and $Y$ with $\mathcal X = [X/G]$ and $\mathcal Y = [Y/G]$, and a $G$-equivariant morphism $X \to Y$ inducing the map $f$. Conversely, given a morphism of quasiprojective varieties $X \to Y$ equivariant with respect to the action of a finite group $G$, the corresponding morphism of nice varieties $[X/G] \to [Y/G]$ is representable.
<!-- end lem-4 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
Choose a nice quotient presentation $\mathcal Y = [Y/G]$, and take $X := \mathcal X \times_{\mathcal Y} Y$. Then we have a Cartesian diagram
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        X \arrow[d] \arrow[r] & Y \arrow[d] \arrow[r] & \operatorname{Spec} {\mathbb{C}} \arrow[d] \\
        \mathcal X \arrow[r] & \left[Y/G\right] \arrow[r] & BG
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    where $X \to Y$ is the needed $G$-equivariant map and $\mathcal X = [X/G]$. (For quasiprojectivity of $X$, note that $\mathcal X$ has a nice quotient presentation $[X'/G']$, so that $X' \times_{\mathcal X} X$ is a finite cover of the quasiprojective variety $X'$, therefore quasiprojective \cite[Tag 0C4M]{stacks-project}, and since it is a finite cover of $X$, then $X$ too is quasiprojective \cite[Tag 0C4N]{stacks-project}.)

    In the other direction, such a $G$-equivariant morphism induces a Cartesian diagram
        \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        X \arrow[d] \arrow[r] & Y \arrow[d] \arrow[r] & \operatorname{Spec} {\mathbb{C}} \arrow[d] \\
        \left[X/G\right] \arrow[r, "f"] & \left[Y/G\right] \arrow[r] & BG
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    Since $Y \to [Y/G]$ is an \'etale cover and $X$ a scheme, we conclude that the induced map $f$ is representable \cite[Tag 04ZP]{stacks-project}.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
(a) Let $f: \mathcal X \to \mathcal Y$ be a morphism of nice quotients and $\mathcal E \in K^0(I \mathcal Y)$. We note that the canonical isomorphism of $\mathcal E$ induced by the canonical isomorphism on $I\mathcal Y$ pulls back to the canonical isomorphism on $If^*\mathcal E$. Thus $If^* ( \mathcal E^{\operatorname{fix}}) = (If^* \mathcal E)^{\operatorname{fix}}$, and similarly for the dual of the moving part, and $If^*$ commutes with $\rho$ and $\lambda_{-1}$. Then it suffices to note that $If^*$ commutes with the equivariant classes $\operatorname{td}^{EG}$ and ${\mathrm{ch}}^{EG}$ \cite[\S 3.6]{Kresch}. Finally, for $\mathcal F \in K^0(\mathcal Y)$, it suffices to note that $If^*\iota_{\mathcal Y}^* \mathcal F = \iota_{\mathcal X}^* f^* \mathcal F$.\\
    
    (b) We have
    $$If_*(\operatorname{td}^I(If^* \mathcal E) \cap \alpha) = If_*(If^*\operatorname{td}^I(\mathcal E) \cap \alpha) = \operatorname{td}^I(\mathcal E) \cap If_* \alpha,$$
    where the first equality follows from part (a) and the second from the projection formula for $If$, which is again a proper morphism of nice quotients.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
Let $\mathcal X = [X/G]$ be a nice presentation. We trace through the steps in the definition of $\tau$. First, we have
    $$\pi(\mathcal E \cdot \mathcal F) = \mathcal E \cdot \pi(\mathcal F)$$
    since the actions of $K^0(BG) \to K^0(\mathcal X)$ on $K_0(\mathcal X)$ commute, and thus the product with $\mathcal E$ is an isomorphism of $K^0(BG)$-modules. Then by the projection formula
    $$\iota_*^{-1} \circ \pi(\mathcal E \cdot \mathcal F) = \iota_*^{-1}(\mathcal E \cdot \pi(\mathcal F)) = \iota^* \mathcal E \cdot \iota_*^{-1}(\pi(\mathcal F)).$$
    Next, we note that
    $$\rho(\iota^* \mathcal E \cdot \iota_*^{-1}(\pi(\mathcal F))) = \rho(\iota^* \mathcal E) \cdot \rho(\iota_*^{-1}(\pi(\mathcal F))) $$
    and so
    $$\tau(\mathcal E \cdot \mathcal F) = \tau^{EG} \circ \rho \circ \iota_*^{-1} \circ \pi(\mathcal E \cdot \mathcal F) = \tau^{EG}(\rho(\iota^* \mathcal E) \cdot \rho(\iota_*^{-1}(\pi(\mathcal F))))$$
    $$={\mathrm{ch}}^{EG}(\rho(\iota^* \mathcal E)) \cap \tau^{EG}(\rho(\iota_*^{-1}(\pi(\mathcal F))))) = \operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}(\mathcal E) \cap \tau(\mathcal F)$$
    by \cite[Theorem 3.1(c)]{EG-RRequivChow}.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
Let $\mathcal X = [X/G]$ and $\mathcal Y = [Y/H]$ be nice presentations, so that we have a nice presentation $\mathcal X \times \mathcal Y \cong [X \times Y/G \times H]$. We start by claiming that
    $$\pi_{(g,h)}(\mathcal F \boxtimes \mathcal G) = \pi_g(\mathcal F) \boxtimes \pi_h(\mathcal G)$$
    Indeed, since $\mathfrak m_g \subset K^0(BG)_{\mathbb{C}}$ annihilates $\pi_g(\mathcal F)$ and similarly for $\mathcal G$, we certainly have
    $$\pi_g(\mathcal F) \boxtimes \pi_h(\mathcal G) \subset K_0(\mathcal X \times \mathcal Y)_{\mathfrak m_{(g,h)}, {\mathbb{C}}} \subset K_0(\mathcal X \times \mathcal Y)_{\mathbb{C}}$$
    and on the other hand
    $$\sum_{g \in G, h \in H} \pi_g(\mathcal F) \boxtimes \pi_h(\mathcal G) = \mathcal F \boxtimes \mathcal G.$$
    Next,
    $$\iota_{(g,h) *} (\iota_{g*}^{-1}(\pi_g(\mathcal F) \boxtimes \iota_{h*}^{-1}(\pi_h(\mathcal G)))) = (\iota_g \times \iota_h)_*(\iota_{g*}^{-1}(\pi_g(\mathcal F) \boxtimes \iota_{h*}^{-1}(\pi_h(\mathcal G)))) = \pi_g(\mathcal F) \boxtimes \pi_h(\mathcal G)$$
    by Lemma \ref{lemma: pushforward exterior product}, i.e., writing $\iota_*^{-1} \circ \pi(\mathcal F) =: (\mathcal F_g)_{g \in G}$ and similarly for $\mathcal G$, we have
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: boxtimes loc}
        \iota_*^{-1} \circ \pi (\mathcal F \boxtimes \mathcal G) = (\mathcal F_g \boxtimes \mathcal G_h)_{(g,h) \in G \times H}.
    \end{equation}

    Now, we have
    $$\rho_{(g,h)}(\mathcal F_g \boxtimes \mathcal G_h) = \rho_g(\mathcal F_g) \boxtimes \rho_h(\mathcal G_h)$$
    and so
    $$\tau^{EG}(\rho_g(\mathcal F_g) \boxtimes \rho_h(\mathcal G_h)) = \tau^{EG}(\rho_g(\mathcal F_g)) \times \tau^{EG}(\rho_h(\mathcal G_h)),$$
    which follows from the corresponding fact for $\tau^F$ \cite[Example 18.3.1]{Fulton} when one uses representations $V_G, V_H, V_G \oplus V_H$ to compute the functors $\tau^{EG}$ for the groups $G,H, G \times H$ (respectively).
    By definition, this means
    $$\tau(\mathcal F \boxtimes \mathcal G) = \tau(\mathcal F) \times \tau(\mathcal G).$$
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
First, by Lemma \ref{lemma: nonrepresentable presentation}, there are nice presentations $\mathcal X = [X/G]$ and $\mathcal Y = [Y/H]$ such that $f$ is induced by a morphism $\tilde f:X \to Y$ equivariant with respect to a homomorphism $\phi: G \to H$. Note that the morphism $If: I\mathcal X \to I \mathcal Y$ breaks into morphisms
    $If_g: \mathcal X^g \to \mathcal Y^{\phi(g)}$ induced by $\tilde f|_{X^g}: X^g \to Y^{\phi(g)}$. 

    Writing $\iota_*^{-1} \circ \pi(\mathcal F) = (\mathcal F_g)_{g \in G}$, we claim that
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: pushforward loc}
        \iota_*^{-1} \circ \pi(f_* \mathcal F)_h = \sum_{g \in \phi^{-1}(h)} If_* \mathcal F_g \in K_0(\mathcal Y^h)_{\mathfrak m_h,{\mathbb{C}}}.
    \end{equation}
    Since
    $$\sum_{h \in H}\iota_{\mathcal Y, h*} \sum_{g \in \phi^{-1}(h)} If_{g*} \mathcal F_g = \iota_{\mathcal Y*} If_{*} \left(\sum_{g \in G} \mathcal F_g\right) = f_* \iota_{\mathcal X*}\left(\sum_{g \in G} \mathcal F_g\right) = f_* \mathcal F,$$
    it suffices to verify that $If_{g*} \mathcal F_g \in K_0(\mathcal Y^h)_{\mathfrak m_h, {\mathbb{C}}}$ for $h = \phi(g)$, or in other words that for any $r \in \mathfrak m_h \subset K^0(BH)$ we have $r \cdot If_{g*} \mathcal F_g = 0$. This follows since, with notation as in the following commutative (but not necessarily Cartesian) square
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
    \mathcal X^g \arrow[r, "If_g"] \arrow[d, "p"] & \mathcal Y^h \arrow[d, "q"] \\
    BG \arrow[r, "\phi"] & BH
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    the projection formula \cite[Proposition 3.7]{Khan} implies that
    $$q^*r \cdot If_{g*} \mathcal F_g = If_{g*}(If^*_g q^*r \cdot \mathcal F_g) = If_{g*}(p^* \phi^*r \cdot \mathcal F_g) = 0,$$
    since $\phi^* r \in \mathfrak m_g$ and thus by assumption that $\mathcal F_g \in K_0(\mathcal X^g)_{\mathfrak m_g, {\mathbb{C}}}$ we have $p^* \phi^* r \cdot \mathcal F_g = 0$.

    Next, we note that $If_* \circ \rho_X = \rho_Y \circ If_*$ since the canonical automorphism on $If_* \mathcal G$ for any $\mathcal G \in K_0(I \mathcal X)$ is given by the composition of $If_*$ with the canonical automorphism on $\mathcal G$, and so in particular the eigensheaf decomposition is preserved by $If_*$.
    
    Finally, to show that $If_* \circ \tau^{EG} = \tau^{EG} \circ If_*$ we use compatibility of $\tau^{EG}$ with representable proper pushforward \cite[Theorem 3.1(b)]{EG-RRequivChow}: Since $p: \coprod_{g \in G} X^g \to I\mathcal X$ is proper and representable, we have a diagram
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        K_0(\coprod_{g \in G} X^g)_{\mathfrak m_1, {\mathbb{Q}}} \arrow{r}{\sim}[swap]{\tau^{EG}} \arrow[d, "p_*"] & \operatorname{CH}_*(\coprod_{g \in G} X^g)_{\mathbb{Q}} \arrow[d, two heads, "p_*"] \\
        K_0(I \mathcal X)_{\mathfrak m_1, {\mathbb{Q}}} \arrow{r}{\sim}[swap]{\tau^{EG}} & \operatorname{CH}_*(I \mathcal X)_{\mathbb{Q}}
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    (where the horizontal arrows are isomorphisms by \cite[Corollary 5.1]{EG-RRequivChow}, and the right vertical arrow is a surjection by \cite[Example 1.7.6]{Fulton}). Thus, for any $\mathcal G \in K_0(I\mathcal X)_{\mathfrak m_1, {\mathbb{Q}}}$ we can find $\mathcal H \in K_0(\coprod_{g \in G} X^g)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ with $p_* \mathcal H = \mathcal G$. To show that $\tau^{EG}(If_* \mathcal G) = If_* \tau^{EG}(\mathcal G)$ it suffices to see that $\tau^{EG}((If \circ p)_* \mathcal H) = (If \circ p)_* \tau^{EG}(\mathcal H)$, but now note that $If \circ p: \coprod_{g \in G} X^g \to I \mathcal Y$ is again representable and proper, as we can factor $\coprod_{g \in G} X^g \to \coprod_{h \in H} Y^h \to I\mathcal Y$.
    
    Thus we conclude that
    $$\tau(f_* \mathcal F) = \tau^{EG} \circ \rho \circ \iota_*^{-1} \circ \pi(f_* \mathcal F) = \tau^{EG} \circ \rho\left(\sum_{g \in \phi^{-1}(h)} If_{g*} \mathcal F_g\right)_{h \in H} $$
    $$= \tau^{EG} \left( \sum_{g \in \phi^{-1}(h)} If_{g*} \rho_g(\mathcal F_g) \right)_{h \in H} = \left( \sum_{g \in \phi^{-1}(h)}If_{g*} \tau^{EG}(\rho_g(\mathcal F_g)) \right)_{h \in H} = If_* \tau(\mathcal F).$$
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
First, since $f$ is representable, by Lemma \ref{lem: representable representation} we may choose nice presentations $\mathcal X = [X/G]$ and $\mathcal Y = [Y/G]$ such that $f$ is induced by a $G$-equivariant morphism $\tilde f: X \to Y$. Since $\mathcal X$ and $\mathcal Y$ are smooth, the same is true of $X$ and $Y$, as well as the fixed loci $X^g, Y^g$ \cite[Proposition 3.1]{Thomason}.

    By Lemma \ref{lem: smooth localization} we have
    $$\tau(f^*\mathcal F) = \operatorname{td}^I(\mathcal N_{\iota_{\mathcal X}}) \cap \tau^{EG}(\rho(\iota_{\mathcal X}^* f^* \mathcal F)),$$
    where we note that
    $$\tau^{EG}(\rho(\iota_{\mathcal X}^* f^* \mathcal F)) = \tau^{EG}(\rho(If^* \iota_{\mathcal Y}^* \mathcal F)) = \tau^{EG}(If^*(\rho(\iota_{\mathcal Y}^* \mathcal F)))$$
    $$= \operatorname{td}^{EG}(T_{If}) \cap If^!\tau^{EG}(\rho(\iota_{\mathcal Y}^* \mathcal F)))$$
    by the proof of \cite[Theorem 3.1(d)(ii)]{EG-RRequivChow}, 
    since $If: I \mathcal X \to I\mathcal Y$ is induced by the $G$-equivariant morphism of smooth quasiprojective varieties $\coprod_{g \in G} \tilde f|_{X^g}
    : \coprod X^g \to \coprod Y^g$ (a morphism of smooth varieties being l.c.i.), and we replace the hypothesis on $G$ with the quasiprojectivity of $X^g$ and $Y^g$, so that one may now apply \cite[Proposition 23(1)]{EG-equivint}).

    We conclude that
    $$\tau(f^* \mathcal F) = \operatorname{td}^I(\mathcal N_{\iota_{\mathcal X}}) \cap \operatorname{td}^{EG}(T_{If}) \cap If^!\tau^{EG}(\rho(\iota_{\mathcal Y}^* \mathcal F))$$
    $$= \operatorname{td}^I(\mathcal N_{\iota_{\mathcal X}}) \cap \operatorname{td}^{EG}(T_{If}) \cap If^!(\operatorname{td}^I(\mathcal N_{\iota_{\mathcal Y}})^{-1} \cap \operatorname{td}^I(\mathcal N_{\iota_{\mathcal Y}}) \cap
    \tau^{EG}(\rho(\iota_{\mathcal Y}^* \mathcal F))) $$
    $$= \operatorname{td}^I(\mathcal N_{\iota_{\mathcal X}}) \cap \operatorname{td}^{EG}(T_{If}) \cap \operatorname{td}^I(If^* \mathcal N_{\iota_{\mathcal Y}})^{-1} \cap If^!(\operatorname{td}^I(\mathcal N_{\iota_{\mathcal Y}}) \cap
    \tau^{EG}(\rho(\iota_{\mathcal Y}^* \mathcal F)) )$$
    $$= \operatorname{td}^I(\mathcal N_{\iota_{\mathcal X}} - If^* \mathcal N_{\iota_Y}) \cap \operatorname{td}^{EG}(T_{If}) \cap If^!(\tau(\mathcal F)) $$
    again by Lemma \ref{lem: smooth localization}. Now, note that $\iota_{\mathcal X}^* T_f$ satisfies
    $$(\iota_{\mathcal X}^* T_f)^{\operatorname{mov}} = (\iota_{\mathcal X}^* T_{\mathcal X} - \iota_{\mathcal X}^* f^* T_{\mathcal Y})^{\operatorname{mov}} = \mathcal N_{\iota_{\mathcal X}} - If^* \mathcal N_{\iota_{\mathcal Y}}$$
    $$ (\iota_{\mathcal X}^* T_f)^{\operatorname{fix}} = (\iota_{\mathcal X}^* T_{\mathcal X} - \iota_{\mathcal X}^* f^* T_{\mathcal Y})^{\operatorname{fix}} = T_{I\mathcal X} - If^* T_{I \mathcal Y} = T_{If},$$
    so that we may rewrite the above as
    $$\tau(f^* \mathcal F) = \operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(T_f) \cap If^!(\tau(\mathcal F)).$$

    Finally, for the last part, if $\mathcal X = [X/G]$ is a nice quotient presentation, consider the morphism $\pi: \mathcal X \to BG$. Note that $T_\pi = T_{\mathcal X}$ since $T_{BG}$ is of rank 0. Note also that
    $$\tau(\mathscr O_{BG}) = ([BG])_{g \in G} \in \operatorname{CH}_*(IBG) = \oplus_{g \in G} \operatorname{CH}_*(BG)$$
    since $\operatorname{CH}_*(BG) = \operatorname{CH}_0(BG)$, and on an approximation $U/G \to BG$ we have $\tau(\mathscr O_{U/G}) = [U/G] + \ldots$ \cite[Theorem 18.3(5)]{Fulton}. Then for any $\mathcal E \in K^0(\mathcal X)$ we have
    $$\tau(\mathcal E) \overset{(a)}{=} \operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}(\mathcal E) \cap \tau(\mathscr O_{\mathcal X}) = \operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}(\mathcal E) \cap \tau(\pi^* \mathscr O_{BG}) = \operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}(\mathcal E) \cap \operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(T_{\mathcal X}) \cap [I \mathcal X].$$
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- lem-5: body_md -->
\label{lem: smooth localization}
    If $\mathcal X$ is a smooth nice quotient, then
    $$\tau(\mathcal F) = \operatorname{td}^I(\mathcal N_\iota) \cap \tau^{EG}(\rho(\iota^* \mathcal F)) \in \operatorname{CH}_*(I\mathcal X)_{\mathbb{C}}$$
    for any $\mathcal F \in K_0(\mathcal X)_{\mathbb{C}}$, where $\mathcal N_\iota$ is the normal bundle of the local embedding $\iota: I\mathcal X \to \mathcal X$.
<!-- end lem-5 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Recall from Lemma \ref{lem: localization inverse} that for each $g \in G$ we have
    $$(\lambda_{-1} \mathcal N_{\iota_g}^\vee)^{-1} \cdot \iota_g^* = \iota_{g*}^{-1}: K_0(\mathcal X)_{\mathfrak m_g, {\mathbb{C}}} \to K_0(\mathcal X^g)_{\mathfrak m_g, {\mathbb{C}}}$$
    where the inverse $(\lambda_{-1} \mathcal N_{\iota_g}^\vee)^{-1}$ is taken in the quotient ring $K^0(\mathcal X^g)_{\mathfrak m_g, {\mathbb{C}}}$.
    Note that although this is not an inverse in $K^0(\mathcal X^g)_{\mathbb{C}}$, it nevertheless satisfies the property that
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: lambda-1 inverse}
    {\mathrm{ch}}^{EG}(\rho((\lambda_{-1} \mathcal N_{\iota_g}^\vee)^{-1})) \cap {\mathrm{ch}}^{EG}(\rho(\lambda_{-1} \mathcal N_{\iota_g}^\vee)) = {\mathrm{ch}}^{EG}(\rho(\pi_g(\mathscr O_{\mathcal X^g}))) =  1 \in \operatorname{CH}^*(\mathcal X^g)_{\mathbb{C}},
    \end{equation}
    where $\pi_g$ is the projection onto the $\mathfrak m_g$ component as in (\ref{eq: pi}), and we note that
    $${\mathrm{ch}}^{EG}(\rho(\pi_g(\mathscr O_{\mathcal X^g}))) = {\mathrm{ch}}^{EG}(\rho(\mathscr O_{\mathcal X^g})) = {\mathrm{ch}}^{EG}(\mathscr O_{\mathcal X^g}) = 1$$
    since $\rho$ permutes components as described in equation (\ref{eq: rho components}) and ${\mathrm{ch}}^{EG}: K^0(\mathcal X^g)_{\mathbb{C}} \to \operatorname{CH}^*(\mathcal X^g)_{{\mathbb{C}}}$ factors through $K^0(\mathcal X^g)_{\mathfrak m_1, {\mathbb{C}}}$ (Proposition \ref{prop: EG factors through m1}).

    Then we have
    $$\tau(\mathcal F) = \tau^{EG} \circ \rho(\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_\iota)^{-1} \cdot \iota_g^* \pi(\mathcal F))$$
    $$ = \tau^{EG}(\rho(\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N_\iota^\vee)^{-1}) \cdot \rho(\iota^* \pi( \mathcal F))) = {\mathrm{ch}}^{EG}(\rho(\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_\iota)^{-1})) \cap \tau^{EG}(\rho(\iota^* \pi(\mathcal F)))$$
    by \cite[Theorem 3.1(c)]{EG-RRequivChow}
    $$= \operatorname{td}^I(\mathcal N_\iota) \cap \tau^{EG}(\rho(\iota^* \pi(\mathcal F)))$$
    by definition and (\ref{eq: lambda-1 inverse})
    $$ = \operatorname{td}^I(\mathcal N_\iota) \cap \tau(\iota^* \mathcal F)$$
    since $\tau^{EG} \circ \rho$ factors through the projections $\pi_g: K_0(I\mathcal X^g)_{\mathbb{C}} \to K_0(I\mathcal X^g)_{\mathfrak m_g, {\mathbb{C}}}$ by (\ref{eq: rho components}) and Proposition \ref{prop: EG factors through m1}, and $\pi_g(\iota_g^* \mathcal F) = \iota_g^* \pi_g(\mathcal F)$.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
\textbf{Case 1:} Suppose all morphisms in the square are closed embeddings.
    By Lemma \ref{lem: pullback first step}, for any $\mathcal F \in K_0(\mathcal Y)_{\mathbb{C}}$ we have
    $$\iota_{\mathcal X *}^{-1} \circ \pi(f^* \mathcal F) =\lambda_{-1}((Ic)^*(\iota_{\mathcal Z}^*\mathcal N^\vee_e)^{\operatorname{mov}}) \cdot (Ie)^!(\iota_{\mathcal Y*}^{-1} \circ \pi(\mathcal F)).$$
    Note that $\rho$ commutes with $(Ie)^!$ since $(Ie)^!(\mathcal F) = \sum (-1)^i\operatorname{Tor}_i^{I\mathcal W}(\mathscr O_{I \mathcal Z}, \mathcal F)$ and each $\mathscr O_{\mathcal Z^g}$ is $g$-fixed, so we have
    $$\rho \circ \iota_{\mathcal X *}^{-1} \circ \pi(f^* \mathcal F) = \rho(\lambda_{-1}((Ic)^*(\iota_{\mathcal Z}^*\mathcal N^\vee_e)^{\operatorname{mov}})) \cdot (Ie)^!(\rho \circ \iota_{\mathcal Y*}^{-1} \circ \pi(\mathcal F)).$$
    Thus
    $$\tau(f^* \mathcal F) = \tau^{EG}(\rho(\lambda_{-1}((Ic)^*(\iota_{\mathcal Z}^*\mathcal N^\vee_e)^{\operatorname{mov}})) \cdot (Ie)^!(\rho \circ \iota_{\mathcal Y*}^{-1} \circ \pi(\mathcal F)))$$
    $$ = {\mathrm{ch}}^{EG}(\rho(\lambda_{-1}((Ic)^*(\iota_{\mathcal Z}^*\mathcal N^\vee_e)^{\operatorname{mov}}))) \cap \tau^{EG}((Ie)^!(\rho \circ \iota_{\mathcal Y*}^{-1} \circ \pi(\mathcal F)))$$
    by \cite[Theorem 3.1(c)]{EG-RRequivChow}
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: tau pullback case 1}
     = {\mathrm{ch}}^{EG}(\rho(\lambda_{-1}((Ic)^*(\iota_{\mathcal Z}^*\mathcal N^\vee_e)^{\operatorname{mov}}))) \cap \operatorname{td}^{EG}((Ic)^* T_{Ie}) \cap (Ie)^! \tau^{EG}(\rho \circ \iota_{\mathcal Y*}^{-1} \circ \pi(\mathcal F))   
    \end{equation} 
    by Lemma \ref{lem: tauEG and Gysin}.
    Note that we have a surjection of vector bundles $c^* \mathcal N_e^\vee \twoheadrightarrow \mathcal N_f^\vee$ \cite[Tag 0473]{stacks-project}, where by assumption these are of the same rank; thus this map is an isomorphism, and
    $$\iota_{\mathcal X}^* T_f = - \iota_{\mathcal X}^* \mathcal N_f = -\iota_{\mathcal X}^*(c^* \mathcal N_e) = - (Ic)^*(\iota_{\mathcal Z}^* \mathcal N_e)$$
    has fixed part
    $$(\iota_{\mathcal X}^* T_f)^{\operatorname{fix}} = -(Ic)^*(\iota_{\mathcal Z}^* \mathcal N_e)^{\operatorname{fix}} = (Ic)^* T_{Ie}$$
    and moving part
    $$(\iota_{\mathcal X}^* T_f)^{\operatorname{mov}} = -(Ic)^*(\iota_{\mathcal Z}^* \mathcal N_e)^{\operatorname{mov}}.$$
    Furthermore, since ${\mathrm{ch}}^{EG} \circ \rho \circ \lambda_{-1}$ is a group homomorphism, as described in Proposition \ref{prop: moving part of ttd},
    we have
    $${\mathrm{ch}}^{EG} \circ \rho \circ \lambda_{-1}(-(\iota_{\mathcal X}^* T^\vee_f)^{\operatorname{mov}}) = {\mathrm{ch}}^{EG} \circ \rho \circ \lambda_{-1}((\iota_{\mathcal X}^* T^\vee_f)^{\operatorname{mov}})^{-1}.$$
    Thus (\ref{eq: tau pullback case 1}) gives
    $$\tau(f^* \mathcal F) = \operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(T_f) \cap (Ie)^! \tau(\mathcal F).$$
    \\
    \textbf{Case 2:} Suppose $e: \mathcal Z \hookrightarrow \mathcal W$ (and thus also $f: \mathcal X \to \mathcal Y$) is an open embedding. As in Lemma \ref{lem: representable representation}, by choosing a nice quotient presentation of $\mathcal W$ we can find a finite abelian group $G$ acting on quasiprojective varieties $X,Y,Z,W$ such that the morphisms of stacks are induced by $G$-equivariant morphisms of varieties.
    
    First, we claim that
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: tau pullback step 2}
     \iota_{\mathcal X *}^{-1}(\pi(f^*\mathcal F)) = \iota_{\mathcal X *}^{-1}(f^*(\pi \mathcal F)) = (If)^* \iota_{\mathcal Y*}^{-1}(\pi \mathcal F).   
    \end{equation}
    Indeed, the first equality follows from the fact that $f^*$ is compatible with the $K^0(BG)_{\mathbb{C}}$-module structure and the second from the fact that
    $$f^*\iota_{\mathcal Y *} = \iota_{\mathcal X *}(If)^*,$$
    by the corresponding (canonical, thus $G$-equivariant) isomorphism of complexes of sheaves \cite[Tag 08IB]{stacks-project}, since $f$ is flat and $I \mathcal X = \mathcal X \times_{\mathcal Y} I\mathcal Y$ by \cite[Tag 06R5]{stacks-project}, as $\mathcal X \to \mathcal Y$ is an open embedding, therefore a monomorphism.

    We conclude that
    $$\tau(f^* \mathcal F) = \tau^{EG} \circ \rho(\iota_{\mathcal X *}^{-1}(\pi(f^*\mathcal F))) = \tau^{EG} \circ \rho((If)^* \iota_{\mathcal Y*}^{-1}(\pi \mathcal F))$$
    by (\ref{eq: tau pullback step 2})
    $$=\tau^{EG}((If)^* \rho(\iota_{\mathcal Y*}^{-1}(\pi \mathcal F))) $$
    since $(If)^*$ respects the $G$-equivariant structure and thus commutes with $\rho$
    $$ = (If)^*\tau^{EG}(\rho(\iota_{\mathcal Y*}^{-1}(\pi \mathcal F))) = (If)^* \tau(\mathcal F).$$
    by \cite[Theorem 3.1(d)(i)]{EG-RRequivChow}, since as described above $If$ is the base change of $f$, and thus an open embedding. Note that in this case $T_f$ is trivial. Furthermore, for the same reasons $Ie$ is an open embedding, and $(Ie)^! = (If)^*: \operatorname{CH}_*(I \mathcal Y) \to \operatorname{CH}_*(I \mathcal X)$ is simply the restriction.
    \\
    \textbf{The general case:} Suppose we are given a Cartesian square as described in the statement of the theorem. Again, choose a presentation by a finite abelian group $G$ and quasiprojective varieties $X,Y,Z,W$. By replacing $W$ and $Z$ by the $G$-stable open subsets $W' := W\setminus (\overline{Y} \setminus Y)$ and $Z' := Z \cap W'$ if necessary, we may assume that the vertical morphisms are closed embeddings. Now factoring $e: Z \hookrightarrow W$ as $Z \hookrightarrow W \setminus (\overline{Z} \setminus Z) \hookrightarrow W$ and considering the corresponding factorization of $f: X \hookrightarrow Y$, we reduce to the previous two cases.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- lem-6: body_md -->
\label{lem: tauEG and Gysin}
    Suppose there is a $G$-equivariant Cartesian square of varieties
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        A \arrow[d, "a"] \arrow[r] & B \arrow[d, "b"] \\
        C \arrow[r, "c"]  & D 
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    such that all the morphisms are closed embeddings and $C$ and $D$ are smooth. Then
    $$\tau^{EG}(c^! \mathcal F) = \operatorname{td}^{EG}(-a^*\mathcal N_{\mathcal C/\mathcal D}) \cap c^! \tau^{EG}(\mathcal F)$$
    for all $\mathcal F \in K_0(\mathcal B)$.
<!-- end lem-6 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
We start by proving the corresponding statement for the Fulton tau functor $\tau^F$. Recalling the definition of $\tau^F$ in terms of the localized Chern character and a smooth embedding \cite[p.~349]{Fulton}, we have
    $$\tau^F(c^! \mathcal F) = \operatorname{td}(a^*T_C) \cap {\mathrm{ch}}^C_A(c^! \mathcal F) \cap [C]$$
    where
    $${\mathrm{ch}}^C_A(c^! \mathcal F) \cap [C] = {\mathrm{ch}}^C_A(c^! \mathcal F) \cap c^*[D] = c^!({\mathrm{ch}}^D_B(\mathcal F) \cap [D])$$
    by \cite[p.~343, (19)]{Fulton}. Thus
    $$\tau^F(c^! \mathcal F) = \operatorname{td}(a^*T_C) \cap c^!({\mathrm{ch}}^D_B(\mathcal F) \cap [D])$$
    $$= \operatorname{td}(a^*T_C -a^*c^* T_D) \cap \tau^F(\mathcal F) = \operatorname{td}(-a^*\mathcal N_{C/D}) \cap \tau^F(\mathcal F).$$
    
    Now, let $p_A: A_G \to \mathcal A$, etc. be schematic approximations given by a fixed choice of $U$. Then
    $$p_A^* \circ \tau^{EF} \circ c^! := \tau^F \circ p_A^* \circ c^! = \tau^F \circ c^! \circ p_A^*$$
    by \cite[Lemma 3.2]{Anderson-Payne}, where here we use $c^!: K_0(B_G) \to K_0(A_G)$ to mean the Gysin pullback induced by $\mathcal C \to \mathcal D$, which is the same as that induced by $C_G \to D_G$ by Lemma \ref{lem: excess intersection}(a). Then it suffices to note that from the previous paragraph we have
    $$\tau^F \circ c^! \circ p_A^* = \operatorname{td}(-a_G^* \mathcal N_{C_G/D_G}) \cap c^! \circ \tau^F \circ p_A^* =: p_A^*(\operatorname{td}^{EG}(-a^* \mathcal N_{\mathcal C/\mathcal D}) \cap c^! \tau^{EG}(\mathcal F))$$
    since $p_C^* \mathcal N_{\mathcal C/\mathcal D} = \mathcal N_{C_G/D_G}$.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- lem-7: body_md -->
\label{lem: pullback first step}
    In the situation of Theorem \ref{thm: tau properties}(e), if all morphisms in the Cartesian square are closed embeddings, then we have
    $$\iota_{\mathcal X *}^{-1} \circ \pi(f^* \mathcal F) = f^!(\iota_{\mathcal Y *}^{-1} \circ \pi(\mathcal F)) = \lambda_{-1}((Ic)^*(\iota_{\mathcal Z}^*\mathcal N^\vee_{Z/W})^{\operatorname{mov}}) \cdot (Ie)^!(\iota_{\mathcal Y*}^{-1} \circ \pi(\mathcal F))$$
    for all $\mathcal F \in K_0(\mathcal Y)_{\mathbb{C}}$.
<!-- end lem-7 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
As in Lemma \ref{lem: representable representation}, choosing a nice presentation $\mathcal W = [W/G]$, we may suppose the given Cartesian square is induced by a $G$-equivariant Cartesian square
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        X \arrow[r,hook, "f"] \arrow[d, hook, "c"] & Y \arrow[d, hook, "d"] \\
        Z \arrow[r, hook, "e"] & W
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    with $Z$ and $W$ smooth, all morphisms closed embeddings, and $f$ a regular embedding.
    Now, from Lemma \ref{lem: localization inverse} applied to $X \hookrightarrow W$, we have
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: pullback 1}
        \iota_{\mathcal X*}^{-1}\circ \pi(f^* \mathcal F) = Ic^*e_g^*(\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N_{\iota_{\mathcal W}}^\vee)^{-1}) \cdot \iota_W^!\circ \pi(f^* \mathcal F).
    \end{equation}
    where
    $$\iota_W^! \circ \pi(f^* \mathcal F) = \iota_W^!(f^* \circ \pi(\mathcal F)) = \iota_W^!(f^! \circ \pi( \mathcal F)) = f^!(\iota_W^! \circ \pi( \mathcal F))$$
    with the first equality since $f^*$ is a morphism of $K^0(BG)_{\mathbb{C}}$-modules, the second by definition of Gysin pullback, and the third by \cite[Lemma 3.2]{Anderson-Payne}. Then from (\ref{eq: pullback 1}) we obtain
    \begin{equation*}
        \iota_{X*}^{-1}\circ \pi(f^* \mathcal F) = Ic^*Ie^*(\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N_{\iota_{\mathcal W}}^\vee)^{-1}) \cdot f^!(\iota_{\mathcal W}^! \circ \pi(\mathcal F))
    \end{equation*}
    $$ = If^*Id^*(\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N_{\iota_{\mathcal W}}^\vee)^{-1}) \cdot f^!(\iota_{\mathcal W}^! \circ \pi(\mathcal F)) = f^!(Id^*(\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N_{\iota_{\mathcal W}}^\vee)^{-1}) \cdot \iota_{\mathcal W}^!(\pi(\mathcal F)))$$
    by Lemma \ref{lem: Gysin pullback K0}(b)
    $$= f^!(\iota_{\mathcal Y*}^{-1} \circ \pi(\mathcal F))$$
    by Lemma \ref{lem: localization inverse} applied to $d: Y \hookrightarrow W$.

    To prove the second equality in the statement of the lemma, we start by noting that $e$ is regular embedding since $Z,W$ are smooth \cite[Tag 0E9J]{stacks-project}, and $f$ is a regular embedding by assumption, so by Lemma \ref{lem: Tor indep}(b) we have that $Y$ and $Z$ are $\operatorname{Tor}$-independent over $W$.
    Thus by Lemma \ref{lem: excess intersection}(a) we have
    $$f^! = e^! : K_0(\mathcal Y^g)_{\mathfrak m_g, {\mathbb{C}}} \to K_0(\mathcal X^g)_{\mathfrak m_g, {\mathbb{C}}}$$
    and by Lemma \ref{lem: excess intersection}(b) we have
    $$e^! = (Ic)^* \lambda_{-1}((\iota_{\mathcal Z}^*\mathcal N_{\mathcal Z/\mathcal W}^\vee)^{\operatorname{mov}}) \cdot  (Ie)^!.$$
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- lem-8: body_md -->
\label{lem: excess intersection}
    Consider a Cartesian diagram of $G$-equivariant varieties
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        A \arrow[r, "a"] \arrow[d, "c"] & B \arrow[r, "b"] \arrow[d,hook, "e"] & C \arrow[d,hook, "f"] \\
        D \arrow[r, "h"] & E \arrow[r, "i"] & H
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    such that $e$ and $f$ are regular embeddings.\\
    (a) If $f$ and $i$ are $\operatorname{Tor}$-independent, then $e^! = f^!: K_0(\mathcal D) \to K_0(\mathcal A)$.\\
    (b) If $h$ and $f$ are closed embeddings, $C$ and $H$ are smooth, $G$ is finite abelian, and $E = H^g$ for some $g \in G$, then
    $$f^! = a^* \lambda_{-1}((b^*\mathcal N_{\mathcal C/\mathcal H}^\vee)^{\operatorname{mov}}) \cdot e^!: K_0(\mathcal D)_{{\mathbb{C}}} \to K_0(\mathcal A)_{\mathfrak m_g, {\mathbb{C}}}.$$
<!-- end lem-8 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
(a) It suffices to show that given ring maps $R \to R' \to R''$ and $R \to S$, where $\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(R', S) = 0$ for $i > 0$, and given $M \in \operatorname{Mod}(R'')$, the natural (thus $G$-equivariant) map $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(M, S) \to \operatorname{Tor}_i^{R'}(M, R' \otimes_R S)$ is an isomorphism. Picking a resolution $S^\bullet$ of $S$ by free $R$-modules, note that $R' \otimes_R S^\bullet$ is a resolution of $R' \otimes_R S$ by free $R'$-modules, as the homology groups of this complex calculate $\operatorname{Tor}^R_*(R', S)$. We obtain an isomorphism of the complexes $M \otimes_R S^\bullet = M \otimes_{R'} (R' \otimes_R S^\bullet)$ computing $\operatorname{Tor}$ groups on each side. \\
    (b) We start by noting that the Gysin morphism
    $$f^{(-)}(-): K_0(\mathcal C) \times K_0(\mathcal D) \to K_0(\mathcal A)$$
    (where here all elements of $K_0(\mathcal C)$ are $f$-perfect by smoothness of $H$) is a bilinear morphism of $K^0(BG)$-modules (Lemma \ref{lem: Gysin pullback K0}), and so defines a morphism
    $$f^{(-)}(-): K_0(\mathcal C)_{\mathfrak m_g, {\mathbb{C}}} \times K_0(\mathcal D)_{\mathfrak m_g, {\mathbb{C}}} \to K_0(\mathcal A)_{\mathfrak m_g, {\mathbb{C}}}.$$
    Recall that $f^!(-) := f^{[\mathscr O_{\mathcal C}]}(-)$, where
    $$[\mathscr O_{\mathcal C}] = b_*(\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_{\mathcal C^g/\mathcal C})^{-1}) \in K_0(\mathcal C)_{\mathfrak m_g, {\mathbb{C}}}$$
    by \cite[Lemme 3.3]{Thomason}, since $C$ is assumed smooth and $B = C^g$. Then by definition of Gysin pullback
    $$f^{b_*(\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_{\mathcal C^g/\mathcal C})^{-1})} = (f \circ b)^{\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_{\mathcal C^g/\mathcal C})^{-1}}: K_0(\mathcal D)_{\mathfrak m_g, {\mathbb{C}}} \to K_0(\mathcal A)_{\mathfrak m_g, {\mathbb{C}}}$$
    and
    $$(f \circ b)^{\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_{\mathcal C^g/\mathcal C})^{-1}} = a^*(\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_{\mathcal C^g/\mathcal C})^{-1}) \cdot (f \circ b)^{\mathscr O_B} $$
    by Lemma \ref{lem: Gysin pullback K0}(a). Thus
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: f!}
        f^!(-) = a^*(\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_{\mathcal C^g/\mathcal C})^{-1}) \cdot (f \circ b)^!(-): K_0(\mathcal D)_{\mathfrak m_g, {\mathbb{C}}} \to K_0(\mathcal A)_{\mathfrak m_g, {\mathbb{C}}}
    \end{equation}
    
    Next, we claim that for any $\mathcal F \in K_0(\mathcal D)_{{\mathbb{C}}}$ we have
    $$(f \circ b)^!(\mathcal F) = (i \circ e)^!(\mathcal F) = 
    a^* e^*\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_{\mathcal H^g/\mathcal H}) \cdot e^! \mathcal F$$
    Indeed, consider the morphisms of relative $K$-groups
    $$(\cap \mathcal F)_{\mathcal H}: K^0_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal H) \to K_0(\mathcal A), \,\,\,\,\, (\cap \mathcal F)_{\mathcal E}: K^0_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal E) \to K_0(\mathcal A),$$
    as well as the pullback and pushforward
    $$i^*: K^0_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal H) \to K^0_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal E), \,\,\,\,\, i_*: K^0_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal E) \xrightarrow{\sim} K^0_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal H).$$
    We note that by the projection formula
    $$(\cap \mathcal F)_{\mathcal E} \circ i^* = (\cap \mathcal F)_{\mathcal H}: K^0_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal H) \to K_0(\mathcal A).$$
    Then
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: excess 1}
        (i \circ e)^!(\mathcal F) := (\cap \mathcal F)_{\mathcal H}([i_* e_* \mathscr O_{\mathcal B}]) = (\cap \mathcal F)_{\mathcal E}(i^*[i_* e_* \mathscr O_{\mathcal B}]).
    \end{equation}
    Next
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: excess 2}
        i^* \circ i_* = (\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_{\mathcal H^g/\mathcal H}) \cdot) : K^0_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal E) \to K^0_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal H) \to K^0_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal E)
    \end{equation}
    as in \cite[Lemme 3.3]{Thomason}: because $i_*$ is an isomorphism (both groups being identified with $K_0(\mathcal B)$ by smoothness of $E,F$), it suffices to check that for a complex of $G$-equivariant sheaves $S$ supported on $B$ we have
    $$i_* \circ i^* \circ i_*([S]) = [i_*i^*i_* S] = [i_* \mathscr O_E \otimes i_* S] = [i_*(i^* i_* \mathscr O_E \otimes S)] = i_*(\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_{\mathcal H^g/\mathcal H}) \cdot [S]).$$
    Thus
    $$(i \circ e)^!(\mathcal F) \overset{(\ref{eq: excess 1})}{=} (\cap \mathcal F)_{\mathcal E}(i^*i_*[e_* \mathscr O_B]) \overset{(\ref{eq: excess 2})}{=} (\cap \mathcal F)_{\mathcal E}(\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_{F^g/F}) \cdot [e_* \mathscr O_B])$$
    $$ = (\cap \mathcal F)_{\mathcal E}(e_*[e^*\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_{\mathcal H^g/\mathcal H})]) = e^{e^* \lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_{\mathcal H^g/\mathcal H})}(\mathcal F) = a^* e^*\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_{\mathcal H^g/\mathcal H}) \cdot e^! \mathcal F$$
    by Lemma \ref{lem: Gysin pullback K0}(a).
    
    Comparing this to (\ref{eq: f!}), we see that
    $$f^!(\mathcal F) = a^* \lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_{\mathcal C^g/\mathcal C})^{-1} \cdot (i \circ e)^!(\mathcal F) = a^*(\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_{\mathcal C^g/\mathcal C})^{-1} \cdot e^* \lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_{\mathcal H^g/\mathcal H})) \cdot e^! \mathcal F \in K_0(\mathcal A)_{\mathfrak m_g, {\mathbb{C}}}.$$
    Thus it suffices to note that
    $$\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_{\mathcal C^g/\mathcal C})^{-1} \cdot e^* \lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_{\mathcal H^g/\mathcal H}) = \lambda_{-1}((b^*\mathcal N_{\mathcal C/\mathcal H}^\vee)^{\operatorname{mov}}) \in K^0(\mathcal B)_{\mathfrak m_g, {\mathbb{C}}}$$
    since
    $$(b^*\mathcal N_{\mathcal C/\mathcal H}^\vee)^{\operatorname{mov}} = (e^* i^* T_{\mathcal H}^\vee - b^* T_{\mathcal C}^\vee) - (e^* i^* T_{\mathcal H}^\vee - b^* T_{\mathcal C}^\vee)^{\operatorname{fix}} = e^*(\mathcal N^\vee_{\mathcal H^g/\mathcal H}) - \mathcal N^\vee_{\mathcal C^g/\mathcal C}$$
    and thus
    $$\lambda_{-1}(e^*\mathcal N^\vee_{\mathcal H^g/\mathcal H}) = \lambda_{-1}((b^*\mathcal N_{\mathcal C/\mathcal H}^\vee)^{\operatorname{mov}}) \cdot \lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N^\vee_{\mathcal C^g/\mathcal C}) \in K^0(\mathcal B).$$
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- lem-9: body_md -->
\label{lem: Gysin pullback K0}
    Suppose given a Cartesian square of $G$-equivariant varieties
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        A \arrow[r, "a"] \arrow[d, "b"] & B \arrow[d, hook, "c"]\\
        C \arrow[r, "d"] & D
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    with $c$ a closed embedding. \\
    (a) If $D$ is smooth, the Gysin pullback functor
    $$c^{(-)}(-): K_0(\mathcal B) \times K_0(\mathcal C) \to K_0(\mathcal A)$$
    is $K^0(\mathcal B)$-linear, where $K^0(\mathcal B)$ acts on the left side via its action on $K_0(\mathcal B)$ and on the right side via the action of $a^*: K^0(\mathcal B) \to K^0(\mathcal A)$ on $K_0(\mathcal A)$. \\
    (b) Given a $c$-perfect $G$-equivariant complex $\mathscr F \in D^b\mathrm{Coh}(B)$, the Gysin pullback
    $$c^{\mathscr F}: K_0(\mathcal C) \to K_0(\mathcal A)$$
    is $K^0(\mathcal C)$-linear, where $K^0(\mathcal C)$ acts on the left as usual and on the right through $b^*: K^0(\mathcal C) \to K^0(\mathcal A)$.
<!-- end lem-9 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
For (a), note that since $c$ is a closed embedding into a smooth variety, all coherent sheaves on $B$ are in fact $c$-perfect, so the map above is well-defined on $K_0(\mathcal B)$.

    Now, for both parts of the lemma, it suffices to note that, in the affine case $R \to S, T$, given modules $N \in \operatorname{Mod}(S)$ and $M, L \in \operatorname{Mod}(T)$ with $L$ free and finitely generated over $T$, the natural (thus $G$-equivariant) morphism $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(N, M \otimes_T L) \to \operatorname{Tor}^R_i(N, M) \otimes_T L = \operatorname{Tor}^R_i(N, M) \otimes_{S \otimes_R T} (S \otimes_R L)$ is an isomorphism. Taking a free $R$-resolution $N^\bullet$ of $N$, we have
    $$\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(N, M \otimes_T L) = H_i(N^\bullet \otimes_R M \otimes_T L) = H_i(N^\bullet \otimes_R M) \otimes_T L = \operatorname{Tor}^R_i(N, M) \otimes_T L$$
    where the second equality follows from the fact that $L$ is a flat $T$-module.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- lem-10: body_md -->
\label{lem: Tor indep}
    Suppose there is a Cartesian square of varieties
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
    A \arrow[r, "f'"] \arrow[d, "g'"] & B \arrow[d, "g"] \\
    C \arrow[r, hook, "f"] & D
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    where $f$ is a regular embedding of codimension $d$.\\
    (a) If $B$ is Cohen-Macaulay, and $A$ and $B$ are equidimensional with $\dim B - \dim A = d$, then $f'$ is also a regular embedding of codimension $d$. \\
    (b) If $f'$ is a regular embedding of codimension $d$, then
    $B$ and $C$ are $\operatorname{Tor}$-independent over $D$. In particular, we have a canonical isomorphism
    $$Lf^* Rg_* \mathscr F = Rg'_* Lf'^* \mathscr F$$
    for any $\mathscr F \in D^b\mathrm{Coh}(B).$
<!-- end lem-10 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
(a) Choose any pair of points $x \in C \subset D$ and $y \in g^{-1}(x)$. By assumption, $\mathscr I_{C, x} \subset \mathscr O_{D,x}$ is generated by a regular sequence $f_1, \ldots, f_d$. Since $A$ and $B$ are varieties, we have $\dim \mathscr O_{B,y} - \dim \mathscr O_{A,y} = (\dim B - \dim \bar{y}) - (\dim A - \dim \bar{y}) = d$ \cite[Tag 00OS]{stacks-project}. Now, since $g^* f_1, \ldots, g^* f_d$ generate $\mathscr I_{A,y} \subset \mathscr O_{B,y}$ and $B$ is Cohen-Macaulay, it follows that $g^* f_1, \ldots, g^* f_d$ form a regular sequence \cite[Tag 02JN]{stacks-project}. \\
    (b) Choose points $x \in C \subset D, y \in g^{-1}(x)$ and a Koszul-regular sequence $f_1, \ldots, f_d \in \mathscr I_{C,x}$. (Regular implies Koszul-regular by \cite[Tag 062F]{stacks-project}.) Then $\operatorname{Tor}_i^{\mathscr O_{D,x}}(\mathscr O_{C,x}, \mathscr O_{B,y})$ can be calculated using the Koszul resolution $K_\bullet(\mathscr O_{D,x}, f_1, \ldots, f_d)$ of $\mathscr O_{C,x}$. Since $g^* f_1, \ldots, g^* f_d$ generate $\mathscr I_{A,y}$ and this can be generated by a regular sequence of length $d$, we conclude that $g^* f_1, \ldots, g^* f_d$ is still a Koszul-regular sequence \cite[Tag 066A]{stacks-project}.
    In particular the pullback Koszul complex $K_\bullet(\mathscr O_{D,x}, f_1, \ldots, f_d) \otimes_{\mathscr O_{D,x}} \mathscr O_{B,y} = K_\bullet(\mathscr O_{B,y}, g^*f_1, \ldots, g^*f_d)$ is exact in positive degree, and so $\operatorname{Tor}_i^{\mathscr O_{D,x}}(\mathscr O_{C,x}, \mathscr O_{B,y}) = 0$ for $i > 0$, proving Tor independence. The second part now follows from \cite[Tag 08IB]{stacks-project}.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- defn-6: body_md -->
\label{defn: compactified Prym}
    Let $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B)$ be the relative compactified Jacobian of $X/B$, parametrizing torsion free sheaves of rank 1 and degree 0 on the fibers $X_b$.
    Consider the relative norm map
    $$\operatorname{Nm}_{X/C}: \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B) \to \operatorname{J}^0(C) \times B$$
    given pointwise by 
    $$\mathscr L_b \in \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_b) \mapsto \det (c_* \mathscr L_b) \otimes \det(c_* \mathscr O_{X_b})^\vee \in \operatorname{J}^0(C).$$
    (Note that the pushforward of a rank 1 torsion-free sheaf on $X_b$ is a rank $n$ vector bundle on $C$.)\\
    The compactified Prym fibration associated to $X \to B$ and $C$ is
    $$\pi: \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B) := \operatorname{Nm}_{X/C}^{-1}(\{\mathscr O_C\} \times B) \to B.$$
<!-- end defn-6 -->
<!-- rmk-7: body_md -->
\label{rmk: i is reg}
    Given our assumptions, the variety $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B)$ is Cohen-Macaulay \cite[Theorem 9]{AIK}. Note that $\operatorname{Nm}_{X/C}$ is $\operatorname{J}^0(C)$-equivariant, where $\operatorname{J}^0(C)$ acts on $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B)$ by pullback and tensor product, and on $\operatorname{J}^0(C) \times B$ by tensor product by the $n^{\mathrm{th}}$ power (in particular, transitively over each point of $B$). Then all fibers are of the same dimension $g(\tilde X_b) - g$, and by miracle flatness we conclude that $\operatorname{Nm}_{X/C}$ is flat. In particular, the embedding $\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B) \hookrightarrow \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B)$, which is the flat base change of $\{\mathscr O_C\} \hookrightarrow \operatorname{J}^0(C)$, is regular of codimension $g$.
<!-- end rmk-7 -->
<!-- rmk-8: body_md -->
\label{rmk: etale cover}
    From the tensor product morphism
    $$\operatorname{J}^0(C) \times \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B) \to \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B)$$
    we see that $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B)$ is the quotient of $\operatorname{J}^0(C) \times \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B)$ by the (free) diagonal action of the $n$-torsion subgroup $\operatorname{J}^0(C)[n]$. In particular, $\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B)$ is smooth if and only if the same is true of $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B)$.
<!-- end rmk-8 -->
<!-- defn-7: body_md -->
\label{defn: Gamma}
    Set $\Gamma := \operatorname{J}^0(C)[n]$. Then $\Gamma$ acts on $\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B)$ over $B$ by tensor product: for $\gamma \in \Gamma$ we set
    $$\gamma \cdot \mathscr L_b := c_b^*\gamma \otimes \mathscr L_b \in \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X_b).$$
    We use $\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B)^\gamma$ to denote the fixed locus and
    $$B_\gamma := \pi(\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B)^\gamma) \subset B$$
    to denote its image under $\pi$. (Here, the use of a subscript rather than superscript is to indicate that $B_\gamma$ is not a fixed locus, and indeed $B$ is not equipped with a nontrivial action of $\Gamma$.) Abusively, we write $IB := \coprod_{\gamma \in \Gamma} B_\gamma$ and $\iota_B: IB \to B$ for the obvious inclusion map, although $IB$ is not an inertia stack.
<!-- end defn-7 -->
<!-- rmk-9: body_md -->
\label{rmk: endoscopic locus defs}
    Another, perhaps more usual, characterization of the \textit{endoscopic locus} $B_\gamma$ is given by
    $$b \in B_\gamma \iff \gamma \in \ker(\operatorname{J}^0(C) \to \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X_b)),$$
    where $\nu: \tilde X_b \to X_b$ is the normalization.
    Indeed, if we have $b \in B_\gamma$, then by definition there is some $F \in \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X_b)$ such that $c^*_b \gamma \otimes F \cong F$. Then $\nu^* c^*_b \gamma$ fixes the line bundle $\nu^*F/T \in \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X_b)$, where $T \subset \nu^* F$ is the torsion subsheaf, thus $\nu^* c^*_b \gamma \cong \mathscr O_{\tilde X_b}$. In the other direction, note that we have a pushforward map $\nu_*: \operatorname{J}^{-k}(\tilde X_b) \to \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_b)$, for $k := h^0(X_b, \nu_* \mathscr O_{\tilde X_b}/\mathscr O_{X_b})$ (since the pushforward of a line bundle from $\tilde X_b$ remains torsion-free of rank 1), and if $\nu^* c^*_b \gamma \cong \mathscr O_{\tilde X_b}$, then by the projection formula, the image of $\nu_*$ is a $\gamma$-fixed point in $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_b)$; moreover, note that the map $\nu_*$ is $\operatorname{J}^0(C)$-equivariant, and since $\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B)$ meets each $\operatorname{J}^0(C)$-orbit, in particular it meets the image of $\nu_*$.
<!-- end rmk-9 -->
<!-- defn-8: body_md -->
\label{def: Mvee}
    Set $M := \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B)$. We define
    $$M^\vee := [\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B)/\Gamma] = [\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B)/\operatorname{J}^0(C)].$$
    We also introduce notation
    $$IM^\vee = \coprod_{\gamma \in \Gamma} [M^\gamma/\Gamma] =: \coprod_{\gamma \in \Gamma} M^{\gamma, \vee}.$$
    Since $\Gamma$ acts along the fibers of $M \to B$, we can descend $\pi$ to a morphism $\pi^\vee: M^\vee \to B$. Note as well that we have a natural morphism $\pi_{IB}: IM^\vee \to IB$ such that $\iota_B \circ \pi_{IB} = \pi^\vee \circ \iota_{M^\vee}$.
<!-- end defn-8 -->
<!-- defn-9: body_md -->
\label{def: Weil pairing}
    Consider the canonical pairing on $\Gamma$ induced by the intersection pairing on $H^1(C, {\mathbb{Z}}/n{\mathbb{Z}}) = \operatorname{J}^0(C)[n]$. This gives an isomorphism
    $$\Gamma \to \Gamma^\vee, \gamma \mapsto \langle \gamma,-\rangle,$$
    where $\Gamma^\vee$ is the dual abelian group.
    For any fixed $\gamma \in \Gamma$, we use $\kappa$ to denote the corresponding element $\langle \gamma, - \rangle \in \Gamma^\vee$.
<!-- end defn-9 -->
<!-- defn-10: body_md -->
\label{defn: delta invt}
    Recall that given a reduced curve $Y$ with normalization $\nu: \tilde Y \to Y$, the delta invariant is defined by $\delta(Y) := h^0(Y, \nu_* \mathscr O_{\tilde Y}/\mathscr O_Y),$ or alternatively the dimension of the affine (as opposed to abelian variety) part of $\operatorname{J}^0(Y)$. Given a subvariety $B' \subset B$, we define $\delta(B')$ to be $\delta(X_b)$ for a general point $b \in B'$.
<!-- end defn-10 -->
<!-- defn-11: body_md -->
\label{defn: good fibration}
    Let $X \to C \times B$ be as defined at the beginning of \S \ref{subsec: compactified Prym}. Let $M := \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}^0(X/B) \to B$ be the corresponding relative compactified Prym variety. 
    We say that $\pi: M \to B$ is a \textit{good compactified Prym fibration} if
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $M$ and $IB$ are smooth, and $\pi_{IB}: IM^\vee \to IB$ is flat
        \item (``Ng\^o conditions") For each $\gamma \in \Gamma$, the component $(R\pi_* {\mathbb{C}}_M)_\kappa$ has full support on $B_\gamma$, and each $B_\gamma$ satisfies the support inequality $\delta(B_\gamma) \ge \operatorname{codim} B_\gamma$
        \item The general fiber of $X|_{B_\gamma} \to B_\gamma$ is at worst nodal.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end defn-11 -->
<!-- rmk-10: body_md -->
\label{rmk: Severi/Ngo}
    By the Severi inequality (see, e.g., \cite[Lemma 4.1]{MS-chi-indep}), smoothness of $M$ (or equivalently, of $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B)$, by Remark \ref{rmk: etale cover}) implies that $\delta(B_\gamma) \le \operatorname{codim} B_\gamma$. Thus, the second part of (2) gives an equality $\delta(B_\gamma) = \operatorname{codim} B_\gamma$.
<!-- end rmk-10 -->
<!-- rmk-11: body_md -->
\label{rmk: Ngo}
    We call the conditions (2) ``Ng\^o conditions" because in the cases of interest, they will follow from \cite[Proposition 7.2.3]{Ngo-fundamental}. However, a priori we do not require the fibration $M \to B$ to be a weak abelian fibration as defined by Ng\^o; for the purposes of this paper, the two listed conditions suffice.
<!-- end rmk-11 -->
<!-- rmk-12: body_md -->
\label{rmk: condition 3}
    Condition (3) could probably be weakened, given an analysis of the Arinkin Poincar\'e sheaf and compactified Jacobian of curves with worse than nodal singularities, along the lines of \cite{FHHO}. However, the current formulation suffices for our cases of interest.
<!-- end rmk-12 -->
<!-- prop-5: body_md -->
\label{prop: SL Higgs is good}
    Let $D$ be either $K_C$ or a divisor on $C$ of degree $\ge 2g$. The subset $M$ over the elliptic locus of the moduli space of semistable $D$-twisted $\operatorname{SL}_n$ Higgs bundles of determinant $\mathscr L$, where $\deg \mathscr L \equiv \pm \frac{n(n-1)}{2} \deg D$ mod $n$, is a good compactified Prym fibration.
<!-- end prop-5 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
First of all, note that tensoring by any $\mathscr M \in \mathop{\rm Pic}\nolimits(C)$ defines an isomorphism $\check{M}_{n, \mathscr L}^D \cong \check{M}_{n, \mathscr L \otimes \mathscr M^{\otimes n}}^D$ over the Hitchin base; similarly, dualizing defines an isomorphism $\check{M}_{n, \mathscr L}^D \cong \check{M}^D_{n, \mathscr L^\vee}$ over the Hitchin base. Thus, we reduce to the case $\mathscr L = \mathscr O(-\frac{n(n-1)}{2} D)$, which as described above is a compactified Prym fibration.
    \\
    \\
    For condition (1), start by recalling that the open subvariety of $\check{M}_{n, \mathscr L}^D(C)$ of stable Higgs bundles is smooth. (This follows from the $\operatorname{GL}$ result \cite[Proposition 7.4]{Nitsure} by Remark \ref{rmk: etale cover}.) Now note that $M$ is contained in this locus, as the spectral curve of a direct sum of Higgs bundles breaks into a union of the spectral curves of the summands and is thus not integral.
    
    Next, recall from \cite[(29)]{MS} that $M^\gamma \to B_\gamma$ can be described as a ${\mathbb{Z}}/m{\mathbb{Z}}$-Galois quotient of an open subset of a relative Hitchin fibration $M(\pi) \to A(\pi)$, where $m := \mathrm{ord}_\Gamma(\gamma)$. Note that there is an \'etale cover $M(\pi) \times \operatorname{J}^0(C) \times H^0(C, \mathscr O(D)) \to M_{n/m, \deg \mathscr L}^{D'}(C')$ over the isomorphism $A(\pi) \times H^0(C, \mathscr O(D)) \to A(C')$, where $h_{C'}: M_{n/m, \deg \mathscr L}^{D'}(C') \to A(C')$ is the $D'$-twisted $\operatorname{GL}_{n/m}$ Hitchin fibration for the \'etale cover $C' \to C$ corresponding to $\gamma$. Since $A(\pi) \cong {\mathbb{A}}^{\dim}$ with a linear action of ${\mathbb{Z}}/m{\mathbb{Z}}$, the quotient is again ${\mathbb{A}}^{\dim}$, and in particular the open subset $B_\gamma$ is smooth. Furthermore, since $h_{C'}$ is flat \cite[Proposition 2.4.6]{dC-SL}, we conclude that the same is true of $M(\pi) \to A(\pi)$; in particular, the fiber dimension of its finite quotient $M^\gamma \to B_\gamma$ is constant, and so by miracle flatness, this morphism is flat.
    \\
    \\
    For condition (2), we note first that $M \to B$ is a weak abelian fibration by \cite[Theorem 4.8.1]{dC-SL} (which is stated for $\deg D > 2g-2$, but the proof holds for $D = K_C$).
