Then, as described in \cite[\S 4.9]{dC-SL}, from the characterization of the endoscopic loci in terms of $\ker(\operatorname{J}^0(C) \to \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X_b)) = \pi_0(\operatorname{Prym}(X_b))^\vee$ (see Remark \ref{rmk: endoscopic locus defs} and \cite[Theorem 1.1(1)]{HP}), both statements follow from \cite[Proposition 7.2.3]{Ngo-fundamental}.
    \\
    \\
    Condition (3) may be well-known, at least in the case $\deg D \ge 2g$, but for lack of a reference, we provide a proof. First, any $\gamma \in \Gamma \cong ({\mathbb{Z}}/n{\mathbb{Z}})^{2g}$ is contained in the subgroup generated by some $\beta \in \Gamma$ of order $n$, thus $M^\beta \subset M^\gamma$ and so $B_\beta \subset B_\gamma$. So without loss of generality one may assume $\gamma$ is of order $n$. Then if $\tilde C \to C$ is the \'etale degree $n$ cover trivializing $\gamma \in \operatorname{J}^0(C)[n]$, and $\tilde D$ the pullback of $D$, recall (e.g. from \cite[\S 1.5, Lemma 3.4]{MS}) that there is a ${\mathbb{Z}}/n{\mathbb{Z}}$-quotient map $H^0(\tilde C, \mathscr O_{\tilde C}(\tilde D))_{var} \to B_\gamma$, where $H^0(\tilde C, \mathscr O_{\tilde C}(\tilde D))_{var}$ is the sum of the nontrivial eigenspaces of the $\operatorname{Gal}(\tilde C/C)$ action on $H^0(\tilde C, \mathscr O_{\tilde C}(\tilde D))$; on the level of spectral curves, for each $\sigma \in H^0(\tilde C, \mathscr O_{\tilde C}(\tilde D))_{var}$, the spectral curve over the image is given by descending the union of the spectral curves $V(t-\sigma) \subset |\mathscr O_{\tilde C}(\tilde D)|$ of the Galois conjugates of $\sigma$. It thus suffices to check that for the general $\sigma \in H^0(\tilde C, \mathscr O_{\tilde C}(\tilde D))_{var}$, there is no $p \in \tilde C$ such that three distinct Galois conjugates of $\sigma$ take the same value on $p$, and moreover, when two branches $V(t-\sigma)$ and $V(t - x \cdot \sigma)$ meet, they do so transversely.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                

    To check that no more than two branches meet at a point (when $n > 2$): trivialize $\mathscr O_{\tilde C}(\tilde D)$ over an open subset $U \subset \tilde C$, and choose two disjoint elements $x,y \ne 1 \in \operatorname{Gal}(\tilde C/C)$. We define a morphism
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: bpf map}
        \alpha: U \times H^0(\tilde C, \mathscr O_{\tilde C}(\tilde D))_{var} \to {\mathbb{A}}^2, (p, \sigma) \mapsto (\sigma(p) - x \cdot \sigma(p), \sigma(p) - y \cdot \sigma(p)).
    \end{equation}
    From Lemma \ref{lem: alpha rk} we have $\dim \alpha^{-1}(0,0) = h^0(\tilde C, \mathscr O(\tilde D))_{var} - 1$, thus $\alpha^{-1}(0,0)$ does not dominate $H^0(\tilde C, \mathscr O(\tilde D))_{var}$, and we can find an open subset $V_{U,x,y} \subset H^0(\tilde C, \mathscr O(\tilde D))_{var}$ such that for any section $\sigma \in V_{U,x,y}$, elements of the set $\{\sigma, x \cdot \sigma, y \cdot \sigma\}$ do not all take the same value on any point $p \in U$. Taking the intersection over the finitely many choices of $x,y \in \operatorname{Gal}(\tilde C/C)$, as well as over a finite cover $C = \cup_i U_i$, we conclude that for general $\sigma$, the union $\cup_{x \in \operatorname{Gal}(\tilde C/C)} V(t - x \cdot \sigma)$ consists of points where no more than two branches meet.

    It remains to check that for general $\sigma$ and $x \in \operatorname{Gal}(\tilde C/C)$, the intersection $V(t - \sigma) \cap V(t - x \cdot \sigma)$ is transverse, or in other words, the zeroes of $\sigma - x \cdot \sigma$ are simple. Let $G' := \langle x \rangle \subset \operatorname{Gal}(\tilde C/C)$, and consider $\varpi: \tilde C \to \tilde C/G'$. By definition $(1-x)$ acts invertibly on $H^0(\tilde C, \mathscr O(\tilde D))_{var}$, where now we mean the variant subspace with respect to the action of $G'$ on $\tilde C$ over $\tilde C/G'$. Then it suffices to check that the general element of $H^0(\tilde C, \mathscr O(\tilde D))_{var}$ has simple zeroes. By Bertini's theorem \cite[Example 5.2.14]{PosinAG}, the general element of
    $H^0(\tilde C, \mathscr O(\tilde D))_{var}$ has only simple zeroes away from the basepoints, and since the finitely many basepoints are simple by Lemma \ref{lem: bpf}(b), the general element has only simple zeroes on them as well.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- lem-11: body_md -->
\label{lem: bpf}
    Fix a divisor $D$ on $C$ and an \'etale ${\mathbb{Z}}/m{\mathbb{Z}}$-cover $\varpi: C' \to C$. Let $D'$ be the pullback of $D$ to $C'$.\\
    (a) If $\deg D \ge 2g$, then for any character $\chi$ of ${\mathbb{Z}}/m{\mathbb{Z}}$, the component $H^0(C', \mathscr O_{C'}(D'))_\chi$ is basepoint free.\\
    (b) If $D = K_C$, then $p \in C'$ is not a basepoint of $H^0(C', \mathscr O_{C'}(D'))_{var}$ unless $m = 2$ and $C'$ is hyperelliptic with hyperelliptic divisor given by the ${\mathbb{Z}}/2{\mathbb{Z}}$-orbit of $p$. In this case $p$ is a simple basepoint.\\
<!-- end lem-11 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
(a) Suppose $p$ is a basepoint of $H^0(C', \mathscr O_{C'}( D'))_\chi$. Then the same is true of the ${\mathbb{Z}}/m{\mathbb{Z}}$-orbit $O_p$, so $H^0(C', \mathscr O(D'))_\chi = H^0(C', \mathscr O(D' - O_p))_\chi$. Using the identifications of \cite[Remark 1.6]{MS}, this means that $H^0(C, \mathscr O(D) \otimes L_\chi) = H^0(C, \mathscr O(D-\varpi(p))\otimes L_\chi)$ for a suitable torsion line bundle $L_\chi \in \operatorname{J}^0(C)$. However, this is impossible by Riemann-Roch (since by the condition on $\deg D$, there are no nontrivial $h^1$ terms).
    \\
    (b) Suppose $p \in C'$ is a basepoint of $H^0(C', \omega_{C'})_{var}$. In this case
    \begin{multline*}
        h^0(C',\omega_{C'}) - h^0(C, \omega_C) = h^0(C', \omega_{C'})_{var} = \\ h^0(C', \omega_{C'}(-O_p))_{var}  = h^0(C', \omega_{C'}(-O_p)) - h^0(C, \omega_C(-\varpi(p)))
    \end{multline*}
    $$\implies 1 = h^0(C, \omega_C) - h^0(C, \omega_C(-\varpi(p))) = h^0(C', \omega_{C'}) - h^0(C', \omega_{C'}(-O_p)).$$
    By Clifford's theorem, this is impossible unless $\deg O_p = 2$ (i.e., $m=2$), $C'$ is hyperelliptic, and $O_p$ is the hyperelliptic divisor.

    Suppose this is the case, and let $\sigma$ be the hyperelliptic involution. Then $\sigma$ commutes with all automorphisms of $C'$, in particular $\operatorname{Gal}(C'/C)$, and so defines an involution $\sigma_C$ of $C$. From the induced map $C'/\sigma = {\mathbb{P}}^1 \to C/\sigma_C$ we see that $C/\sigma_C \cong {\mathbb{P}}^1$, and $\sigma_C$ is a hyperelliptic involution on $C$. If $O_p$ is a hyperelliptic divisor, then we must have $O_p = p + \sigma(p)$, thus $\varpi(p)$ is a fixed point of $\sigma_C$, and $2\varpi(p)$ is a hyperelliptic divisor on $C$. Then
    $$h^0(C, \omega_C) - h^0(C, \omega_C(-2\varpi(p)) = 1$$
    whereas
    $$h^0(C', \omega_{C'}) - h^0(C', \omega_{C'}(-2O_p)) = 2$$
    and so $h^0(C', \omega_{C'})_{var} > h^0(C', \omega_{C'}(-2O_p))_{var} = h^0(C', \omega_{C'}(-2p))_{var}$, i.e., $p$ is a basepoint of order 1.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- lem-12: body_md -->
\label{lem: alpha rk}
    In the situation of Proposition \ref{prop: SL Higgs is good}, if $n \ge 3$, then the morphism $\alpha$ of (\ref{eq: bpf map}) satisfies
    $$\dim \alpha^{-1}(0,0) = h^0(\tilde C, \mathscr O(\tilde D))_{var} - 1.$$
<!-- end lem-12 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
We begin with the more straightforward case $\deg D \ge 2g$. We claim that for each $p \in U$, the linear map $\alpha(p,-)$ is of full rank. Indeed, since $\{x,y,1\}$ are distinct, the characters $1-x, 1-y$ of $\operatorname{Gal}(\tilde C/C)^\vee$ are linearly independent, i.e., for any $(\alpha_1, \alpha_2) \ne (0,0) \in {\mathbb{C}}^2$ there is some $\chi \in \operatorname{Gal}(\tilde C/C)^\vee$ with $\alpha_1(1-x)(\chi) + \alpha_2(1-y)(\chi) \ne 0$. By Lemma \ref{lem: bpf}(a) there is some $\sigma \in H^0(\tilde C, \mathscr O(\tilde D))_\chi$ with $\sigma(p) \ne 0$ and so $\alpha(p, \sigma) \notin \langle (-\alpha_2, \alpha_1) \rangle.$ Since this holds for any choice of $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2) \ne (0,0)$, we conclude that $\textrm{im}(\alpha(p,-))$ is not contained in any line, i.e., $\alpha(p,-)$ is of full rank 2. Thus in particular $\alpha^{-1}(0,0) \subset U \times H^0(\tilde C, \mathscr O(\tilde D))_{var}$ is of codimension 2.

    Now, suppose that $D = K_C$. We claim that $\alpha(p,-)$ is of rank 2 for general $p \in U$ and of rank $\ge 1$ for all $p$; this is still enough to conclude that $\alpha^{-1}(0,0)$ is of codimension 2. For general $p \in U$, the image $\varpi(p) \in C$ is not a basepoint of $\omega_C \otimes L_\chi$ for any $L_\chi \in \operatorname{J}^0(C)[n]$, thus as in \ref{lem: bpf}(a) we see that no $H^0(\tilde C, \mathscr O(\tilde D))_\chi$ has a basepoint at $p$, and the argument of the previous paragraph shows that $\alpha(p,-)$ is of rank 2. To show that $\alpha(p,-)$ is of rank $\ge 1$, i.e., nonzero, for any $p \in U$: let $G' := \langle x,y \rangle \subset \operatorname{Gal}(\tilde C/C) = {\mathbb{Z}}/n{\mathbb{Z}}$, and consider $\varpi: \tilde C \to \tilde C/G' $. As $\{1,x,y\}$ are distinct, we have $\deg \varpi \ge 3$, and so by Lemma \ref{lem: bpf}(b), there is $\sigma \in H^0(\tilde C, \omega_{\tilde C})_{var}$ (variant with respect to $G'$) with $\sigma(p) \ne 0$; by definition of $G'$, at least one of $(1-x) \sigma(p), (1-y)\sigma(p) \ne 0$, and so $\alpha(p,\sigma) \ne 0$, as required.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- prop-6: body_md -->
\label{prop: GS}
    Let $X \to C \times B$ be as described at the beginning of \S \ref{subsec: compactified Prym}, and assume that $\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B)$ is smooth.
    The restriction of the Arinkin Poincar\'e sheaf $\mathcal P_{J/J}$ to $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B) \times_B \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B)$ can be uniquely descended to a sheaf $\mathcal P$, flat over each factor of $[\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B)/\operatorname{J}^0(C)] \times_B \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B) = M^\vee \times_B M$.
    Taking $\mathcal P^{-1} := R\mathcal Hom(\mathcal P^T, \pi_B^* \mathscr A)[\dim \pi]$, where $\mathscr A \in \mathop{\rm Pic}\nolimits(B)$ is as defined in Lemma \ref{lem: oPrym is flat}, and $(-)^T$ denotes the pullback under the involution $M \times_B M^\vee \to M^\vee \times_B M$ switching the two factors, we have
    $$\mathcal P \circ \mathcal P^{-1} \cong \mathscr O_{\Delta_M}, \,\, \mathcal P^{-1} \circ \mathcal P \cong \mathscr O_{\Delta_{M^\vee}}.$$
<!-- end prop-6 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
For the first part, see \cite[\S 4.1]{GS} or Proposition \ref{prop: GS descent}.

    Now, we note that the left and right adjoints to the Fourier-Mukai transform $\Phi_{\mathcal P^T}: D^b\mathrm{Coh}(M) \to D^b\mathrm{Coh}(M^\vee)$ are Fourier-Mukai transforms with kernels given by the standard formulas $\mathcal P^T_L := R\mathcal Hom(\mathcal P, \pi_2^! \mathscr O_M)$ and $\mathcal P_R^T := R \mathcal Hom(\mathcal P, \pi_1^! \mathscr O_{M^\vee})$ in $D^b\mathrm{Coh}(M^\vee \times_B M)$. (This follows from the usual proof, see, e.g., \cite[Theorem 1.1]{Rizzardo}, using the theory of Grothendieck duality on Deligne-Mumford stacks, see \cite{Neeman}.) In particular, from Lemma \ref{lem: oPrym is flat}, we see that $\mathcal P_L^T \cong \mathcal P_R^T \cong (\mathcal P^{-1})^T$.

    From \cite[Proposition 4.5]{GS} we have $(\mathcal P^{-1})^T \circ \mathcal P^T \cong \mathscr O_{\Delta_M}$. Thus $\Phi_{\mathcal P^T}$ is fully faithful \cite[Corollary 1.23]{Huybrechts-FM}. Without loss of generality, we may assume that $B$ is connected; otherwise apply this argument to each component separately. Then, as described in Lemma \ref{lem: indecomposability}, we have an orthogonal direct sum decomposition of $D^b(M^\vee)$ into indecomposable components $D^b(M^\vee)_{\chi'}$ indexed by characters of the subgroup $\Gamma' \subset \Gamma$ that acts trivially on $M$. Choosing any point $b\in B$, since any $\gamma \in \Gamma'$ acts trivially on $\operatorname{Prym}(X_b)$, we see that $\gamma$ must pull back to the trivial line bundle on $X_b$, thus also the normalization $\tilde X_b$; in particular, from \cite[Theorem 1.1]{HP} we obtain a surjection $\pi_0(\operatorname{Prym}(X_b)) = \ker(\operatorname{J}^0(C) \to \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X_b))^\vee \twoheadrightarrow (\Gamma')^\vee$. Then for each $\chi' \in (\Gamma')^\vee$, picking a point $x$ in the corresponding component of $\pi_0(\operatorname{Prym}(X_b))$, it follows from Corollary \ref{cor: eigenvalue of P} and Proposition \ref{prop: smooth and singular Poincare} that $\Phi_{\mathcal P^T}(\mathscr O_x) \ne 0 \in D^b\mathrm{Coh}(M^\vee)_{\chi'}$. Thus the image of $\Phi_{\mathcal P^T}$ meets all the subcategories $D^b\mathrm{Coh}(M^\vee)_{\chi'}$. Then, since the left and right adjoints of $\Phi_{\mathcal P^T}$ agree, it follows from the proof of \cite[Proposition 1.54]{Huybrechts-FM} that $\Phi_{\mathcal P^T}$ is an equivalence (since $\mathcal D_1'$ and $\mathcal D_2'$ give a decomposition of each $D^b\mathrm{Coh}(M^\vee)_{\chi'}$ with $\mathcal D_1' \cap D^b\mathrm{Coh}(M^\vee)_{\chi'} = D^b\mathrm{Coh}(M^\vee)_{\chi'}$ for each $\chi'$).
    Then the left and right adjoint of $\Phi_{\mathcal P^T}$ is the inverse, and so we have
    $$(\mathcal P^{-1})^T \circ \mathcal P^T \cong \mathscr O_{\Delta_M}, \,\,\, \mathcal P^T \circ (\mathcal P^{-1})^T \cong \mathscr O_{\Delta_{M^\vee}}$$
    by Lemma \ref{lem: FM id}, giving the transposes of the needed identities.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- lem-13: body_md -->
\label{lem: oPrym is flat}
    The fibrations $\pi: M \to B$ and $\pi^\vee: M^\vee \to B$ are syntomic (so in particular, flat and Gorenstein), and the relative canonical bundles $\omega_\pi$ and $\omega_{\pi^\vee}$ are the pullbacks of the same line bundle $\mathscr A := \det \pi_{X/B*} \omega_{X/B} \in \mathop{\rm Pic}\nolimits(B)$ under $\pi$ and $\pi^\vee$, respectively.
<!-- end lem-13 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
By \cite[Theorem 9]{AIK} the compactified Jacobian fibration $\pi_J: \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B) \to B$ is flat, and the fibers are local complete intersections; in other words $\pi_J$ is syntomic \cite[Tag 01UF]{stacks-project}. Recall from Remark \ref{rmk: etale cover} the \'etale map
    $\operatorname{J}^0(C) \times \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B) \to \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B)$ over $B$. It follows that $M = \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B)$ and $M^\vee = [M/\Gamma]$ are syntomic over $B$.

    As for the relative canonical bundles, recall from \cite[Corollary 9]{Arinkin-cohomology} that $\omega_{\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B)/B}$ is pulled back from $\mathscr A \in \mathop{\rm Pic}\nolimits(B)$. Using the \'etale map above and triviality of $\omega_{\operatorname{J}^0(C)}$, we see that the same is true of $\omega_\pi$. To check this for $\pi^\vee$, choose any point $b \in B$. Note that any element in the kernel of the pullback map $c_b^*: \Gamma \to \operatorname{J}^0(X_b)$ acts trivially on $\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X_b)$, hence on $\omega_{\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X_b)}$. Thus the $\Gamma$-equivariant structure is determined by the $\Gamma/\ker(c^*)$-equivariant structure on $\omega_{\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X_b)} \cong \mathscr O_{\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X_b)}$. We note that restricting to the locus of line bundles $\operatorname{Prym}(X_b)$, the quotient $[\operatorname{Prym}(X_b)/(\Gamma/\ker(c^*))]$ is an algebraic group, therefore has trivial canonical bundle. Since $\operatorname{J}^0(X_b) \subset \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_b)$ is a dense open subset by \cite[Theorem 9]{AIK}, via the \'etale map above the same is true for $\operatorname{Prym}(X_b) \subset \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X_b)$.
    Then since the $\Gamma$-equivariant structure on $\mathscr O_{\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X_b)}$ for $\omega_{[\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X_b)/\Gamma]}$ agrees with that for $\mathscr O_{[\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X_b)/\Gamma]}$ on a dense open subset, we conclude that the two agree, i.e., $\omega_{[\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X_b)/\Gamma]} \cong \mathscr O_{[\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X_b)/\Gamma]}$. Returning to the family over $B$, this suffices to show that the descent data for $(\pi^\vee)^* \mathscr A$ and $\omega_{\pi^\vee}$ are the same.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- lem-14: body_md -->
\label{lem: indecomposability}
    If $B$ is connected, and $\Gamma' \subset \Gamma$ is the subgroup acting trivially on $M$, then $D^b\mathrm{Coh}(M^\vee)$ splits as an orthogonal direct sum of indecomposable categories $D^b\mathrm{Coh}(M^\vee)_{\chi'}$ running over the characters $\chi'$ of $\Gamma'$, where $D^b\mathrm{Coh}(M^\vee)_{\chi'}$ is the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on which $\Gamma'$ acts by $\chi'$.
<!-- end lem-14 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
Clearly there is such a direct sum decomposition, so the only point to check is indecomposability of the factors.
    This follows from the proof of \cite[Lemma 4.2]{BKR} applied to each $D^b\mathrm{Coh}(M^\vee)_{\chi'}$, letting $D$ be a free $\Gamma/\Gamma'$-orbit, replacing $\mathscr O_D$ with $\mathscr O_D \otimes \chi$ for any character $\chi$ of $\Gamma$ extending $\chi'$, and letting $\rho_i$ run over the set of such characters. The one additional point to note is that $\mathscr O_M \otimes \rho_i$ is an indecomposable $\Gamma$-sheaf because $\Gamma$ acts transitively on the set of connected components of $M$: to see this, since $B$ is connected, it suffices to note for each $b \in B$ that $\Gamma$ acts transitively on the set of connected components of $\operatorname{Prym}(X_b)$ \cite[Theorem 1.1(2)]{HP}, which is a dense open subset of $\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X_b)$ by \cite[Theorem 9]{AIK} and Remark \ref{rmk: etale cover}.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- lem-15: body_md -->
\label{lem: FM id}
    Let $\mathcal X$ be a smooth nice quotient, flat and proper over a smooth variety $B$. If Fourier-Mukai transform $\Phi_{\mathcal F}$ by $\mathcal F \in D^b\mathrm{Coh}(\mathcal X \times_B \mathcal X)$ induces the identity morphism on $D^b\mathrm{Coh}(\mathcal X)$, then $\mathcal F \cong \mathscr O_{\Delta_{\mathcal X/B}}.$
<!-- end lem-15 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
Let $\mathcal X = [X/G]$ be a nice presentation, with quotient map $\alpha: X \to \mathcal X$. Then $\mathcal G := (\alpha \times \alpha)^* \mathcal F$ induces the Fourier-Mukai transform
    $$\Phi_{\mathcal G} = \alpha^* \circ \alpha_* = \Phi_{(\alpha \times \alpha)^* \Delta_{\mathcal X *} \mathscr O_{\mathcal X}}$$ on $D^b\mathrm{Coh}(X)$. 
    Since $X$ is quasiprojective and $\alpha^* \circ \alpha_*$ preserves $\mathrm{Coh}(X)$, it follows from \cite[Theorem 5.7]{Genovese} that $\mathcal G \cong (\alpha \times \alpha)^* \Delta_{\mathcal X*} \mathscr O_{\mathcal X}$. Then by descent $\mathcal F = \Delta_{\mathcal X*} \mathscr L$ for some $\mathscr L \in \mathop{\rm Pic}\nolimits(\mathcal X)$, and $\Phi_{\mathcal F}(\mathscr O_{\mathcal X}) = \mathscr O_{\mathcal X}$ implies $\mathscr L \cong \mathscr O_{\mathcal X}$.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- defn-12: body_md -->
Define $b_\gamma := \dim B_\gamma$, $h_\gamma := \dim M^\gamma - \dim B_\gamma$, and $d_\gamma := h-h_\gamma$. We also write $b_1 =: b$ and $h_1 =: h$.
<!-- end defn-12 -->
<!-- rmk-13: body_md -->
\label{rmk: h-hgamma}
    We will show in Corollary \ref{cor: h-hgamma} that $h-h_\gamma = b-b_\gamma$. We use this fact freely throughout the paper.
<!-- end rmk-13 -->
<!-- rmk-14: body_md -->
\label{rmk: fermionic shift}
    When $M$ is an open subset of a moduli space of ($D=K_C$) $\operatorname{SL}_n$-Higgs bundles (see Proposition \ref{prop: SL Higgs is good}), then $d_\gamma$ is the ``fermionic shift" of \cite{HT}, as noted in \cite[Remark 0.6]{MS}. As in the formula for the stringy mixed Hodge polynomial in \cite{HT}, a class of codimension $i$ on $M^{\gamma,\vee}$ should be considered to be of codimension $i + d_\gamma$ on the inertia stack $IM^\vee$, even though in fact $\dim IM^\vee - \dim M^{\gamma,\vee} = \dim M - \dim M^\gamma = 2d_\gamma$.
<!-- end rmk-14 -->
<!-- defn-13: body_md -->
\label{def: G and p}
    Define Chow correspondences
    $$\mathfrak G := \operatorname{td}^I(\pi_{IB}^* T_{\iota_B}-T_{IM^\vee \times_B M}) \cap \tau(\mathcal P) \in \operatorname{Corr}^*_B(IM^\vee, M)$$
    $$\mathfrak G^{-1} := \operatorname{td}^I(-\pi_{IB}^* T_{IB} +T_{\iota_{M \times_B M^\vee}}) \cap \tau(\mathcal P^{-1}) \in \operatorname{Corr}^*_B(M, IM^\vee).$$
    We can decompose $\mathfrak G$ and $\mathfrak G^{-1}$ by degree and component of $IM^\vee$
    $$\mathfrak G = \sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma} \sum_{i \ge 0} \mathfrak G_{\gamma,i}, \,\, \mathfrak G_{\gamma,i} \in \operatorname{CH}_{\dim M^\gamma \times_B M + d_\gamma - i}(M^{\gamma, \vee} \times_B M) = \operatorname{Corr}_B^{i-h_\gamma}(M^{\gamma, \vee}, M)$$
    $$\mathfrak G^{-1} = \sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma} \sum_{i \ge 0} \mathfrak G_{\gamma,i}^{-1}, \,\, \mathfrak G_{\gamma,i}^{-1} \in \operatorname{CH}_{\dim M \times_B M^\gamma + d_\gamma - i}(M \times_B M^{\gamma, \vee}) = \operatorname{Corr}_B^{i-2h + h_\gamma}(M, M^{\gamma, \vee}).$$
    Furthermore, we define correspondences
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: pGgk def}
    \mathfrak p_{\gamma,k}^{\mathfrak G} := \sum_{i \le k} \mathfrak G_{\gamma, i} \circ \mathfrak G_{\gamma, 2h-i}^{-1} ,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, \mathfrak p^{\mathfrak G}_{(k_\gamma)_\gamma} := \sum_\gamma \mathfrak p^{\mathfrak G}_{\gamma, k_\gamma}, \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, \mathfrak p^{\mathfrak G}_k := \mathfrak p^{\mathfrak G}_{(k_\gamma=k)_\gamma}
    \end{equation}
    and
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: qGgk def}
     \mathfrak q_{\gamma,k}^{\mathfrak G} := \sum_{i \ge k} \mathfrak G_{\gamma, i} \circ \mathfrak G_{\gamma, 2h-i}^{-1} ,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, \mathfrak q^{\mathfrak G}_{(k_\gamma)_\gamma } := \sum_\gamma \mathfrak q^{\mathfrak G}_{\gamma, k_\gamma}, \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, \mathfrak q^{\mathfrak G}_k := \mathfrak q^{\mathfrak G}_{(k_\gamma = k)_\gamma}  
    \end{equation}
    in $\operatorname{Corr}^0_B(M,M)$.
<!-- end defn-13 -->
<!-- thm-3: body_md -->
\label{thm: main sec 2}
    Let $M \to B$ be a good compactified Prym fibration.\\
    (i) For any tuple $(k_\gamma) \in {\mathbb{N}}^\Gamma$, the correspondences $\mathfrak{p}^{\mathfrak{G}}_{(k_\gamma)_\gamma}$ and $\mathfrak{q}^{\mathfrak{G}}_{(k_\gamma)_\gamma}$ are projectors.
    Moreover, $\mathfrak{p}^{\mathfrak{G}}_{(k_\gamma)_\gamma}$ and $\mathfrak{q}^{\mathfrak{G}}_{(k_\gamma+1)_\gamma}$ are orthogonal and sum to $[\Delta_{M}]$.\\
    (ii) Fix $\gamma \in \Gamma$, with corresponding character $\kappa \in \Gamma^\vee$, as well as $k \in {\mathbb{N}}$. By (i) we may define Chow motives $P_{\gamma,k}h(M) := (M, \mathfrak{p}^{\mathfrak{G}}_{\gamma,k},0)$ and $Q_{\gamma,k}h(M) := (M, \mathfrak{q}^{\mathfrak{G}}_{\gamma,k},0)$, equipped with the preferred morphisms to and from $h(M)$. The homological realization of $P_{\gamma, k}h(M)\to h(M)$ is given by the inclusion of the $\kappa$ component and truncation morphism
    $$(\prescript{\mathfrak p}{}{\tau}_{\le k + b} \pi_* {\mathbb{Q}}_M)_\kappa \to \prescript{\mathfrak p}{}{\tau}_{\le k + b} \pi_* {\mathbb{Q}}_M \to \pi_* {\mathbb{Q}}_M.$$
    Similarly, the homological realization of $h(M) \to Q_{\gamma, k}h(M)$ is given by 
    $$\pi_* {\mathbb{Q}}_M \to \prescript{\mathfrak p}{}{\tau}_{\ge k+b} \pi_* {\mathbb{Q}}_M \to (\prescript{\mathfrak p}{}{\tau}_{\ge k+b} \pi_* {\mathbb{Q}}_M)_\kappa.$$
    (iii) For any degrees $k,l \in {\mathbb{N}}$, the composition
    $$\mathfrak{q}^{\mathfrak{G}}_{k+l+1} \circ [\Delta_{M}^{s}] \circ (\mathfrak{p}^{\mathfrak{G}}_k \times \mathfrak{p}^{\mathfrak{G}}_l) = 0.$$
    In particular, after taking the homological realization, we see that the perverse filtration $P_\bullet H^*(M)$ is multiplicative.
<!-- end thm-3 -->
<!-- prop-7: body_md -->
\label{prop: G and G-1 inverse}
    Given a smooth (but not necessarily good) compactified Prym fibration such that $IB$ is smooth and $IM^\vee \to IB$ is flat, we have
    $$\mathfrak G \circ \mathfrak G^{-1} = [\Delta_M] \in \operatorname{CH}_*(M \times_B M)$$
    $$\mathfrak G^{-1} \circ \mathfrak G = [\Delta_{IM^\vee}] \in \operatorname{CH}_*(IM^\vee \times_B IM^\vee).$$
<!-- end prop-7 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
We start with the first identity: by definition
    $$\mathfrak G \circ \mathfrak G^{-1} = Ip_{13*}(\Delta_{IM^\vee}^!(\mathfrak G^{-1} \times \mathfrak G))$$
    $$= Ip_{13*}(\operatorname{td}^I(\pi_{IB}^*(T_{\iota_B} - T_{IB}) + p_{12}^* T_{\iota_{M \times_B M^\vee}} - p_{23}^* T_{IM^\vee \times_B M}) \cap \Delta_{IM^\vee}^!(\tau(\mathcal P) \times \tau(\mathcal P^{-1})))$$
    $$= Ip_{13*}(\operatorname{td}^I(\pi_{IB}^*(T_{\iota_B} - T_{IB})
    + p_2^* T_{\iota_{M^\vee}} - p_2^* T_{IM^\vee} + \pi_B^* T_B - p_3^* T_M) \cap \delta_{IM^\vee}^!(\tau(\mathcal P) \times \tau(\mathcal P^{-1})))$$
    (where to compute $T_{IM^\vee \times_B M}$ we used that $IM^\vee \to IB$ is flat, and that $IM^\vee \times_B M = (IM^\vee \times M) \times_{(IB \times B)} IB$)
    \begin{equation*}
        \begin{aligned}[c]
        = Ip_{13*}(\operatorname{td}^I(-p_2^* \iota_{M^\vee}^*T_{M^\vee} - p_3^* T_M) \cap \Delta_{IM^\vee}^!(\tau(\mathcal P) \times \tau(\mathcal P^{-1}))) \\
        = \operatorname{td}(-p_2^*T_M) \cap Ip_{13*}(\operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(-p_2^* T_{M^\vee}) \cap \Delta_{IM^\vee}^!(\tau(\mathcal P) \times \tau(\mathcal P^{-1}))) \\
        = \operatorname{td}(-p_2^*T_M) \cap Ip_{13*}(\operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(-p_2^* T_{M^\vee}) \cap \Delta_{IM^\vee}^!(\tau(\mathcal P \boxtimes \mathcal P^{-1}))) \\
        = \operatorname{td}(-p_2^*T_M) \cap Ip_{13*}(\tau( \delta_{IM^\vee}^*(\mathcal P \boxtimes \mathcal P^{-1})))\\
        = \operatorname{td}(-p_2^*T_M) \cap \tau(p_{13*}( \delta_{IM^\vee}^*(\mathcal P \boxtimes \mathcal P^{-1})))\\
        = \operatorname{td}(-p_2^* T_M) \cap \tau(\mathcal P^{-1} \circ \mathcal P)\\
        = \operatorname{td}(-p_2^* T_M) \cap \tau(\mathscr O_{\Delta_M})
        \end{aligned}
        \qquad
        \begin{aligned}[c]
        \hphantom{x}\\
            \textrm{(Proposition \ref{prop: ttd properties}(b))}\\
            \textrm{(Theorem \ref{thm: tau properties}(b))}\\
            \textrm{(Corollary \ref{cor: part e})}\\
            \textrm{(Theorem \ref{thm: tau properties}(c))}\\
            \hphantom{x}\\
            \textrm{(Proposition \ref{prop: GS})}
        \end{aligned}
    \end{equation*}
    $$= \operatorname{td}(-p_2^* T_M) \cap \Delta_{M*} \tau(\mathscr O_M) = \operatorname{td}(-p_2^* T_M) \cap \Delta_{M*} (\operatorname{td}(T_M) \cap [M])$$
    $$= \Delta_{M*}(\operatorname{td}(-T_M+T_M) \cap [M]) = [\Delta_M].$$
\\
    The proof of the second identity is similar, though not identical: we have
    $$\mathfrak G^{-1} \circ \mathfrak G = Ip_{13*}(\Delta^!_M(\mathfrak G \times \mathfrak G^{-1}))$$
    $$= Ip_{13*}(\operatorname{td}^I(\pi_{IB}^*(T_{\iota_B} - T_{IB}) - p_{12}^* T_{IM^\vee \times_B M} + p_{23}^* T_{\iota_{M \times_B M^\vee}}) \cap \Delta_M^!(\tau(\mathcal P) \times \tau(\mathcal P^{-1})))$$
    $$ = Ip_{13*}(\operatorname{td}^I(-p_1^* T_{IM^\vee} - p_2^* T_M + p_3^* T_{\iota_{M^\vee}}) \cap \Delta_M^!(\tau(\mathcal P) \times \tau(\mathcal P^{-1})))$$
    $$ = \operatorname{td}^I(-p_1^* T_{IM^\vee} + p_2^* T_{\iota_{M^\vee}}) \cap  Ip_{13*}(\operatorname{td}^I(- p_2^* T_M) \cap \Delta_M^!(\tau(\mathcal P) \times \tau(\mathcal P^{-1})))$$
    $$ = \operatorname{td}^I(-p_1^* T_{IM^\vee} + p_2^* T_{\iota_{M^\vee}}) \cap  Ip_{13*}(\operatorname{td}^I(- p_2^* T_M) \cap \Delta_M^!(\tau(\mathcal P \boxtimes \mathcal P^{-1})))$$
    $$ = \operatorname{td}^I(-p_1^* T_{IM^\vee} + p_2^* T_{\iota_{M^\vee}}) \cap  Ip_{13*}(\tau(\delta_M^*(\mathcal P \boxtimes \mathcal P^{-1})))$$
    $$ = \operatorname{td}^I(-p_1^* T_{IM^\vee} + p_2^* T_{\iota_{M^\vee}}) \cap  \tau(p_{13*}(\delta_M^*(\mathcal P \boxtimes \mathcal P^{-1})))$$
    $$ = \operatorname{td}^I(-p_1^* T_{IM^\vee} + p_2^* T_{\iota_{M^\vee}}) \cap  \tau(\mathcal P^{-1} \circ \mathcal P)$$
    $$ = \operatorname{td}^I(-p_1^* T_{IM^\vee} + p_2^* T_{\iota_{M^\vee}}) \cap  \tau(\mathscr O_{\Delta_{M^\vee}}) = \operatorname{td}^I(-p_1^* T_{IM^\vee} + p_2^* T_{\iota_{M^\vee}}) \cap  I\Delta_{M^\vee *}\tau(\mathscr O_{M^\vee})$$
    $$ = \operatorname{td}^I(-p_1^* T_{IM^\vee} + p_2^* T_{\iota_{M^\vee}}) \cap  I\Delta_{M^\vee *}(\operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(T_{M^\vee}) \cap [IM^\vee]) \qquad \textrm{(Theorem \ref{thm: tau properties}(d))}$$
    $$ = I\Delta_{M^\vee *}(\operatorname{td}^I(-T_{IM^\vee} + T_{\iota_{M^\vee}} + \iota_{M^\vee}^*T_{M^\vee}) \cap [IM^\vee]) = [\Delta_{IM^\vee}].$$
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
Consider the morphisms $\pi_* {\mathbb{C}}_M \to \oplus \pi_*^\vee {\mathbb{C}}_{M^\vee}[i]$ and $\pi_*^\vee {\mathbb{C}}_{M^\vee} \to \oplus \pi_* {\mathbb{C}}_M[i]$ induced by $cl(\mathfrak G^{-1})$ and $cl(\mathfrak G^{-1})$, as described in \S \ref{subsubsec: constructible sheaves}. By Proposition \ref{prop: G and G-1 inverse} and the compatibilities of the cycle class map, composing these morphisms in either direction yields the identity. In particular, after passing to global cohomology we obtain inverse isomorphisms $H^*(M, {\mathbb{C}}) \leftrightarrow H^*(IM^\vee, {\mathbb{C}})$ induced by multi-degree algebraic correspondences. These may not be isomorphisms of mixed Hodge structures (and in fact, e.g., in the setting of \cite{HT} there is no such isomorphism without the proper degree/weight convention for the various components $H^*(M^{\gamma, \vee}, {\mathbb{C}}) \subset H^*(IM^\vee, {\mathbb{C}})$, see Remark \ref{rmk: fermionic shift}). However, since each fixed-degree component $H^*(M, {\mathbb{C}}) \to H^{*+k}(IM^\vee, {\mathbb{C}})$ (and vice versa) gives a morphism of mixed Hodge structures $H^*(M, {\mathbb{C}}) \to H^{*+k}(IM^\vee, {\mathbb{C}})(k)$, we obtain an isomorphism of mixed Hodge structures
    $$\oplus_k H^k(M, {\mathbb{C}})(k) \cong \oplus_k H^k(IM^\vee, {\mathbb{C}})(k)$$
    (where for the inertia stack it is equivalent to use the standard topological notion of degree or the fermionic shift, which comes with a corresponding shift in weight and is thus canceled out by the Tate twist).
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- rmk-15: body_md -->
A similar result is proved in \cite[Theorem A]{Popa}, starting with an arbitrary derived equivalence of smooth orbifolds with projective coarse spaces. (The difference for us is that $M, M^\vee$ are only projective over $B$, over which they are not smooth, necessitating the result on compatibility of $\tau$ with pullback in the singular case in Theorem \ref{thm: tau properties}(e).) As discussed in \cite[\S 3]{Popa}, this result should be understood as an example of the derived invariance of (orbifold) Hochschild homology, rather than part of the \cite{MSY} package.
<!-- end rmk-15 -->
<!-- rmk-16: body_md -->
\label{rmk: not reg}
    Note that the morphism $\delta_M: M^\vee \times_B M \times_B M^\vee \hookrightarrow M^\vee \times_B M \times M \times_B M^\vee$ used in Proposition \ref{prop: G and G-1 inverse} is a representable regular embedding such that the corresponding map of inertia stacks $I\delta_M$ is \textit{not} a regular embedding. Indeed, given $\gamma \in \Gamma$ such that $b-b_\gamma= \delta(B_\gamma) \ne 0$, we note that $(I\delta_M)_{(\gamma,\gamma)}$ is a flat base change of the inclusion
    $$M|_{B_\gamma} \hookrightarrow M|_{B_\gamma} \times M|_{B_\gamma}.$$
    Here $M|_{B_\gamma}$ is the compactified Jacobian of a family of curves whose general member is (nontrivially) nodal, thus singular (see \S \ref{subsubsec: FHHO setup} for a description of the normalization of the compactified Jacobian of a nodal curve), and so the diagonal map is not a regular embedding.
<!-- end rmk-16 -->
<!-- example-2: body_md -->
\cite[Example 3.7]{Brochard}
    The dual of a constant finite abelian group $G$ over $U$ is $D(G) = BG^\vee$, where $G^\vee = \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ab}}(G, {\mathbb{C}}^*)$ is the standard dual group. The dual of an abelian scheme $A$ over $U$ is the dual abelian scheme $A^\vee$.
<!-- end example-2 -->
<!-- prop-8: body_md -->
\label{prop: Prym has correct dual}
    (i) The dual of the commutative group stack $\operatorname{Prym}(Y/U)$ is $[\operatorname{J}^0(Y/U)/\operatorname{J}^0(C)]$, and vice versa. \\
    (ii) The dual of the abelian scheme $\operatorname{Prym}(Y/U)^\circ$ is $[\operatorname{J}^0(Y/U)/(\operatorname{J}^0(C)/K)]$ for $K := \ker(\operatorname{J}^0(C) \to \operatorname{J}^0(Y/U)$.
<!-- end prop-8 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
Consider the ``exact sequence" (see \cite[Definition 2.11]{Brochard}) of commutative group stacks
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: duality 1}
        0 \to \operatorname{J}^0(C) \to \operatorname{J}^0(Y/U) \to [\operatorname{J}^0(Y/U)/\operatorname{J}^0(C)] \to 0.
    \end{equation}
    Applying the duality functor, we obtain a short exact sequence
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: duality 2}
            0 \to D([\operatorname{J}^0(Y/U)/\operatorname{J}^0(C)]) \to \operatorname{J}^0(Y/U) \to \operatorname{J}^0(C) \to 0
    \end{equation}
    by \cite[Example 3.7]{Brochard} (since Jacobians are self-dual abelian varieties) and \cite[Proposition 3.18.a(iii)]{Brochard} (since the norm map $\operatorname{J}^0(Y/U) \to \operatorname{J}^0(C)$ is surjective). Thus $D([\operatorname{J}^0(Y/U)/\operatorname{J}^0(C)]) = \ker(\operatorname{J}^0(Y/U) \to \operatorname{J}^0(C)) = \operatorname{Prym}(Y/U)$.

    Next, we claim that $K := \ker(\operatorname{J}^0(C) \to \operatorname{J}^0(Y/U))$ is a constant group scheme: indeed, by the projection formula it is a subobject of the constant finite group scheme $\operatorname{J}^0(C)[m]$, and on the other hand it is (analytically) locally constant since $\pi_0(\operatorname{Prym}(Y/U))$ is so by Ehresmann's theorem, and we have a canonical identification $\ker(\operatorname{J}^0(C) \to \operatorname{J}^0(Y/U))^\vee = \pi_0(\operatorname{Prym}(Y/U))$ by \cite[Theorem 1.1(1)]{HP}. Note also that $[\operatorname{J}^0(Y/U)/(\operatorname{J}^0(C)/K)]$ is an abelian scheme. Then 
    $$D(\operatorname{Prym}(Y/U)) = D(D([\operatorname{J}^0(Y/U)/\operatorname{J}^0(C)])) = [\operatorname{J}^0(Y/U)/\operatorname{J}^0(C)]$$
    by \cite[Example 4.10]{Brochard}.

    Finally, it follows from \cite[Theorem 4.11]{Brochard} applied to $\operatorname{Prym}(Y/U)$ that
    $$(\operatorname{Prym}(Y/U)^\circ)^\vee = H^0([\operatorname{J}^0(C) \to \operatorname{J}^0(Y/U)]) = [\operatorname{J}^0(Y/U)/(\operatorname{J}^0(C)/K)].$$
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- lem-16: body_md -->
\label{lem: compare smooth Poincare sheaves}
    Let $f: \mathcal X \to \mathcal Y$ be a morphism of commutative group stacks. Then
    $$(1 \times Df)^* \mathcal P_{\mathcal X/D\mathcal X} = (f \times 1)^* \mathcal P_{\mathcal Y/D \mathcal Y}.$$
<!-- end lem-16 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
This follows from the statement that the following (non-Cartesian) diagram of commutative group stacks commutes
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        \mathcal X \times_U D(\mathcal Y) \arrow[r, "f \times 1"] \arrow[d, "1 \times Df"] & \mathcal Y \times_U D(\mathcal Y) \arrow[d, "ev_{\mathcal Y}"] \\
        \mathcal X \times_U D(\mathcal X) \arrow[r, "ev_{\mathcal X}"] & B {\mathbb{G}}_m
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    which is a tautology from the definition of $Df$.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- cor-3: body_md -->
\label{cor: multiplicativity of P}
    If $\mathcal X$ is a commutative group stack with addition map $\mu: \mathcal X \times_U \mathcal X \to \mathcal X$, then the Poincar\'e sheaf satisfies
    $$(\mu \times 1)^* \mathcal P_{\mathcal X/D\mathcal X} \cong p_{13}^* \mathcal P_{\mathcal X/D\mathcal X} \otimes p_{23}^* \mathcal P_{\mathcal X/D\mathcal X}.$$
    If the natural map $\mathcal X \to D(D(\mathcal X))$ is an isomorphism, then also
    $$(1 \times \mu)^* \mathcal P_{D\mathcal X/\mathcal X} \cong p_{12}^* \mathcal P_{D\mathcal X/\mathcal X} \otimes p_{13}^* \mathcal P_{D \mathcal X/\mathcal X}.$$
<!-- end cor-3 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
We apply Lemma \ref{lem: compare smooth Poincare sheaves} to $\mu$. Note that applying $D$ to the split exact sequence
    $$0 \to \mathcal X \to \mathcal X \times_U \mathcal X \to \mathcal X \to 0 = \alpha(0 \to \alpha^{-1}(\mathcal X) \to \alpha^{-1}(\mathcal X)^{\oplus 2} \to \alpha^{-1}(\mathcal X) \to 0),$$
    we obtain another split exact sequence, so $D(\mathcal X \times_U \mathcal X) \cong D(\mathcal X) \times_U D(\mathcal X)$. We then have $ev_{\mathcal X \times \mathcal X} \cong ev_{\mathcal X} \times_U ev_{\mathcal X}$, so
    $$\mathcal P_{\mathcal X \times \mathcal X/D(\mathcal X \times \mathcal X)} \cong p_{13}^* \mathcal P_{\mathcal X/D\mathcal X} \otimes p_{24}^* \mathcal P_{\mathcal X/D\mathcal X}.$$
    Since the two zero-section maps $\mathcal X \to \mathcal X \times_U \mathcal X$ compose with $\mu$ to give the identity, we see that $D\mu = \Delta_{D(\mathcal X)}: D(\mathcal X) \to D(\mathcal X \times_U \mathcal X)$ and thus
    $$(\mu \times 1)^* \mathcal P_{\mathcal X/D\mathcal X} \cong  (1 \times \Delta_{D(\mathcal X)})^* (p_{13}^* \mathcal P_{\mathcal X/D\mathcal X} \otimes p_{24}^* \mathcal P_{\mathcal X/D\mathcal X}) = p_{13}^* \mathcal P_{\mathcal X/D\mathcal X} \otimes p_{23}^* \mathcal P_{\mathcal X/D\mathcal X}.$$

    For the second statement, one applies Lemma \ref{lem: compare smooth Poincare sheaves} to $\Delta_{D(\mathcal X)} = D\mu$, noting that
    $$(1 \times DD\mu)^* \mathcal P_{D\mathcal X/DD\mathcal X} = (1 \times \mu)^* \mathcal P_{D \mathcal X/\mathcal X}$$
    and
    $$(\Delta_{D(\mathcal X)} \times 1)^* \mathcal P_{D\mathcal X \times D\mathcal X/ DD\mathcal X \times DD\mathcal X}  = (\Delta_{D(\mathcal X)} \times 1)^* \mathcal P_{D\mathcal X \times D\mathcal X/ \mathcal X \times \mathcal X} $$
    $$\cong (\Delta_{D \mathcal X} \times 1)^*(p_{13}^*\mathcal P_{D\mathcal X/\mathcal X} \otimes p_{24}^* \mathcal P_{D \mathcal X/\mathcal X}) = p_{12}^* \mathcal P_{D \mathcal X/\mathcal X} \otimes p_{13}^* \mathcal P_{D \mathcal X/\mathcal X}.$$
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- cor-4: body_md -->
\label{cor: smooth Prym P/P vs J/J}
    The Poincar\'e bundle $\mathcal P_{D(\operatorname{Prym})/\operatorname{Prym}}$ is obtained from $\mathcal P_{J/J}$ on $\operatorname{J}^0(Y/U) \times_U \operatorname{J}^0(Y/U)$ as in Proposition \ref{prop: GS}, by restricting to $\operatorname{Prym}(Y/U)$ in the second factor and descending to $[\operatorname{J}^0(Y/U)/\operatorname{J}^0(C)]$ in the first.
<!-- end cor-4 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
This follows directly from Lemma \ref{lem: compare smooth Poincare sheaves} applied to $i: \operatorname{Prym}(Y/U) \hookrightarrow \operatorname{J}^0(Y/U)$. Indeed, since (\ref{eq: duality 1}) and (\ref{eq: duality 2}) were shown to be dual in the proof of Proposition \ref{prop: G and G-1 inverse}, we see that $Di$ is the quotient $\operatorname{J}^0(Y/U) \to [\operatorname{J}^0(Y/U)/\operatorname{J}^0(C)]$.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- cor-5: body_md -->
\label{cor: eigenvalue of P}
    An element $\gamma \in K := \ker(\operatorname{J}^0(C) \to \operatorname{J}^0(Y/U))$ acts on $\mathcal P_{D(\operatorname{Prym})/\operatorname{Prym}}$ such that the eigenvalue on $D(\operatorname{Prym}(Y/U)) \times_U \operatorname{Prym}^\alpha(Y/U)$ for any $\alpha \in \pi_0(\operatorname{Prym}(Y/U)) = K^\vee$ is given by $\alpha(\gamma) \in {\mathbb{C}}^*$.
<!-- end cor-5 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
First, note that $D(BK)$ can be described as follows \cite[Corollary 3.5]{Brochard}: isomorphism classes of morphisms $BK \to B{\mathbb{G}}_m$ are given by morphisms $[K \to 0] \to [{\mathbb{G}}_m \to 0]$ in $D^{[-1,0]}(U, {\mathbb{Z}})$, i.e., $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ab}}(K, {\mathbb{G}}_m) = K^\vee$. It follows from this description of  $D(BK)$ and the evaluation map that for each $\alpha \in K^\vee$, $K$ acts on $\mathcal P_{BK/K^\vee}|_{BK \times \alpha}$ by the character $\alpha$.

    Next, note that the morphism of complexes $[K \to 0] \to [\operatorname{J}^0(C) \to \operatorname{J}^0(Y/U)]$ gives a morphism of commutative group stacks $f: BK \to D(\operatorname{Prym}(Y/U))$ fitting into the canonical truncation exact sequence \cite[Example 2.13]{Brochard}
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: trunc}
    0 \to BK \to D(\operatorname{Prym}(Y/U)) \to [\operatorname{Prym}(Y/U)/(\operatorname{J}^0(C)/K)] \to 0.        
    \end{equation}
    Dualizing, by \cite[Remark 3.19, Corollary 11.5(ii)]{Brochard}, we obtain the exact sequence
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: trunc D}
     0 \to \operatorname{Prym}(Y/U)^\circ \to \operatorname{Prym}(Y/U) \to K^\vee \to 0. 
    \end{equation}
    Using this to identify $K^\vee = \pi_0(\operatorname{Prym}(Y/U))$, we see that $Df: \operatorname{Prym}(Y/U) \to \pi_0(\operatorname{Prym}(Y/U))$ is given by $\operatorname{Prym}(Y/U)^{\alpha} \mapsto \alpha$.    
    
    Finally, viewing $\mathcal P_{D(\operatorname{Prym})/\operatorname{Prym}}$ as a $\operatorname{J}^0(C)[m]$-equivariant line bundle on $\operatorname{Prym}(Y/U) \times_U \operatorname{Prym}(Y/U)$, we note that $\operatorname{J}^0(C)[m]$ acts transitively on $\pi_0(\operatorname{Prym}(Y/U))$ \cite[Theorem 1.1(2)]{HP}, and so it suffices to calculate the eigenvalue on the zero section $\{\mathscr O\} \times_U \operatorname{Prym}(Y/U)$, i.e., identify the $K$-action on $(f \times 1)^* \mathcal P_{D(\operatorname{Prym})/\operatorname{Prym}}$ on $BK \times_U \operatorname{Prym}(Y/U)$. Combining the isomorphism $(f \times 1)^* \mathcal P_{D(\operatorname{Prym})/ \operatorname{Prym}} \cong (1 \times Df)^* \mathcal P_{BK/K^\vee}$ of Lemma \ref{lem: compare smooth Poincare sheaves} with the description of $\mathcal P_{BK/K^\vee}$ in the first paragraph and the description of $Df$ in the second paragraph, we see that $K$ acts on $(f \times 1)^* \mathcal P_{D(\operatorname{Prym})/\operatorname{Prym}}|_{D(\operatorname{Prym}) \times \operatorname{Prym}^\alpha}$ by the character $\alpha \in K^\vee = \pi_0(Y/U)$.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- prop-9: body_md -->
\label{prop: components of smooth chP}
    For any $\gamma \in K$ and $\alpha \in K^\vee$, we have
    $$cl((1 \times f_\alpha)^*\tilde{\mathfrak G}_{\gamma, \alpha}) = (\alpha(\gamma) \cdot cl((g \times 1)^* \mathfrak F))_{\gamma \in K} \in \oplus_{\gamma \in K} H^{BM}_*(D(\operatorname{Prym}) \times_U \operatorname{Prym}^\circ).$$
<!-- end prop-9 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
First, note that
    $$(1 \times f_\alpha)^* \mathcal P_{D(\operatorname{Prym})/\operatorname{Prym}} = (1 \times \mu(L_\alpha, -))^* \mathcal P_{D(\operatorname{Prym})/\operatorname{Prym}} \cong p_1^* \mathcal P_\alpha \otimes \mathcal P_{D(\operatorname{Prym})/\operatorname{Prym}}$$
    by Corollary \ref{cor: multiplicativity of P}, using the fact that $\operatorname{Prym} = D(D(\operatorname{Prym}))$ \cite[Theorem 4.13(i)]{Brochard}. In particular, if $j: \operatorname{Prym}^\circ \hookrightarrow \operatorname{Prym}$ is the inclusion, then
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: smooth comparison 1}
    (1 \times f_\alpha)^* \tilde{\mathfrak G}_{\gamma,\alpha} = \operatorname{\widetilde{Ch}}(p_1^* \mathcal P_\alpha \otimes (1 \times j)^*\mathcal P_{D(\operatorname{Prym})/\operatorname{Prym}})_\gamma.   
    \end{equation}
    Now, from the pair of dual exact sequences (\ref{eq: trunc}) and (\ref{eq: trunc D}) we see that $j = Dg$. Thus, by Lemma \ref{lem: compare smooth Poincare sheaves} we have
    $$(1 \times j)^* \mathcal P_{D(\operatorname{Prym})/\operatorname{Prym}} = (g \times 1)^* \mathcal P_{(\operatorname{Prym}^\circ)^\vee/\operatorname{Prym}^\circ}.$$
    Using the compatibility of the operational class $\operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}$ with pullback (Proposition \ref{prop: ttd properties}(a)), we see that
    $$\operatorname{\widetilde{Ch}}((1 \times j)^* \mathcal P_{D(\operatorname{Prym})/\operatorname{Prym}}) = (g \times 1)^* \operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal P_{(\operatorname{Prym}^\circ)^\vee/\operatorname{Prym}^\circ}) \in \operatorname{CH}_*(D(\operatorname{Prym}) \times_U \operatorname{Prym}^\circ).$$
    Combining this with (\ref{eq: smooth comparison 1}), we have
    $$(1 \times f_\alpha)^* \tilde{\mathfrak G}_{\gamma,\alpha} = \operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}(p_1^* \mathcal P_\alpha) \cap (g \times 1)^*\mathfrak F.$$
    Applying the cycle class map, we obtain the needed result from Lemma \ref{lem: Palpha top trivial}.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- lem-17: body_md -->
\label{lem: Palpha top trivial}
    We have $c_1(\mathcal P_\alpha) = 0 \in H^*(D(\operatorname{Prym}), {\mathbb{C}})$, and $K$ acts on $\mathcal P_\alpha$ by the character $\alpha \in K^\vee$. In particular, for any $(C_\gamma)_{\gamma \in K} \in \operatorname{CH}_*(D(\operatorname{Prym}) \times_U \operatorname{Prym}^\circ)$ we have
    $$cl(\operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}(p_1^* \mathcal P_\alpha) \cap (C_\gamma)_{\gamma \in K}) = (\alpha(\gamma) \cdot cl(C_\gamma))_{\gamma \in K}.$$
<!-- end lem-17 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
First, since the $\operatorname{J}^0(C)[m]$-quotient map $k:\operatorname{Prym} \to D(\operatorname{Prym})$ induces an injection on cohomology, it suffices to show the vanishing of $c_1(k^* \mathcal P_\alpha)$. Letting $i: \operatorname{Prym} \hookrightarrow \operatorname{J}^0$ be the inclusion, recall from the proof of Corollary \ref{cor: smooth Prym P/P vs J/J} that $k = Di \circ i$, and thus
    $$k^* \mathcal P_\alpha = (i \times 1)^* (Di \times 1)^*\mathcal P_{D(\operatorname{Prym})/\operatorname{Prym}}|_{\operatorname{Prym} \times \{L_\alpha\}}$$
    $$= (i \times 1)^* (1 \times i)^*\mathcal P_{J/J}|_{\operatorname{Prym} \times \{L_\alpha\}} = \mathcal P_{J/J}|_{\operatorname{Prym} \times \{L_\alpha\}}$$
    by Lemma \ref{lem: compare smooth Poincare sheaves}. We now note that under the pullback $l: \operatorname{J}^0(C) \to \operatorname{J}^0(Y/U)$, we obtain a family of line bundles $(i \times l)^* \mathcal P_{J/J}$ on $\operatorname{Prym}(Y/U)$ over the connected base $\operatorname{J}^0(C)$ with $(i \times l)^* \mathcal P_{J/J}|_{\operatorname{Prym} \times \{\mathscr O_C\}} \cong \mathscr O_{\operatorname{Prym}}$. Then $c_1(\mathcal P_{J/J}|_{\operatorname{Prym} \times L_\alpha}) = c_1(\mathscr O_{\operatorname{Prym}}) = 0$ since these two classes are algebraically, thus also topologically, equivalent.

    Next, it follows from Corollary \ref{cor: eigenvalue of P} that $K$ acts on $\mathcal P_\alpha$ via the character $\alpha$, and so
    $$\operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}(\mathcal P_\alpha) = (\alpha(\gamma) \cdot {\mathrm{ch}}^{EG}(\mathcal P_\alpha))_{\gamma \in K} \in \operatorname{CH}^*(ID(\operatorname{Prym})) = \oplus_{\gamma \in K} \operatorname{CH}^*(D(\operatorname{Prym})).$$
    Recalling from \S \ref{subsubsec: constructible sheaves} the compatibility of Chern classes with the cycle class map, we have
    $$cl(\operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}(\mathcal P_\alpha) \cap (C_\gamma)_{\gamma \in K}) = (\alpha(\gamma) \cdot {\mathrm{ch}}^{EG}_{top}(\mathcal P_\alpha))_\gamma \cap (cl(C_\gamma))_\gamma = (\alpha(\gamma) \cdot cl(C_\gamma))_\gamma$$
    by the vanishing of $c_1(\mathcal P_\alpha)$.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- prop-10: body_md -->
\label{prop: components of smooth chP-1}
    For any $\gamma \in K$ and $\alpha \in K^\vee$, we have
    $$cl((f_\alpha \times 1)^*\tilde{\mathfrak G}_{\gamma, \alpha}^{-1}) = (\alpha(\gamma^{-1}) \cdot cl((1 \times g)^* \mathfrak F^{-1}))_{\gamma \in K} \in \oplus_{\gamma \in K} H^{BM}_*(\operatorname{Prym}^\circ \times_U D(\operatorname{Prym})).$$
<!-- end prop-10 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
Exactly as in Proposition \ref{prop: components of smooth chP} we have
    $$cl((f_\alpha \times 1)^* 
    \operatorname{\widetilde{Ch}}(\mathcal P^\vee_{\operatorname{Prym}/D(\operatorname{Prym})})_{\alpha, \gamma})= \alpha(\gamma^{-1}) cl((1 \times g)^*\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal P^\vee_{\operatorname{Prym}^\circ/(\operatorname{Prym}^\circ)^\vee}))$$
    in $H^{BM}_*(\operatorname{Prym}^\circ \times_U D(\operatorname{Prym})).$
    Then applying
    $$cl(\operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}(\pi_U^* \mathscr A[d])_\gamma \cap \operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(-\pi_U^* T_U + T_{\operatorname{Prym}^\circ \times D(\operatorname{Prym})})_\gamma) $$
    $$= cl((1 \times g)^*({\mathrm{ch}}(\pi_U^* \mathscr A[d]) \cap \operatorname{td}(-\pi_U^* T_U + T_{\operatorname{Prym}^\circ \times (\operatorname{Prym}^\circ)^\vee}))) \in H^*(\operatorname{Prym}^\circ \times_U D(\operatorname{Prym}))$$
    to both sides (where for the equality we use Proposition \ref{prop: ttd properties}(a) and the fact that $g^* T_{(\operatorname{Prym}^\circ)^\vee} = T_{D(\operatorname{Prym})}$), the needed result follows from Theorem \ref{thm: tau properties}(a) and (d).
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- example-3: body_md -->
\label{ex: Fourier for finite G}
    Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, and let $G^\vee$ be its dual. Recall from the proof of Corollary \ref{cor: eigenvalue of P} that $BG$ and $G^\vee$ are dual commutative group stacks, and $\mathcal P_{BG/G^\vee}$ is the trivial vector bundle on $G^\vee$ such that $G$ acts on the fiber over $\alpha \in G^\vee$ by the character $\alpha$. We see that
    $$\operatorname{\widetilde{Ch}}(\mathcal P_{BG/G^\vee}) = (\alpha(\gamma) [BG \times_U \{\alpha\}])_{\gamma \in G, \alpha \in G^\vee} \in \oplus_{\gamma \in G, \alpha \in G^\vee} \operatorname{CH}_*(BG \times_U \{\alpha\})$$
    with inverse
    $$\operatorname{\widetilde{Ch}}(\mathcal P_{G^\vee/BG}^{-1}) = (\alpha(\gamma^{-1}) [\{\alpha\} \times_U BG])_{\gamma \in G, \alpha \in G^\vee} \in \oplus_{\gamma \in G, \alpha \in G^\vee} \operatorname{CH}_*( \{\alpha\} \times_U BG).$$
                      
                                                                                                                 
                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
    Consider the decomposition of $H^*(G^\vee)$ into isotypic components indexed by elements $\gamma \in G$: we have
    $$H^*(G^\vee)_\gamma = H^*(U) \cdot (\alpha(\gamma))_\alpha \subset H^*(G^\vee) = \oplus_{\alpha \in G^\vee} H^*(U).$$
    Then note that the cycle class of $\operatorname{\widetilde{Ch}}(\mathcal P^{-1}_{G^\vee/BG})_\gamma$ for any $\gamma \in G$ gives a morphism
    $$H^*(G^\vee) = \oplus_\alpha H^*(U) \to H^*(BG) = H^*(U), (x_\alpha)_\alpha \mapsto \frac{1}{\# G} \sum_\alpha \alpha(\gamma^{-1}) x_\alpha,$$
    which is trivial on all isotypic components other than $H^*(G^\vee)_\gamma$ but defines an isomorphism $H^*(G^\vee)_\gamma \to H^*(BG)$.
<!-- end example-3 -->
<!-- prop-11: body_md -->
\label{prop: MSY smooth}
    The $\mathfrak p_k, \mathfrak q_k \in \operatorname{Corr}^0_U(\operatorname{Prym}^\circ, \operatorname{Prym}^\circ)$ are projectors, such that the homological realization of $(\operatorname{Prym}^\circ, \mathfrak p_k, 0) \to (\operatorname{Prym}^\circ, \Delta_{\operatorname{Prym}^\circ}, 0)$ is the perverse truncation
    $$\prescript{\mathfrak p}{}{\tau}_{\le k+\dim U} \pi_{U*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}^\circ} \to \pi_{U*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}^\circ}$$
    and the homological realization of $(\operatorname{Prym}^\circ, \Delta_{\operatorname{Prym}^\circ}, 0) \to (\operatorname{Prym}^\circ, \mathfrak q_k, 0)$ is
    $$\pi_{U*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}^\circ} \to \prescript{\mathfrak p}{}{\tau}_{\ge k +\dim U} \pi_{U*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}^\circ}.$$
<!-- end prop-11 -->
<!-- prop-12: body_md -->
\label{prop: (ii) smooth}
    Theorem \ref{thm: main sec 2}(ii) holds for the smooth Prym fibration $\pi_U: \operatorname{Prym}(Y/U) \to U$.
<!-- end prop-12 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
Note that components of $I(D(\operatorname{Prym}))$ are indexed by $\gamma \in K$ and that $\ker(\operatorname{J}^0(C)[m] \to \pi_0(\operatorname{Prym}))$ acts trivially on $\pi_{U*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}}$ (see \cite[Lemma 7.2]{HP}), and so the isotypic components of $\pi_{U*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}}$ are indexed by characters of $\pi_0(\operatorname{Prym}) = K^\vee$, i.e., by elements of $K$. As noted in \cite[Proof of Proposition 1.3]{MS}, the character $\operatorname{J}^0(C)[m] \to \pi_0(\operatorname{Prym}) \xrightarrow{\gamma} {\mathbb{C}}^*$ can be described in terms of the Weil pairing as $\kappa := \langle \gamma, - \rangle$; we use $(\pi_{U*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}})_\gamma$ and $(\pi_{U*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}})_\kappa$ interchangeably to describe this component.
    
    We consider only $\mathfrak p_{\gamma, k}^{\tilde{\mathfrak G}}$; the proof for $\mathfrak q_{\gamma, k}^{\tilde{\mathfrak G}}$ is identical. By definition and the compatibility of the cycle class map with the operations on Chow groups (see \S \ref{subsubsec: constructible sheaves}) we have
    $$cl(\mathfrak p_{\gamma, k}^{\tilde{\mathfrak G}}) = \sum_{i \le k} cl(\tilde{\mathfrak G}_{\gamma,i}) \circ cl(\tilde{\mathfrak G}^{-1}_{\gamma, 2d-i})  = \bigg(\sum_{i \le k} cl(\tilde{\mathfrak G}_{\gamma,\beta,i}) \circ cl(\tilde{\mathfrak G}^{-1}_{\gamma, \alpha, 2d-i})\bigg)_{\alpha, \beta \in K^\vee}$$
    $$= \bigg(\sum_{i \le k} \beta(\gamma) cl((g \times 1)^* \mathfrak F_i) \circ \alpha(\gamma^{-1}) cl((1 \times g)^* \mathfrak F^{-1}_{2d-i}) \bigg)_{\alpha, \beta \in K^\vee}\in \oplus_{\alpha, \beta \in K^\vee} H^{BM}_*(\operatorname{Prym}^\circ \times_U \operatorname{Prym}^\circ)$$
    by Propositions \ref{prop: components of smooth chP} and \ref{prop: components of smooth chP-1}, where here we use the isomorphisms $(f_\alpha \times f_\beta): \operatorname{Prym}^\circ \times_U \operatorname{Prym}^\circ \xrightarrow{\sim} \operatorname{Prym}^\alpha \times_U \operatorname{Prym}^\beta$ to identify the sum with $H_*^{BM}(\operatorname{Prym} \times_U \operatorname{Prym})$
    $$ = \bigg( \sum_{i \le k} \alpha^{-1}\beta(\gamma) \cdot cl( \mathfrak F_i \circ [\Gamma_g]) \circ cl([\Gamma_g]^T \circ  \mathfrak F^{-1}_{2d-i}) \bigg)_{\alpha, \beta \in K^\vee}$$
    by Lemma \ref{lem: composition with graphs}(a)
    $$ = \bigg(\sum_{i \le k} \alpha^{-1}\beta(\gamma) \cdot cl( \mathfrak F_i \circ [\Gamma_g] \circ [\Gamma_g]^T \circ  \mathfrak F^{-1}_{2d-i})\bigg)_{\alpha, \beta \in K^\vee}$$
    $$ = \frac{1}{\# K} \bigg(\sum_{i \le k} \alpha^{-1}\beta(\gamma) \cdot cl( \mathfrak F_i \circ  \mathfrak F^{-1}_{2d-i})\bigg)_{\alpha, \beta \in K^\vee} = \frac{1}{\# K} \bigg( \alpha^{-1}\beta(\gamma) \cdot cl( \mathfrak p_k) \bigg)_{\alpha, \beta \in K^\vee}$$
    by Lemma \ref{lem: composition with graphs}(b). Then as in Example \ref{ex: Fourier for finite G} we note that the corresponding morphism of $\pi_{U*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}}$ is trivial on all $K$-isotypic components other than $(\pi_{U*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}})_\gamma$, and under the isomorphism
    $$h := (\alpha(\gamma) \cdot)_{\alpha \in K^\vee}: \pi_{U*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}^\circ} \xrightarrow{\sim} (\pi_{U*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}})_\gamma \subset \oplus_{\alpha \in K^\vee} \pi_{U*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}^\circ}$$
    we see that
    $$\pi_{U*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}^\circ} \xrightarrow{h} (\pi_{U*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}})_\gamma \subset \pi_{U*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}} \xrightarrow{cl(\mathfrak p^{\tilde{\mathfrak G}}_{\gamma, k})} \pi_{U*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}} \cong \oplus_{\beta \in K^\vee} \pi_{U*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}^\circ}$$
    is given by
    $$\frac{1}{\# K} \bigg(\sum_{\alpha \in K^\vee} \alpha(\gamma) \cdot \alpha^{-1} \beta(\gamma) \cdot cl(\mathfrak p_k)\bigg)_{\beta \in K^\vee} = (\beta(\gamma) \cdot cl(\mathfrak p_k))_{\beta \in K^\vee} = h \circ cl(\mathfrak p_k).$$
    In other words, we see that the morphisms induced by $\mathfrak p^{\tilde{\mathfrak G}}_{\gamma, k}$ and $\mathfrak p_k$ agree under the isomorphism $h: \pi_{U*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}^\circ} \xrightarrow{\sim} (\pi_{U*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}})_\kappa $, and thus, by Proposition \ref{prop: MSY smooth}, the image of $cl(\mathfrak p_{\gamma, k}^{\tilde{\mathfrak G}})$ is exactly
    $$\prescript{\mathfrak p}{}{\tau}_{\le k + \dim U} (\pi_{U*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}})_\kappa.$$
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- lem-18: body_md -->
\label{lem: composition with graphs}
    (a) Let $\mathcal X, \mathcal Y, \mathcal Z$ be smooth nice quotients, all of which are proper over a smooth base variety $B$. Given $\eta \in \operatorname{Corr}_B^*(\mathcal X,\mathcal Y)$ and a morphism $f: \mathcal Y \to \mathcal Z$ over $B$ with graph $[\Gamma_f] \in \operatorname{Corr}^*_B(\mathcal Y, \mathcal Z)$, we have
    $$(1 \times f)_* \eta = [\Gamma_f] \circ \eta, \,\, \textrm{and the transpose} \,\, (f \times 1)_* \eta^T = \eta^T \circ [\Gamma_f]^T.$$
    Similarly, given $\eta \in \operatorname{Corr}_B^*(\mathcal Z, \mathcal X)$, we have
    $$(f \times 1)^* \eta = \eta \circ [\Gamma_f], \,\, \textrm{and the transpose} \,\, (1 \times f)^* \eta^T = [\Gamma_f]^T \circ \eta^T.$$

    (b) Let $[\Gamma_g] \in \operatorname{Corr}^0_U(D(\operatorname{Prym}), (\operatorname{Prym}^\circ)^\vee)$ be the graph of the morphism $g$ defined in (\ref{eq: def of g}). We have
    $$[\Gamma_g] \circ [\Gamma_g]^T = \frac{1}{\# K} [\Delta_{(\operatorname{Prym}^\circ)^\vee}] \in \operatorname{Corr}^0_U((\operatorname{Prym}^\circ)^\vee, (\operatorname{Prym}^\circ)^\vee).$$
<!-- end lem-18 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
Part (a) follows as in the scheme case (see \cite[Proposition 16.1.1(c)]{Fulton}, which is stated in the case that $B$ is trivial but holds in this generality). The point to note is that the diagonal $\delta_{\mathcal Y}$ for the first statement, respectively $\delta_{\mathcal Z}$ for the second, is a representable regular local immersion in the sense of \cite[\S 4.1]{Kresch}, and thus there is a well-defined Gysin pullback satisfying the standard compatibilities with flat pullback and projective pushforward.

    For part (b), consider the stack of Cartesian squares
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        D(\operatorname{Prym}) \arrow[r] \arrow[d, "g \times 1 \times g"] & D(\operatorname{Prym}) \times D(\operatorname{Prym}) \arrow[d, "(g \times 1) \times (1 \times g)"] \\
        (\operatorname{Prym}^\circ)^\vee \times_U D(\operatorname{Prym}) \times_U (\operatorname{Prym}^\circ)^\vee \arrow[d, "p_2"] \arrow[r] & (\operatorname{Prym}^\circ)^\vee \times_U D(\operatorname{Prym}) \times D(\operatorname{Prym}) \times_U (\operatorname{Prym}^\circ)^\vee \arrow[d, "p_{23}"] \\
        D(\operatorname{Prym}) \arrow[r, "\Delta_{D(\operatorname{Prym})}"] & D(\operatorname{Prym}) \times D(\operatorname{Prym})
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    We start by observing that
    $$\Delta_{D(\operatorname{Prym})}^!([\Gamma_g]^T \times [\Gamma_g]) = \Delta^!_{D(\operatorname{Prym})}(g \times 1 \times 1 \times g)_* [D(\operatorname{Prym}) \times D(\operatorname{Prym})] $$
    $$= (g \times 1 \times g)_* \Delta_{D(\operatorname{Prym})}^![D(\operatorname{Prym}) \times D(\operatorname{Prym})]$$
    by the generalization of \cite[Theorem 6.2(a)]{Fulton} (see \cite[\S 4.1]{Kresch}), noting that $\Delta_{D(\operatorname{Prym})}$ is a regular local immersion
    $$=(g \times 1 \times g)_* [D(\operatorname{Prym})]$$
    by the corresponding statement on schematic approximations (noting that $\Delta_{D(\operatorname{Prym})}$ is representable). Thus, we see that
    $$[\Gamma_g] \circ [\Gamma_g]^T = p_{13*} (g \times 1 \times g)_* [D(\operatorname{Prym})] = \Delta_{(\operatorname{Prym}^\circ)^\vee *} g_*[D(\operatorname{Prym})]$$
    $$= \frac{1}{\# K} [\Delta_{(\operatorname{Prym}^\circ)^\vee}] \in \operatorname{Corr}^0_U((\operatorname{Prym}^\circ)^\vee, (\operatorname{Prym}^\circ)^\vee),$$
    as $D(\operatorname{Prym})$, respectively $(\operatorname{Prym}^\circ)^\vee$, is a $\operatorname{J}^0(C)[m]$-quotient, respectively $\operatorname{J}^0(C)[m]/K$-quotient, of $\operatorname{Prym}$.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- defn-14: body_md -->
\label{def: PMod}
    Consider the ${\mathbb{P}}^1$-bundle
    $${\mathbb{P}}_i := {\mathbb{P}}((\sigma_i^1 \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}_{\tilde X/J} \oplus (\sigma_i^2 \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}_{\tilde X/J})$$
    over $\operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)$.
    We define varieties
    $$\operatorname{PMod} := {\mathbb{P}}_1 \times_{\operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)} \cdots \times_{\operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)} {\mathbb{P}}_k, \,\,\,\operatorname{PMod}_P := \operatorname{Prym}(\tilde X/U) \times_{\operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)} \operatorname{PMod}$$
    as well as line bundles
    $$\mathcal V := \mathscr O_{{\mathbb{P}}_1}(-1) \boxtimes \cdots \boxtimes \mathscr O_{{\mathbb{P}}_k}(-1) \in \mathop{\rm Pic}\nolimits(\operatorname{PMod}), \,\,\, \mathcal V_P := \mathcal V|_{\operatorname{PMod}_P}.$$
    (Note that $\operatorname{PMod}$ is independent of the choice of normalization of $\tilde{\mathcal P}_{\tilde X/J}$, but $\mathcal V$ is not.)
<!-- end defn-14 -->
<!-- prop-13: body_md -->
\label{prop: PMod = Sigma}
    The morphism $(f, p): \operatorname{PMod} \to \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U) \times_U \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)$ is a closed embedding whose image is the closure of the graph of the pullback morphism $\nu^*: \operatorname{J}^0(X/U) \to \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)$. The same holds for $(f_P, p_P): \operatorname{PMod}_P \to \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U) \times_U\operatorname{Prym}(\tilde X/U)$ and $\nu^*: \operatorname{Prym}(X/U) \to \operatorname{Prym}(\tilde X/U)$.
<!-- end prop-13 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
Recall that $f: \operatorname{PMod} \to \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U)$ is an isomorphism over $\operatorname{J}^0(X/U) \subset \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U)$, with inverse given by
    $$\mathscr L \in \operatorname{J}^0(X_u) \mapsto (\nu_u^* \mathscr L, \textrm{coker}(\mathscr L \hookrightarrow \nu_{u*} \nu_u^* \mathscr L)) \in \operatorname{PMod}_u.$$
    Since $f^{-1}(\operatorname{J}^0(X/U))$ is dense in $\operatorname{PMod}$ and $p,f$ are proper, we see that the image of $(f,p)$ is the closure of $(f,p)(f^{-1}(\operatorname{J}^0(X/U)) = \Gamma_{\nu^*}$. It follows from \cite[Lemma 3.7(3)]{FHHO} that $(f,p)$ is injective on points. Then since $\overline{\Gamma}_{\nu^*}$ is smooth \cite[Lemma A.3.1]{Yun}, it follows from Zariski's main theorem that $(f,p): \operatorname{PMod} \to \overline{\Gamma}_{\nu^*}$ is an isomorphism. The same argument holds for $(f_P, p_P)$.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- prop-14: body_md -->
\label{prop: smooth and singular Poincare}
    With the definitions of this section, and letting $q_1$ be the projection onto the first factor of $\operatorname{PMod}_P \times_U [\operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)/\operatorname{J}^0(C)]$, there is an isomorphism
    $$(1 \times a_P)^* \mathcal P^{-1} \cong (f_P \times 1)_*(q_1^*(\omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_P} \otimes \mathcal V_P^\vee) \otimes (p_P \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}^{-1})[k]$$
    of $h$-shifted sheaves on $\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U) \times_U [\operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)/\operatorname{J}^0(C)]$.
<!-- end prop-14 -->
<!-- rmk-17: body_md -->
The Grothendieck dual of a very similar identity (over a trivial base $U$) is proved in \cite[Propositions 5.16-7]{FHHO}. However, there the $\Gamma$-equivariant structure of the Poincar\'e sheaf on $\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X_u) \times \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X_u)$ is defined in order to make the equality hold. In particular, it is not a priori clear that the resulting sheaf is $\mathcal P$ as defined in Proposition \ref{prop: GS} rather than, say, a tensor product of $\mathcal P$ with the pullback of a nontrivial line bundle from $B\Gamma$.
<!-- end rmk-17 -->
<!-- lem-19: body_md -->
\label{lem: FHHO}
    With notation and definitions as before, for any $u \in U$ there is an isomorphism
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: lem FHHO}
      (1 \times a_u)^* \mathcal P_{J_u/J_u} \cong (f_u \times 1)_*(q_1^* \mathcal V_u \otimes (p_u \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}_{J_u/J_u})  
    \end{equation}
    of sheaves on $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_u) \times \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X_u)$. Moreover, the right and left side of the equation do not change if all functors are taken to be derived.
<!-- end lem-19 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
The first part is \cite[Theorem 5.3]{FHHO}. For the second part, on the right side of the equation, since $\mathcal V_u$ and $\tilde{\mathcal P}_{J_u/J_u}$ are line bundles, it suffices to note that $R(f_u \times 1)_* = (f_u \times 1)_*$ since $f_u \times 1$ is finite. On the left side of the equation, recall from \cite[Theorem A(2)]{Arinkin} that $\mathcal P_{J_u/J_u}$ is flat over the second factor $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_u)$, and so $L(1 \times a_u)^* = (1 \times a_u)^*$ by \cite[Tag 0C0V]{stacks-project}.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- lem-20: body_md -->
\label{lem: FHHO families to point}
    Consider sheaves
    $$\mathcal F := (1 \times a)^* \mathcal P_{J/J}$$
    $$\mathcal G := (f \times 1)_*(q_1^* \mathcal V \otimes (p \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}_{J/J})$$
    on $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U) \times_U \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)$.
    For each $u \in U$, let $\iota_u: \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_u) \times \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X_u) \hookrightarrow \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U) \times_U \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)$ be the inclusion. Then $\iota_u^*\mathcal F, \iota_u^*\mathcal G$ are isomorphic to the sheaves of Lemma \ref{lem: FHHO}.
<!-- end lem-20 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
The statement for $\mathcal F$ is clear once we recall from \cite{Arinkin} that $\iota_u^* \mathcal P_{J/J} = \mathcal P_{J_u/J_u}$. (From the description of each in terms of pushforward of determinant of cohomology it is clear that they agree on $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0 \times \operatorname{J}^0 \cup \operatorname{J}^0 \times \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0$, i.e., away from codimension 2. Recall that $\mathcal P_{J/J}$ and $\mathcal P_{J_u/J_u}$ are maximal Cohen-Macaulay; by \cite[Lemma 2.3]{Arinkin} the same is true of $\iota_u^* \mathcal P_{J/J}$, and thus this agrees with $\mathcal P_{J_u/J_u}$ by \cite[Lemma 2.2]{Arinkin}.)
    
    As for $\mathcal G$, we start by noting that $L\iota_u^* (f \times 1)_* = (f_{u} \times 1)_* L\iota_u^*$ by Lemma \ref{lem: Tor indep}(b) and finiteness of $f$. Thus
    $$\iota_u^* \mathcal G = \mathcal H^0((f \times 1)_* L\iota_u^*(q_1^* \mathcal V \otimes (p \times 1)^*\tilde{\mathcal P}_{J/J}))$$
    $$=\mathcal H^0((f \times 1)_*(q_1^* \mathcal V_u \otimes (p_{u} \times 1)^* \iota_u^*\tilde{\mathcal P}_{J/J}))$$
    since $L\iota_u^* = \iota_u^*$ on a line bundle. Finally, we note that the $\mathcal H^0$ is superfluous, and that $\iota_u^* \tilde{\mathcal P}_{J/J} = \tilde{\mathcal P}_{J_u/J_u}$.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- lem-21: body_md -->
\label{lem: FHHO relative J iso}
    We have $\mathcal F \cong \mathcal G$ for the sheaves $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$ on $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U) \times_U \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)$ of Lemma \ref{lem: FHHO families to point}.
<!-- end lem-21 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
Our first goal is to show that $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$ are relatively Gieseker stable (for any polarization) in the sense of \cite[\S 1]{Simpson-reps1}, i.e., flat over $U$ with $\iota_u^* \mathcal F \cong \iota_u^* \mathcal G$ Gieseker stable for each $u \in U$. Since $\mathcal P_{J/J}$ is flat over each factor \cite[Theorem A(2)]{Arinkin}, we see that $\mathcal F = (1 \times a)^* \mathcal P_{J/J}$ is flat over the second factor $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U)$, thus over $U$. As for $\mathcal G$, we note that $q_1^* \mathcal V \otimes (p \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}_{J/J}$ is a line bundle over $\operatorname{PMod}$, which is flat over $U$. Then since $(f_P \times 1)$ is finite (thus affine), the pushforward $\mathcal G$ remains flat over $U$. Finally, since by Lemma \ref{lem: FHHO families to point} the fiber $\iota_u^* \mathcal F \cong \iota_u^* \mathcal G$ is isomorphic to the right side of (\ref{eq: lem FHHO}), we see that this must be torsion-free (being the pushforward of a line bundle from an integral variety) of rank 1. Thus this is Gieseker stable for any polarization.

    Thus, choosing any relatively ample line bundle $H$ on $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U) \times_U \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U) \to U$, both $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$ give rise to morphisms $\phi_{\mathcal F}, \phi_{\mathcal G}: U \to M$, where $M$ is the coarse moduli space of relatively Gieseker semistable sheaves on $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U) \times_U \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U)$ with Hilbert polynomial matching that of $\iota_u^* \mathcal F \cong \iota_u^* \mathcal G$ constructed, as constructed in \cite[Theorem 1.21]{Simpson-reps1}. Importantly, $M$ is projective \cite[Theorem 1.21(2)]{Simpson-reps1}, thus separated; then $\phi_{\mathcal F}$ and $\phi_{\mathcal G}$ agree on some closed subscheme on $U$ \cite[Tag 01KM]{stacks-project}, which contains every closed point (Lemma \ref{lem: FHHO families to point}), and thus must be all of $U$, since $U$ is reduced. Furthermore, since $\phi_{\mathcal F} = \phi_{\mathcal G}$ lands in the open locus $M^s \subset M$ of relatively stable sheaves, by \cite[Theorem 1.21(4)]{Simpson-reps1} we see that there is an \'etale cover $a: U' \to U$ such that $a^* \mathcal F \cong a^* \mathcal G$. We conclude that $\pi_{U'*} \mathcal Hom(a^* \mathcal F, a^* \mathcal G) \cong \mathscr O_{U'}$ \cite[Lemma 4.6.3]{Huybrechts-Lehn} and the evaluation map
    \begin{equation*}
        a^* \mathcal F \otimes \pi_{U'}^* \pi_{U'*} \mathcal Hom(a^* \mathcal F, a^* \mathcal G) \to a^* \mathcal F \otimes \mathcal Hom(a^* \mathcal F, a^* \mathcal G) \to a^* \mathcal G
    \end{equation*}
    is an isomorphism. These properties descend to $U$, once we note the following: since $a^* = La^*$ we have
    $$\mathcal Hom(a^* \mathcal F, a^* \mathcal G) = \mathcal Hom_{U'}(La^* \mathcal F, La^* \mathcal G) = \mathcal H^0(R\mathcal Hom(La^* \mathcal F, La^* \mathcal G))$$
    $$= \mathcal H^0(La^*R\mathcal Hom(\mathcal F, \mathcal G)) = a^* \mathcal Hom(\mathcal F, \mathcal G)$$
    and so
    $$\pi_{U'*}\mathcal Hom(a^* \mathcal F, a^* \mathcal G) = \pi_{U'*} a^* \mathcal Hom(\mathcal F, \mathcal G) = a^* \pi_{U*} \mathcal Hom(\mathcal F, \mathcal G)$$
    with the last equality following from applying $\mathcal H^0$ to \cite[Tag 08IB]{stacks-project}. Thus, we conclude that $\pi_{U*} \mathcal Hom(\mathcal F, \mathcal G)$ is a line bundle and that there is an isomorphism
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: stable ev}
        \mathcal F \otimes \pi_U^* \pi_{U*} \mathcal Hom(\mathcal F, \mathcal G) \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathcal G.
    \end{equation}
    
    Finally, to identify the line bundle $\pi_U^* \pi_{U*} \mathcal Hom(\mathcal F, \mathcal G)$, we pull back along the section
    $$t: U \to \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U) \times_U \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U), u \mapsto (\mathscr O_{X_u}, \mathscr O_{\tilde X_u}).$$
    Note that $\mathcal P_{J/J}$ is trivial along $\{\mathscr O_{X_u}\} \times_U \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U)$, so that we have
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: FHHO equality F}
    t^*(\mathcal F \otimes \pi_U^* \pi_{U*} \mathcal Hom(\mathcal F, \mathcal G)) = t^* \mathcal F \otimes \pi_{U*} \mathcal Hom(\mathcal F, \mathcal G) \cong  \pi_{U*} \mathcal Hom(\mathcal F, \mathcal G).  
    \end{equation}
    On the other hand, recall that $f$ is an isomorphism over $\operatorname{J}^0(X/U)$, and thus
    $$t^* \mathcal G = t^*(q_1^* \mathcal V \otimes (p \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}_{J/J}).$$
    Now, recall that $\tilde{\mathcal P}_{J/J}$ is trivial along $\operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U) \times_U \{\mathscr O_{\tilde X_u}\}$, and so $t^*(p \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}_{J/J}$ is trivial. For the same reason, we also have ${\mathbb{P}}_i|_{\mathscr O_{\tilde X_u}} \cong {\mathbb{P}}^1 \times U$ (see Definition \ref{def: PMod}) and the composition of $t$ with projection $U \xrightarrow{q_1 \circ t} \operatorname{PMod} \to {\mathbb{P}}_i$ is given by $u \mapsto ([1:1], u)$, so that the pullback of $\mathscr O_{{\mathbb{P}}_i}(-1)$, thus also $t^* q_1^* \mathcal V$, is trivial.
    We conclude that $t^* \mathcal G \cong \mathscr O_U$. Combining this with (\ref{eq: stable ev}) and (\ref{eq: FHHO equality F}), we see that $\pi_{U*} \mathcal Hom(\mathcal F, \mathcal G) = \mathscr O_U$ and $\mathcal F \cong \mathcal G$.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- lem-22: body_md -->
We have an isomorphism
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: FHHO pre descent}
    (1 \times a)^* \mathcal Hom(\mathcal P_{P/J}, \mathscr O_{\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}} \times \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0}) \cong (f_P \times 1)_*(q_1^* (\omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_P/U} \otimes \mathcal V^\vee_P) \otimes (p_P \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}_{P/J}^\vee)
    \end{equation}
    of sheaves on $\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U) \times_U \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)$, where both sides are unchanged if any subset of the functors is taken to be derived.
<!-- end lem-22 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
We start by applying $(i \times 1)^*$ to the isomorphism $\mathcal F \cong \mathcal G$ of Lemma \ref{lem: FHHO relative J iso}. Noting that $i$ and the corresponding map $i_{\operatorname{PMod}}: \operatorname{PMod}_P \hookrightarrow \operatorname{PMod}$ (a flat base change of $\tilde i$) are both flat base changes of $\{\mathscr O_C\} \hookrightarrow \operatorname{J}^0(C)$ (see Remark \ref{rmk: i is reg}), we have $L(i \times 1)^* R(f \times 1)_* = R(f_P \times 1)_* L(i_{\operatorname{PMod}} \times 1)^*$ by Lemma \ref{lem: Tor indep}(b), where as usual, since $f, f_P$ are finite the derived pushforwards are underived. Thus
    $$(i \times 1)^* \mathcal G = \mathcal H^0(L(i \times 1)^* (f \times 1)_*(q_1^* \mathcal V \otimes (p \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}_{J/J})$$
    $$ = \mathcal H^0((f_P \times 1)_* L(i_{\operatorname{PMod}} \times 1)^*(q_1^* \mathcal V \otimes (p \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}_{J/J})) = (f_P \times 1)_* (q_1^* \mathcal V_P \otimes (p_P \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}_{P/J})$$
    where in the last equality we use that derived and underived pullback of a line bundle agree. So from Lemma \ref{lem: FHHO relative J iso} we get
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: FHHO restriction}
      (f_P \times 1)_* (q_1^* \mathcal V_P \otimes (p_P \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}_{P/J}) = (i \times 1)^* \mathcal G = (i \times 1)^* \mathcal F = (1 \times a)^* \mathcal P_{P/J}.  
    \end{equation}
    The needed identity will follow by taking the dual $R\mathcal Hom(-, \omega_{\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}} \times_U \operatorname{J}^0}^\bullet)$ of each side of \ref{eq: FHHO restriction}) and tensoring by $\pi_U^* \omega_U^\vee[-e]$ for $e := \dim \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U) \times_U \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)$.

    On the left side, note that
    $$R\mathcal Hom((i \times 1)^* \mathcal G, \omega_{\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}} \times \operatorname{J}^0}^\bullet) = R\mathcal Hom(R(f_P \times 1)_*(q_1^* \mathcal V_P \otimes (p_P \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}_{P/J}), \omega_{\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}} \times_U \operatorname{J}^0}^\bullet)$$
    $$ = R(f_P \times 1)_* R\mathcal Hom(q_1^* \mathcal V_P \otimes (p_P \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}_{P/J}, \omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_P \times_U \operatorname{J}^0}^\bullet)$$
    by Grothendieck duality
    $$ = R(f_P \times 1)_* (q_1^* \mathcal V^\vee_P \otimes R\mathcal Hom((p_P \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}_{P/J}, \mathscr O_{\operatorname{PMod}_P \times \operatorname{J}^0}) \otimes \omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_P \times_U \operatorname{J}^0}[e])$$
    since $\operatorname{PMod}_P \times_U \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)$ is smooth
    $$=R(f_P \times 1)_* (q_1^* \mathcal V^\vee_P \otimes (p_P \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}_{P/J}^\vee \otimes \omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_P \times_U \operatorname{J}^0}[e])$$
    $$=R(f_P \times 1)_* (q_1^*(\omega_{\operatorname{PMod}/U} \otimes \mathcal V^\vee_P) \otimes (p_P \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}_{P/J}^\vee) \otimes \pi_U^* \omega_U[e]$$
    using the projection formula and the fact that $\omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_P \times_U \operatorname{J}^0} \cong q_1^*\omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_P/U} \otimes \pi_U^* \omega_U \otimes q_2^* \omega_{\operatorname{J}^0/U}$, where the third term is trivial by assumption on $U$
    $$=(f_P \times 1)_* (q_1^*(\omega_{\operatorname{PMod}/U} \otimes \mathcal V^\vee_P) \otimes (p_P \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}_{P/J}^\vee) \otimes \pi_U^* \omega_U[e]$$
    since $f_P$ is finite.

    On the right side, we have
    $$R\mathcal Hom((1 \times a)^* \mathcal P_{P/J}, \omega^\bullet_{\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}} \times_U \operatorname{J}^0}) = R\mathcal Hom((1 \times a)^* \mathcal P_{P/J}, \mathscr O) \otimes \omega_{\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}} \times_U \operatorname{J}^0}[e]$$
    since $\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U) \times_U \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)$ is Gorenstein (Lemma \ref{lem: oPrym is flat})
    $$ =  R\mathcal Hom(L(1 \times a)^* \mathcal P_{P/J}, \mathscr O) \otimes \omega_{\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}} \times_U \operatorname{J}^0}[e]$$
    by \cite[Tag 0C0V]{stacks-project}, since $\mathcal P_{P/J}$ and $\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U) \times_U \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)$ are flat over the second factor by \cite[Lemma 4.3(b)]{GS} and Lemma \ref{lem: oPrym is flat}, respectively
    $$ = L(1 \times a)^* R\mathcal Hom(\mathcal P_{P/J}, \mathscr O) \otimes \omega_{\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}} \times_U \operatorname{J}^0}[e]$$
    $$ = L(1 \times a)^* R\mathcal Hom(\mathcal P_{P/J}, \mathscr O) \otimes \pi_U^*\omega_U[e]$$
    since by assumption $\omega_{\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}/U}$ and $ \omega_{\operatorname{J}^0/U}$ are both trivial (see Lemma \ref{lem: oPrym is flat})
    $$ = L(1 \times a)^* \mathcal Hom(\mathcal P_{P/J}, \mathscr O) \otimes \pi_U^*\omega_U[e]$$
    since $\mathcal P_{P/J}$ is maximal Cohen-Macaulay by \cite[Lemma 2.3(b)]{Arinkin}
    $$ = (1 \times a)^* \mathcal Hom(\mathcal P_{P/J}, \mathscr O) \otimes \pi_U^*\omega_U[e]$$
    because by the previous paragraph, the result of applying the duality functor to (\ref{eq: FHHO restriction}) is an $e$-shifted sheaf.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
Let $\tilde \varpi$, respectively $\varpi$, represent all base changes of the $\operatorname{J}^0(C)$-quotient map $\operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U) \to [\operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)/\operatorname{J}^0(C)]$, respectively $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U) \to [\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U)/\operatorname{J}^0(C)]$. We note that 
    $$\tilde \varpi^* (1 \times a_P)^* \mathcal P^{-1} := \tilde \varpi^* (1 \times a_P)^* R\mathcal Hom(\mathcal P^T, \mathscr O)[h] = (1 \times a)^* \varpi^* R\mathcal Hom(\mathcal P^T, \mathscr O)[h]$$
    $$=(1 \times a)^* R\mathcal Hom(\varpi^*\mathcal P^T, \mathscr O)[h]$$
    since $\varpi$ is flat
    $$=(1 \times a)^* R\mathcal Hom(\mathcal P_{P/J}, \mathscr O)[h]$$
