    by definition of $\mathcal P$, so that we recover the left side of (\ref{eq: FHHO pre descent}), shifted by $h$. Similarly,
    $$\tilde \varpi^*(f_P \times 1)_*(q_1^*(\omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_P} \otimes \mathcal V_P^\vee) \otimes (p_P \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}^{-1})$$
    $$:= \tilde \varpi^*(f_P \times 1)_*(q_1^*(\omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_P} \otimes \mathcal V_P^\vee) \otimes (p_P \times 1)^* (\tilde{\mathcal P}^T)^\vee)[h-k]$$
    $$= (f_P \times 1)_*\tilde{\varpi}^*(q_1^*(\omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_P} \otimes \mathcal V_P^\vee) \otimes (p_P \times 1)^* (\tilde{\mathcal P}^T)^\vee)[h-k]$$
    because $\varpi$ is flat and $f_P$ finite
    $$=(f_P \times 1)_*(q_1^*(\omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_P} \otimes \mathcal V_P^\vee) \otimes (p_P \times 1)^* (\tilde{\varpi}^*\tilde{\mathcal P}^T)^\vee)[h-k]$$
    $$=(f_P \times 1)_*(q_1^*(\omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_P} \otimes \mathcal V_P^\vee) \otimes (p_P \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}_{P/J}^\vee)[h-k],$$
    matching the (shifted) right side of (\ref{eq: FHHO pre descent}). Thus, it suffices to check that there is at most one way to descend the sheaf (\ref{eq: FHHO pre descent}) to $\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U) \times_U [\operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)/\operatorname{J}^0(C)]$.

    To ease notation, write
    $$\mathscr L := q_1^*(\omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_P/U} \otimes \mathcal V^\vee_P) \otimes (p_P \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}_{P/J}^\vee \in \mathop{\rm Pic}\nolimits(\operatorname{PMod} \times_U \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)).$$ Consider the sheaf $\mathcal End(p_{23}^*(f_P \times 1)_* \mathscr L)$ on $\operatorname{J}^0(C) \times \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U) \times_U \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)$. As usual, since $p_{23}$ is flat, we have $p_{23}^* (f_P \times 1)_* \mathscr L = (1 \times f_P \times 1)_* p_{23}^* \mathscr L$. Now, since $(1 \times f_P \times 1)$ is finite, therefore in particular affine, note that the adjunction
    $$(1 \times f_P \times 1)^*(1 \times f_P \times 1)_* p_{23}^* \mathscr L \to p_{23}^* \mathscr L$$
    is surjective; moreover, the kernel is torsion since $(1 \times f_P \times 1)$ is an isomorphism over a dense open subset. Since $p_{23}^* \mathscr L$ is a line bundle and thus torsion-free, we conclude that the map
    $$\mathcal Hom(p_{23}^* \mathscr L, p_{23}^* \mathscr L) \to \mathcal Hom((1 \times f_P \times 1)^*(1 \times f_P \times 1)_* p_{23}^* \mathscr L, p_{23}^* \mathscr L)$$
    is an isomorphism, and so
    $$\mathcal End(p_{23}^* (f_P \times 1)_* \mathscr L) = \mathcal Hom((1 \times f_P \times 1)_* p_{23}^* \mathscr L, (1 \times f_P \times 1)_* p_{23}^* \mathscr L)$$
    $$= (1 \times f_P \times 1)_* \mathcal Hom((1 \times f_P \times 1)^*(1 \times f_P \times 1)_* p_{23}^* \mathscr L, p_{23}^* \mathscr L)$$
    $$= (1 \times f_P \times 1)_* \mathcal Hom(p_{23}^* \mathscr L, p_{23}^* \mathscr L) = (1 \times f_P \times 1)_* \mathscr O_{\operatorname{J} \times \operatorname{PMod}_P \times_U \operatorname{J}}.$$
    Taking global sections, we see that
    $$\mathrm{End}(p_{23}^*(f_P \times 1)_* \mathscr L) = H^0(\operatorname{J}^0(C) \times \operatorname{PMod}_P \times_U \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U), \mathscr O) = H^0(\operatorname{PMod}_P \times_U \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U), \mathscr O)$$
    and in particular, an isomorphism of $p_{23}^*(f_P \times 1)_* \mathscr L$ is uniquely determined by its value on $\{\mathscr O_C\} \times \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U) \times_U \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)$. Since a $\operatorname{J}^0(C)$-equivariant structure on the sheaf (\ref{eq: FHHO pre descent}) is given by an isomorphism of sheaves $p_{23}^* (f_P \times 1)_* \mathscr L$ and $\sigma^* (f_P \times 1)_* \mathscr L$ (where $\sigma$ is the action map) satisfying the cocycle condition, which implies in particular that the isomorphism $(p_{23}^*(f_P \times 1)_* \mathscr L)|_{\{\mathscr O_C\}} \cong (\sigma^*(f_P \times 1)_* \mathscr L)|_{\{\mathscr O_C\}}$ is given by the identification of each side with $(f_P \times 1)_* \mathscr L$ under pullback, we conclude that a $\operatorname{J}^0(C)$-equivariant structure must be unique.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- prop-15: body_md -->
\label{prop: GS descent}
    The restriction of the Poincar\'e sheaf $\mathcal P_{J/J}$ to $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B) \times_B \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B)$ descends uniquely to $[\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B)/\operatorname{J}^0(C)] \times_B \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B)$.
<!-- end prop-15 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
First, for each $L \in \operatorname{J}^0(C)$, acting on the first factor of $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B) \times_B \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B)$ by tensor product with the pullback (call this action $\sigma$), we have $\sigma(L,-)^* \mathcal P_{J/J} \cong \mathcal P_{J/J} \otimes p_2^*(\mathcal P_{J/J}|_{\{c^*L\} \times J})$ by \cite[Lemma 6.5]{Arinkin}. We note that $\mathcal P_{J/J}|_{\{c^*L\} \times \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}}$ is trivial, by \cite[Proposition 4.4]{GS} applied to $\mathcal M = p_{13}^* \mathcal L$ and $\mathcal N = \mathscr O_{X \times \operatorname{\overline{J}} \times \operatorname{\overline{J}}}$, since after restricting to $X \times_B \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B) \times_B \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B)$ one has $\det c_*(\mathcal M) \cong \det c_*(\mathcal N)$ by definition of $\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}$. Thus the pullbacks of $\mathcal P_{J/J}|_{\operatorname{\overline{J}} \times \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}} =: \mathcal P_{J/P}$ under the action $\sigma$ and projection $p_{23}:  \operatorname{J}^0(C) \times \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B) \times_B \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B) \to \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B) \times_B \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B)$ are isomorphic over each point $L \in \operatorname{J}^0(C)$.

    Now, consider the projection $p_{13}: \operatorname{J}^0(C) \times \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B) \times_B \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B) \to \operatorname{J}^0(C) \times \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B)$. We note that $\sigma^* \mathcal P_{J/P}, p_{23}^* \mathcal P_{J/P}$ are relatively flat with respect to $p_{13}$ since $\mathcal P_{J/J}$ is flat over each factor. Moreover, for each $x \in \operatorname{J}^0(C) \times \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B)$, the fibers $\sigma^* \mathcal P_{J/P}|_x \cong p_{23}^* \mathcal P_{J/P}|_x$ are torsion-free (because maximal Cohen-Macaulay \cite[Theorem A(2)]{Arinkin}) of rank 1 on the irreducible variety $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_{\pi(x)})$ \cite[Theorem 9]{AIK}, thus stable with respect to any polarization. The argument in the proof of Lemma \ref{lem: FHHO relative J iso} then implies that $\sigma^* \mathcal P_{J/P}$ and $p_{23}^* \mathcal P_{J/P}$ differ by the line bundle $p_{13}^* p_{13*} \mathcal Hom(\sigma^* \mathcal P_{J/P}, p_{23}^* \mathcal P_{J/P})$.

    To identify this line bundle, we pull back along the section $t$ of $p_{13}$ given by the section $B \to \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B), b \mapsto \{\mathscr O_{X_b}\}$. Since this is a section of $\operatorname{J}^0(X/B) \subset \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B)$, we note that $t^* \sigma^* \mathcal P_{J/P}$ and $t^*p_{23}^* \mathcal P_{J/P} = p_2^*\mathcal P_{J/P}|_{\{\mathscr O\} \times P} \cong \mathscr O_{\operatorname{J}^0(C) \times \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}}$ are line bundles, computable by the determinant of cohomology formula \cite[(1.1)]{Arinkin}. In order to calculate $t^* \sigma^* \mathcal P_{J/P}$, we use \cite[Proposition 1.5]{Huishi}, whose proof also holds when $X \to C \times B$ is a flat finite map but not an \'etale double cover (although in general one must replace $\mathcal D_{q_{23}}(q_{12}^* K|_{D_Y})$ by $\mathcal D_{q_{23}}(q_{12}^* K|_{D_Y})^{\otimes (n-1)}$, where $n$ is the degree). Applying this over the base $\operatorname{J}^0(C) \times \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B)$ with $K$ on $C \times \operatorname{J}^0(C) \times \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B)$ pulled back from a universal bundle on $C \times \operatorname{J}^0(C)$, $\mathcal M$ pulled back from a universal bundle on $X \times_B \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B)$, and $\mathcal N$ trivial, since $\det c_*(\mathcal M) \cong \det c_*(\mathcal N)$, we conclude that $t^*\sigma^*\mathcal P_{J/P} = \mathcal P|_{\operatorname{J}^0(C) \times \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}}$ is trivial. In other words, since the line bundles $t^* \sigma^* \mathcal P_{J/P} \cong t^*p_{23}^* \mathcal P_{J/P}$ differ by the line bundle $t^* p_{13}^* p_{13*} \mathcal Hom(\sigma^* \mathcal P_{J/P}, p_{23}^* \mathcal P_{J/P}) = p_{13*}\mathcal Hom(\sigma^* \mathcal P_{J/P}, p_{23}^* \mathcal P_{J/P})$, we conclude that this is trivial, hence in fact $\sigma^* \mathcal P_{J/P} \cong p_{23}^* \mathcal P_{J/P}$.

    Now we are ready to define the equivariant structure on $\mathcal P_{J/P}$. Since from the previous paragraph we have $p_{13*} \mathcal Hom(\sigma^* \mathcal P_{J/P}, p_{23}^* \mathcal P_{J/P}) \cong \mathscr O_{\operatorname{J} \times \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}}$, in particular
    $$\operatorname{Hom}(\sigma^* \mathcal P_{J/P}, p_{23}^* \mathcal P_{J/P}) \cong H^0(\operatorname{J}^0(C) \times \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B), \mathscr O) = H^0(\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B), \mathscr O)$$
    and so a morphism is uniquely determined by its value on the section $s: \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B) \to \operatorname{J}^0(C) \times \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B) \times_B \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B)$ given by $\{\mathscr O_C\} \times \{\mathscr O_{X_b}\} \times_B \textrm{id}$. Let $\phi: \sigma^* \mathcal P_{J/P} \to p_{23}^* \mathcal P_{J/P}$ be the unique morphism restricting to the identity on
    $$s^* \sigma^* \mathcal P_{J/P} = s^* p_{23}^* \mathcal P_{J/P} = \mathcal P_{J/P}|_{\mathscr O \times P} \cong \mathscr O_{\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}},$$
    as required by the cocycle condition. Note that $\phi$ is an isomorphism, as it does not have zeroes on $s$.

    Finally, we claim that $\phi$ must satisfy the cocycle condition, i.e., equality of the two isomorphisms $(m \times 1)^* \phi$ and $p_{234}^* \phi \circ (1 \times \sigma)^* \phi$ on the sheaf isomorphic to $p_{34}^* \mathcal P_{P/J}$ for the projection $p_{34}: \operatorname{J}^0(C) \times \operatorname{J}^0(C) \times \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B) \times_B \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B): \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B) \times_B \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B)$. Indeed, repeating the argument above, we see that
    $$\mathrm{End}(p_{34}^* \mathcal P_{P/J}) \cong H^0(\operatorname{J}^0(C) \times \operatorname{J}^0(C) \times \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B), \mathscr O) = H^0(\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B), \mathscr O)$$
    and so it suffices that the two isomorphisms agree on the section $\{\mathscr O_C\} \times \{\mathscr O_C\} \times \{\mathscr O_{X_b}\} \times_B \textrm{id}$, which is true by choice of $\phi$.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- lem-23: body_md -->
\label{lem: theorem of square}
    Write $M^\circ := \operatorname{Prym}(X/B) \subset M$, and let $\mu: M \times_B M^\circ \to M$ be the multiplication map. Then
    $$(1 \times \mu)^* \mathcal P = p_{12}^* \mathcal P \otimes p_{13}^* \mathcal P|_{M^\vee \times_B M^\circ} \in \mathrm{Coh}(M^\vee \times_B M \times_B M^\circ).$$
<!-- end lem-23 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
Writing $\mathcal P_{J/J}$ for the Arinkin Poincar\'e sheaf on $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B) \times_B \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B)$, the corresponding identity holds on $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B) \times_B \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B) \times_B \operatorname{J}^0(X/B)$ by \cite[Lemma 6.5]{Arinkin}. Restricting to $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B) \times_B \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B) \times_B \operatorname{Prym}(X/B)$, we obtain an identity
    $$(1 \times \mu)^* \mathcal P_{J/M} = p_{12}^* \mathcal P_{J/M} \otimes p_{13}^* \mathcal P_{J/M^\circ} \in \mathrm{Coh}(\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B) \times_B M \times_B M^\circ)$$
    (noting that $\mathcal P_{J/J^\circ}$ is a line bundle). As in the proof of Proposition \ref{prop: GS descent}, we note that this sheaf descends uniquely to $M^\vee \times_B M \times_B M^\circ$ and thus that the two possible descents $(1 \times \mu)^* \mathcal P$ and $p_{12}^* \mathcal P \otimes p_{13}^* \mathcal P|_{M^\vee \times_B M^\circ}$ are isomorphic.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- prop-16: body_md -->
\label{prop: Ggamma in the kappa cpt}
    For any $\gamma \in \Gamma$, we have
    $$cl(\mathfrak G_\gamma) \in H_*^{BM}(M^{\gamma, \vee} \times_B M)_\kappa, \,\,\, cl(\mathfrak G_\gamma^{-1}) \in H^{BM}_*(M \times_B M^{\gamma, \vee})_{\kappa^{-1}},$$
    where $\Gamma$ acts on $M^{\gamma, \vee} \times_B M$,  respectively $M \times_B M^{\gamma, \vee}$, via its action on $M$.
<!-- end prop-16 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
For any $\beta \in \Gamma$, let $\sigma_\beta: M \to M$ be the action map. By Lemma \ref{lem: theorem of square} we have
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: pullback of P}
        \sigma_\beta^* \mathcal P = \mathcal P \otimes p_1^*\mathcal P|_{M^\vee \times \{\beta\}}, \,\,\, \sigma_\beta^* \mathcal P^{-1} = \mathcal P^{-1} \otimes p_2^*\mathcal P|_{M^\vee \times \{\beta\}}^\vee
    \end{equation}
    and thus
    $$\beta \cdot cl(\mathfrak G_\gamma) = cl(\operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}(p_1^*\mathcal P|_{M^\vee \times \{\beta\}})_\gamma \cap \mathfrak G_\gamma), \,\,\, \beta \cdot cl(\mathfrak G_\gamma^{-1}) = cl(\operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}(p_2^*\mathcal P|_{M^\vee \times \{\beta\}}^\vee)_\gamma \cap \mathfrak G_\gamma^{-1}).$$
    Since $\mathcal P|_{M^\vee \times \beta} \in \mathop{\rm Pic}\nolimits(M^\vee)$ is a line bundle, the decomposition into $\gamma$-eigensheaves is trivial, and by Corollary \ref{cor: eigenvalue of P} and Proposition \ref{prop: smooth and singular Poincare} (applied, say, over a single point $b \in B_\gamma$), we see that the eigenvalue of $\gamma$ is $\kappa(\beta)$. As in the proof of Lemma \ref{lem: Palpha top trivial}, we see that $\mathcal P_{M^\vee \times \{\beta\}}$ is topologically trivial, and thus
    $$\beta \cdot cl(\mathfrak G_\gamma) = \operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}^{top}(p_1^*\mathcal P|_{M^\vee \times \{\beta\}})_\gamma \cap cl(\mathfrak G_\gamma) = \kappa(\beta) \cdot cl(\mathfrak G_\gamma), \,\,\, \beta \cdot cl(\mathfrak G_\gamma^{-1}) = \kappa(\beta)^{-1} \cdot cl(\mathfrak G_\gamma^{-1}).$$
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- cor-6: body_md -->
\label{cor: Ggamma triv on other pieces}
    Under the homological realization isomorphism (\ref{eq: BM = sheaf Hom}) the morphism
    $$cl(\mathfrak G_{\gamma, i}) \in \operatorname{Hom}_B(\pi_* {\mathbb{C}}_{M^{\gamma, \vee}}, \pi_* {\mathbb{C}}_M[2(i-h_\gamma)])$$
    factors through the (shifted) inclusion $(\pi_* {\mathbb{C}}_M)_\kappa \subset \pi_* {\mathbb{C}}_M$, and
    $$cl(\mathfrak G_{\gamma, i}^{-1}) \in \operatorname{Hom}_B(\pi_* {\mathbb{C}}_M,\pi_* {\mathbb{C}}_{M^{\gamma, \vee}}[2(i-2h+h_\gamma)])$$
    factors through the projection $\pi_* {\mathbb{C}}_M \twoheadrightarrow (\pi_* {\mathbb{C}}_M)_\kappa$.
<!-- end cor-6 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
It follows from Proposition \ref{prop: Ggamma in the kappa cpt} that each degree component $\mathfrak G_{\gamma,i}$, respectively $\mathfrak G_{\gamma,i}^{-1}$, is in the $\kappa$, respectively $\kappa^{-1}$, component of the relevant $H^{BM}_*$. Since $\Gamma$ acts trivially on $\pi_* {\mathbb{C}}_{M^{\gamma, \vee}}$, note that a $\kappa$-component morphism must have image in $(\pi_* {\mathbb{C}}_M[*])_\kappa$ (for $\mathfrak G_{\gamma, i}$), and in the opposite direction, the image of a $\kappa'$-component subsheaf by a $\kappa^{-1}$ morphism cannot be $\Gamma$-invariant unless $\kappa' = \kappa$ (for $\mathfrak G_{\gamma, i}^{-1}$).
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- prop-17: body_md -->
\label{prop: FV for different chars}
    For any $i,j \in {\mathbb{N}}$ and $\gamma \ne \beta \in \Gamma$, we have
    $$\mathfrak G_{\gamma,i}^{-1} \circ \mathfrak G_{\beta,j} = 0 \in \operatorname{Corr}_B^{i+j-2h}(M^{\beta, \vee}, M^{\gamma, \vee}).$$
<!-- end prop-17 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
For any $\alpha \in \Gamma$ acting on $M$ via an isomorphism $\sigma_\alpha$, we note that
    $$\mathfrak G_{\gamma,i}^{-1} \circ \mathfrak G_{\beta,j} = (\sigma_\alpha \times 1)^* \mathfrak G_{\gamma,i}^{-1} \circ (1 \times \sigma_\alpha)^* \mathfrak G_{\beta,j}.$$
    By definition and (\ref{eq: pullback of P}) we see that
    $$(1 \times \sigma_\alpha)^* \mathfrak G_\beta = \operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}(p_1^* \mathcal P|_{M^\vee \times \{\alpha\}})_\beta \cap \mathfrak G_\beta, \,\,\, (\sigma_\alpha \times 1)^* \mathfrak G_\gamma^{-1} = \operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}(p_2^* \mathcal P|^\vee_{M^\vee \times \{\alpha\}})_\gamma \cap \mathfrak G_\gamma^{-1}.$$
    In particular, splitting into degree pieces
    $$(1 \times \sigma_\alpha)^* \mathfrak G_{\beta,j} = ((1 \times \sigma_\alpha)^* \mathfrak G_{\beta})_j = \sum_{a \ge 0} \operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}^a(p_1^* \mathcal P|_{M^\vee \times \{\alpha\}})_\beta \cap \mathfrak G_{\beta, j-a}$$
    and similarly for $\mathfrak G_{\gamma,i}^{-1}$.
    Then by the projection formula for the representable morphism $p_{13}: M^{\beta, \vee} \times_B M \times_B M^{\gamma, \vee} \to M^{\beta, \vee} \times_B M^{\gamma, \vee}$ we have
    $$\mathfrak G_{\gamma,i}^{-1} \circ \mathfrak G_{\beta,j} = (\sigma_\alpha \times 1)^* \mathfrak G_{\gamma,i}^{-1} \circ (1 \times \sigma_\alpha)^* \mathfrak G_{\beta,j}$$
    $$=\sum_{a,b \ge 0} \operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}^a(p_2^* \mathcal P|^\vee_{M^\vee \times \{\alpha\}})_\gamma \cap \operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}^b(p_1^* \mathcal P|_{M^\vee \times \{\alpha\}})_\beta \cap (\mathfrak G_{\gamma, i-a}^{-1} \circ \mathfrak G_{\beta,j-b}).$$
    
    By induction, we may suppose that for all pairs $(i',j') < (i,j)$ in lexicographic order we have $\mathfrak G_{\gamma,i'}^{-1} \circ \mathfrak G_{\beta, j'} = 0$. Then
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: GV diff cpts}
        \mathfrak G_{\gamma,i}^{-1} \circ \mathfrak G_{\beta, j} = \operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}^0(p_2^* \mathcal P|^\vee_{M^\vee \times \{\alpha\}})_\gamma \cap \operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}^0(p_1^* \mathcal P|_{M^\vee \times \{\alpha\}})_\beta \cap (\mathfrak G_{\gamma, i}^{-1} \circ \mathfrak G_{\beta,j}).
    \end{equation}
    As in the proof of Proposition \ref{prop: Ggamma in the kappa cpt}, we note that
    $$\operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}^0( \mathcal P|^\vee_{M^\vee \times \{\alpha\}})_\gamma  = \langle \gamma, \alpha \rangle^{-1}, \,\,\, \operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}^0( \mathcal P|_{M^\vee \times \{\alpha\}})_\beta  = \langle \beta, \alpha \rangle.$$
    Since $\gamma \ne \beta$ and the pairing of Definition \ref{def: Weil pairing} is nondegenerate, we may choose $\alpha$ with $\langle \gamma^{-1}\beta, \alpha \rangle \ne 1$. Then (\ref{eq: GV diff cpts}) implies that $\mathfrak G_{\gamma, i}^{-1} \circ \mathfrak G_{\beta,j}=0$.
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- prop-18: body_md -->
\label{prop: U exists}
    There is an \'etale morphism $U \to B_\gamma$ which can be equipped with a family $\tilde X \to U$ normalizing $X_U \to U$ and sections $\{\sigma_i, \sigma_i^1, \sigma_i^2, s: 1 \le i \le k\}$, satisfying all the properties described at the beginning of \S \ref{subsubsec: FHHO setup}.
<!-- end prop-18 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
By Definition \ref{defn: good fibration}(3), there is a dense open subset $U' \subset B_\gamma$ over which the curves $X_{U'} \to U'$ are nodal. Restricting further if necessary, by upper semicontinuity of the $\delta$-invariant, we may assume that the number of nodes is some constant $k$. Then there exists a flat family $\tilde X_{U'} \to U'$ of normalizations \cite[Theorem 4.2]{normalization}. Restricting further if needed, we may assume that the line bundles $\det \pi_{U'*} \omega_{\tilde X/U'}, \det \pi_{U'*} \omega_{X/U'}$ are trivial. (Note that since the singularities of $X_{U'} \to U'$ are nodal, this is a family of Gorenstein curves \cite[Tag 0E37]{stacks-project}, and thus $\omega_{X'/U'}$ is a line bundle compatible with base change \cite[Tag 0E6R]{stacks-project}, and by Grauert's theorem $\pi_{U'*} \omega_{X'/U'}$ is a vector bundle.) We will take $U$ to be an \'etale cover of $U'$ (which is smooth by Definition \ref{defn: good fibration}(1)).
    
    Note that the discriminant locus $D$ of $X_{U'} \to U'$ is finite \'etale over $U'$ of order $k$; after passing to a $(k!)$-fold finite \'etale cover $U'' \to U'$, we can trivialize the cover $D \to U'$, i.e., define sections $\sigma_i$. Then $\nu^{-1}(\sigma_i)$ gives a double \'etale cover of $U''$ for each $i$, and trivializing these $k$ covers via some finite \'etale $U''' \to U''$, we obtain sections $\{\sigma_i^1, \sigma_i^2\}$. Finally, after taking an \'etale cover $U$ of $U'''$, we can define a section of the smooth morphism $\tilde X_{U'''} \setminus \cup_i (\sigma_i^1 \cup \sigma_i^2) \to U'''$.
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- prop-19: body_md -->
\label{prop: a is restriction to Mgamma}
    Let $U$ be as in Proposition \ref{prop: U exists}. The morphism $a_P: [\operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)/\operatorname{J}^0(C)] \to [\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U)/\operatorname{J}^0(C)]$ is a closed embedding whose image is the fixed locus $[\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U)^\gamma/\operatorname{J}^0(C)]$.
<!-- end prop-19 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
We start with the claim that $a_P$ (or equivalently $a: \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U) \to \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U)$) is a closed embedding. Consider the closed subvariety $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U)_{|k|} \subset \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U)$ consisting of sheaves $\mathcal F$ which fail to be locally free at each node of $X_u$. (This is the image of the closed subvariety of $\operatorname{PMod} = {\mathbb{P}}_1 \times_{\operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)} \cdots \times {\mathbb{P}}_k$ consisting of points such that the coordinate in each ${\mathbb{P}}_i$ belongs to one of the two distinguished sections of ${\mathbb{P}}_i \to \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)$.) It follows from \cite[Lemma 3.7(3-4)]{FHHO} that this is the image of $a$. Now, note that for $\mathscr L \in \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X_u)$, the adjunction map $\nu_u^* \nu_{u*} \mathscr L \to \mathscr L$ is surjective since $\nu_u$ is finite, thus affine, and the kernel is the torsion subsheaf of $\nu_u^* \nu_{u*} \mathscr L$. In particular, we can define an inverse morphism
    $$b: \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U)_{|k|} \to \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U), \mathcal F \mapsto (\nu_u^* \mathcal F/T_{\nu_u^*\mathcal F})(ks(u))$$
    where $T_{\nu_u^* \mathcal F}$ is the torsion subsheaf. (More precisely, since $a$ and $b$ are inverse on closed points, $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U)_{|k|}$ is connected over each connected component of $U$, and $\operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)$ is a smooth variety, it follows from Zariski's main theorem that $b$ is an isomorphism.)

    Now, recall from Remark \ref{rmk: endoscopic locus defs} that the image of $a$ is contained in the fixed locus $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U)^\gamma$. To show the other containment, for each subset $I \subset \{1, \ldots, k\}$, we consider the locally closed subvariety $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U)_I \subset \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U)$ consisting of sheaves which fail to be locally free exactly at the nodes $\{\sigma_i: i \in I\}$. If $\nu_I: X_{u,I} \to X_u$ is the partial normalization resolving the nodes $\{\sigma_i: i \in I\}$, then by the arguments of the previous paragraph, pushforward gives an isomorphism $\nu_{I*}: \operatorname{J}^{-\# I}(X_{u,I}) \to \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_u)_I$; in particular $\dim \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_u)_I = \dim \operatorname{J}^0(X_{u,I}) = \dim \operatorname{J}^0(X_u) - \#I$. Note that $\nu_{I*}$ is $\operatorname{J}^0(C)$-equivariant by the projection formula, and that $\gamma \in \operatorname{J}^0(C)$ acts on $\operatorname{J}^{-\# I}(X_{u,I})$ without fixed points if the pullback $\nu_I^* a_u^* \gamma \in \operatorname{J}^0(X_{u,I})$ is nontrivial, and otherwise trivially. Thus $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_u)^\gamma$ is of the form $\coprod_{I \in \mathcal S} \nu_{I*} \operatorname{J}^{-\# I}(X_{u,I})$ for some subset $\{|k|\} \subset \mathcal S \subset 2^{2^{|k|}}$.

    We now claim that smoothness of $M$ (Definition \ref{defn: good fibration}(1)) implies that $\mathcal S = \{|k|\}$. Indeed, if $I \subsetneq |k|$ were minimal such that $I \in \mathcal S$, then we note that for each $u \in U$ there would be a proper birational morphism
    $$\operatorname{PMod}_{X_{u,I}} \to \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_{u,I}) \cong \operatorname{\overline{J}}^{-\# I}(X_{u,I}) \xrightarrow{\nu_{I*}} \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_u)^\gamma$$
    onto an irreducible component of $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_u)^\gamma$ with some nontrivially disconnected fibers, and then by Zariski's main theorem $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_u)^\gamma$ would not be smooth. On the other hand, as in Remark \ref{rmk: etale cover}, smoothness of $M$ implies smoothness of $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B)$, thus of the fixed locus $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B)^\gamma$, thus of the \'etale cover $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_U/U)^\gamma$, and thus of a general fiber $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_u)^\gamma$. Thus $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_u)^\gamma = \nu_{u*} \operatorname{J}^{-k}(\tilde X_u) = a_u(\operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X_u))$.
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- cor-7: body_md -->
\label{cor: h-hgamma}
    If $M \to B$ is a good Prym fibration, we have $h-h_\gamma = b-b_\gamma$.
<!-- end cor-7 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
By Proposition \ref{prop: a is restriction to Mgamma} we have $h_\gamma = \dim \operatorname{Prym}(\tilde X_u)$ for any $u \in U$. Then
    $$h := \dim \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X_u) = \dim \operatorname{PMod}_u = \dim \operatorname{Prym}(\tilde X_u) + k = h_\gamma + k,$$
    where by definition $k = \delta(B_\gamma)$. Now recall from Remark \ref{rmk: Severi/Ngo} that $\delta(B_\gamma) = b-b_\gamma$.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- prop-20: body_md -->
\label{prop: tau B tau U}
    Let $\alpha: U \to B_\gamma$ be as in Proposition \ref{prop: U exists}. We write $\mathcal P_U^{-1}$, respectively $\mathcal P^{-1}$, for the Poincar\'e sheaves defined in Proposition \ref{prop: GS} on $\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U) \times_U [\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U)/\Gamma]$, respectively $M \times_B M^\vee$. Then
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: prop restrict}
        \alpha^! \tau(\mathcal P^{-1})_\gamma = (1 \times \alpha)^*\operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(-T_{1 \times \iota_{\gamma}})_\gamma \cap \tau((1 \times \iota_{\gamma,U})^*\mathcal P^{-1}_U)_\gamma
    \end{equation}
    in $\operatorname{CH}_*(\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U) \times_U [\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U)^\gamma/\Gamma]),$
    where $\iota_{\gamma,U}: [\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U)^\gamma/\Gamma] \hookrightarrow [\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U)/\Gamma]$ is the inclusion.
<!-- end prop-20 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
Consider the composition
    $$\phi: \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U) \times_U [\operatorname{Prym}(X/U)^\gamma/\Gamma] \xhookrightarrow{1 \times \iota_{\gamma,U}} \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U) \times_U [\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U)/\Gamma]$$
    $$= (M \times_B M^\vee) \times_B U \xrightarrow{1 \times \alpha} M \times_B M^\vee$$
    or equivalently,
    $$\phi: \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U) \times_U [\operatorname{Prym}(X/U)^\gamma/\Gamma] = (M \times_B M^{\gamma,\vee}) \times_B U \xrightarrow{1 \times \alpha} M \times_B M^{\gamma,\vee} \xhookrightarrow{1 \times \iota_\gamma} M \times_B M^\vee.$$
    We claim first that $\mathcal P_U^{-1} = L(1 \times \alpha)^* \mathcal P^{-1}$: indeed, recall that $\mathcal P_{J/J}$ is maximal Cohen-Macaulay \cite[Theorem A(2), Lemma 2.1(1)]{Arinkin}; then since $i \times i: \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B) \times_B \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/B) \hookrightarrow \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B) \times_B \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/B)$ is a flat base change of the regular embedding $\{\mathscr O_C\} \times \{\mathscr O_C\} \hookrightarrow \operatorname{J}^0(C) \times \operatorname{J}^0(C)$, we conclude that $(i \times i)^* \mathcal P_{J/J}$ is maximal Cohen-Macaulay \cite[Lemma 2.3(2)]{Arinkin}; finally, since $\mathcal P$ pulls back to $(i \times i)^* \mathcal P_{J/J}$ under the \'etale map $M \times_B M \to M \times_B M^\vee$, we conclude that $\mathcal P$ is also maximal Cohen-Macaulay, and thus the shifted sheaf $\mathcal P^{-1}$ (the Grothendieck dual, up to shift and the line bundle $\omega_B$) is as well. The same argument applies to $\mathcal P_U^{-1}$. In particular, since $\mathcal P_U^{-1}$ and $L(1 \times \alpha)^* \mathcal P^{-1}$ are maximal Cohen-Macaulay extensions (the second assertion being \cite[Lemma 2.3]{Arinkin}) of the same line bundle defined away from codimension 2, by definition of $\mathcal P, \mathcal P_U$, we conclude from \cite[Lemma 2.2]{Arinkin} that $\mathcal P_U^{-1} \cong L(1 \times \alpha)^* \mathcal P^{-1}$. Note as well that $\iota_{\gamma,U}$ is a representable embedding of smooth quotients, and so by another application of \cite[Lemma 2.3(1)]{Arinkin} we see that $(1 \times \iota_{\gamma,U})^* \mathcal P_U^{-1} = L(1 \times \iota_{\gamma,U})^* \mathcal P_U^{-1}$.

    With these preliminaries, we rewrite the right side of (\ref{eq: prop restrict}) using
    $$\tau((1 \times \iota_{\gamma,U})^*\mathcal P_U^{-1})_\gamma = \tau(L(1 \times \iota_{\gamma,U})^*\mathcal P_U^{-1})_\gamma = \tau(L\phi^* \mathcal P^{-1})_\gamma = \tau(L(1 \times \alpha)^* L(1 \times \iota_\gamma)^* \mathcal P^{-1})_\gamma$$
    $$= \tau^{EG} \circ \rho_\gamma(L(1 \times \alpha)^* L(1 \times \iota_\gamma)^* \mathcal P^{-1})$$
    since $\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U) \times_U [\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U)^\gamma/\Gamma]$ is already $\gamma$-fixed, so $\iota_{\gamma *}^{-1}$ is trivial, and projecting to $\pi_g$ is not necessary by Proposition \ref{prop: EG factors through m1} and (\ref{eq: rho components})
    $$= \tau^{EG}((1 \times \alpha)^* \rho_\gamma(L(1 \times \iota_\gamma)^* \mathcal P^{-1}))$$
    as $(1 \times \alpha)$ is $\Gamma$-equivariant
    $$=(1 \times \alpha)^* \tau^{EG}(\rho_\gamma(L(1 \times \iota_\gamma)^* \mathcal P^{-1}))$$
    by \cite[Theorem 3.1(d)(1)]{EG-RRequivChow}, since $U \to B_\gamma$ is \'etale
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: restricting 1}
        \implies\tau((1 \times \iota_{\gamma,U})^*\mathcal P_U^{-1})_\gamma =(1 \times \alpha)^* \tau(L(1 \times \iota_\gamma)^* \mathcal P^{-1})_\gamma
    \end{equation}
    by the same argument with $\iota_{\gamma *}^{-1}, \pi_\gamma$ as before.

    On the left side, consider the representable regular embedding $(1 \times \iota_\gamma): M \times_BM^{\gamma, \vee} \hookrightarrow M \times_B M^\vee$. By Theorem \ref{thm: tau properties}(e) applied with $\mathcal Z := M \times M^{\gamma, \vee}$ and $\mathcal W := M \times M^\vee$, we see that
                                                                                                                                  
    \begin{equation*} \label{eq: reduce to U 1}
      \tau(\mathcal P^{-1})_\gamma = \operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(-T_{1 \times \iota_\gamma})_\gamma \cap \tau(L(1 \times \iota_\gamma)^*\mathcal P^{-1})_\gamma. 
    \end{equation*}
    Then
    $$\alpha^!\tau(\mathcal P^{-1})_\gamma := (1 \times \alpha)^* \tau(\mathcal P^{-1})_\gamma = (1 \times \alpha)^* \operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(-T_{1 \times \iota_\gamma})_\gamma \cap (1 \times \alpha)^* \tau(L(1 \times \iota_\gamma)^* \mathcal P^{-1})_\gamma.$$
    By (\ref{eq: restricting 1}), this completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- prop-21: body_md -->
\label{prop: comparison on V}
    There is an analytic open subset $V \subset U$ mapping homeomorphically onto its image $V \subset B_\gamma$ such that
    $$cl(\mathfrak G^{-1}_\gamma)|_V = (-1)^k cl(\tilde{\mathfrak G}^{-1}_{\gamma})|_V \circ cl(\Sigma)|_V \in H_*^{BM}(\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X_V/V) \times_V [\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X_V/V)^\gamma/\Gamma]),$$
    where $\Sigma := (f_P \times p_P)_*[\operatorname{PMod}_P] \in \operatorname{Corr}_U^{-k}(\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U), \operatorname{Prym}(\tilde X/U))$.
<!-- end prop-21 -->
<!-- proof-55: body_md -->
Combining Propositions \ref{prop: smooth and singular Poincare} and \ref{prop: tau B tau U}, and using the identification of $a_P: [\operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X/U)/\operatorname{J}^0(C)] \hookrightarrow [\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X/U)/\operatorname{J}^0(C)]$ with $\iota_{\gamma,U}: M^{\gamma,\vee}_U \hookrightarrow M^\vee_U$ from Proposition \ref{prop: a is restriction to Mgamma}, we have
    $$(-1)^k\alpha^! \tau(\mathcal P^{-1})_\gamma = (1 \times \alpha)^*\operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(-T_{1 \times \iota_\gamma})_\gamma \cap \tau((f_P \times 1)_*(q_1^*(\omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_P} \otimes \mathcal V_P^\vee) \otimes (p_P \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}^{-1}))_\gamma$$
    $$= (1 \times \alpha)^*\operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(-T_{1 \times \iota_\gamma})_\gamma \cap I(f_P \times 1)_{\gamma *}\tau((q_1^*(\omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_P} \otimes \mathcal V_P^\vee) \otimes (p_P \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}^{-1}))_\gamma$$
    $$= (1 \times \alpha)^*\operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(-T_{1 \times \iota_\gamma})_\gamma \cap I(f_P \times 1)_{\gamma *}(\operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}(q_1^*(\omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_P} \otimes \mathcal V_P^\vee))_\gamma \cap \tau((p_P \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}^{-1})_\gamma)$$
    $$= (1 \times \alpha)^*\operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(-T_{1 \times \iota_\gamma})_\gamma \cap I(f_P \times 1)_{\gamma *}(\operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}(q_1^*(\omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_P} \otimes \mathcal V_P^\vee))_\gamma \cap \operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(T_{p_P \times 1})_\gamma \cap I(p_P \times 1)^!_\gamma\tau(\tilde{\mathcal P}^{-1})_\gamma)$$
    $$\in \operatorname{CH}_*(\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U) \times_U [\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U)^\gamma/\Gamma])$$
    by applications of Theorem \ref{thm: tau properties}(c), (a), (d), respectively.

    Next, we apply the cycle class map and restrict to an open subset $V \subset U$ as in Lemma \ref{lem: ch and td cancel}, shrinking if necessary to ensure that $V$ maps homeomorphically onto its image under the \'etale map $U \to B_\gamma$. Because of the compatibilities recalled in \S \ref{subsubsec: constructible sheaves}, as well as the fact that proper pushforward in Borel-Moore homology commutes with restriction to an open subset (for schemes, thus immediately for representable morphisms), we see that
    $$(-1)^k cl(\tau(\mathcal P^{-1})_\gamma)|_V = \operatorname{\widetilde{td}}^{top}(-T_{1 \times \iota_\gamma}|_V)_\gamma \cap I(f_P \times 1)_{\gamma *}I(p_P \times 1)^*_\gamma cl(\tau(\tilde{\mathcal P}^{-1})_\gamma)|_V$$
    $$\in H^{BM}_*(\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X_V/V) \times_V [\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X_V/V)^\gamma/\Gamma]).$$
    Multiplying both sides by $\operatorname{\widetilde{td}}^{top}(T_{1 \times \iota_\gamma}|_V-\pi_V^* T_V)$ and using the projection formula, we obtain
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: restrict to V 1}
        \operatorname{\widetilde{td}}^{top}(T_{1 \times \iota_\gamma}|_V-\pi_V^* T_V)_\gamma \cap cl(\tau(\mathcal P^{-1})_\gamma)|_V = (-1)^k I(f_P \times 1)_{\gamma *} I(p_P \times 1)^*_\gamma cl(\tilde{\mathfrak G}^{-1}_{\gamma})|_V.
    \end{equation}
    Since $V \subset B_\gamma$ is a (Euclidean) open subset, the left side of (\ref{eq: restrict to V 1}) is
    \begin{equation*} \label{eq: restrict to V LHS}
        \operatorname{\widetilde{td}}^{top}(T_{1 \times \iota_\gamma}|_V-\pi_V^* T_V)_\gamma \cap cl(\tau(\mathcal P^{-1})_\gamma)|_V = cl(\operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(T_{1 \times \iota_\gamma} - \pi_{B_\gamma}^* T_{B_\gamma})_\gamma \cap \tau(\mathcal P^{-1})_\gamma)|_V = \mathfrak G^{-1}_\gamma|_V.
    \end{equation*}
    On the right side, note that by Lemma \ref{lem: composition with graphs}(a) we have
    $$I(f_P \times 1)_{\gamma *} I(p_P \times 1)^*_\gamma cl(\tilde{\mathfrak G}^{-1}_\gamma)|_V = cl(\tilde{\mathfrak G}^{-1}_\gamma \circ [\Gamma_{p_{P}}] \circ [\Gamma_{f_P}^T])|_V$$
    $$= cl(\tilde{\mathfrak G}^{-1}_\gamma \circ (f_P \times 1)_*[\Gamma_{p_P}])|_V =: cl(\tilde{\mathfrak G}^{-1}_\gamma \circ \Sigma)|_V.$$
    Finally, as before, because of the compatibilities of the class map and restriction to the open subset $V$ with pushforwards and pullbacks, we have
    $$cl(\tilde{\mathfrak G}^{-1}_\gamma \circ \Sigma)|_V = (cl(\tilde{\mathfrak G}^{-1}_\gamma) \circ cl(\Sigma))|_V = cl(\tilde{\mathfrak G}^{-1}_\gamma)|_V \circ cl(\Sigma)|_V.$$
    Thus (\ref{eq: restrict to V 1}) gives the needed equality.
<!-- end proof-55 -->
<!-- lem-24: body_md -->
\label{lem: ch and td cancel}
    In the situation of Proposition \ref{prop: comparison on V}, for each $u \in U$ there is an analytic open subset $u \in V \subset U$ on which
    $$\operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}^{top}(q_1^*(\omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_P} \otimes \mathcal V_P^\vee))_\gamma \cap \operatorname{\widetilde{td}}^{top}(T_{p_P \times 1})_\gamma \in H^*(\operatorname{PMod}_P \times_U [\operatorname{Prym}(\tilde X/U)/\Gamma])$$
    pulls back to $1 \in H^*(\operatorname{PMod}_P \times_U [\operatorname{Prym}(\tilde X/U)/\Gamma] \times_U V)$.
<!-- end lem-24 -->
<!-- proof-56: body_md -->
First, note that since $q_1^*(\omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_P} \otimes \mathcal V^\vee_P)$ and $T_{p_P \times 1} = q_1^* T_{p_P}$ are pulled back from the $\gamma$-fixed factor $\operatorname{PMod}_P$, in fact we have
    $$\operatorname{\widetilde{ch}}(q_1^*(\omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_P} \otimes \mathcal V_P^\vee))_\gamma \cap \operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(T_{p_P \times 1})_\gamma = q_1^*({\mathrm{ch}}(\omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_P} \otimes \mathcal V^\vee_P) \cap \operatorname{td}(T_{p_P})).$$
    Since the cycle class map is compatible with pullback, it therefore suffices to show that there is $V$ such that
    $$({\mathrm{ch}}^{top}(\omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_P} \otimes \mathcal V^\vee_P) \cap \operatorname{td}^{top}(T_{p_P}))|_V = 1 \in H^*(\operatorname{PMod}_P|_V).$$
    
    By Ehresmann's theorem, we may choose some contractible open $V \ni u$ such that the morphism $\operatorname{PMod}_P \to  U$ is topologically trivial; then restriction $H^*(\operatorname{PMod}_P|_V) \to H^*(\operatorname{PMod}_{P,u})$ is an isomorphism, and so it suffices to work over the point $u$.

    Note first that $\operatorname{PMod}_{P,u} \cong \operatorname{Prym}(\tilde X_u) \times ({\mathbb{P}}^1)^k$, as each ${\mathbb{P}}_i$ is the projectivization of the sum of topologically trivial line bundles $(\sigma_i^j \times 1)^* \tilde{\mathcal P}_{\tilde X_u/J}$ (which via the Abel-Jacobi map are restrictions of the universal bundle on $\mathop{\rm Pic}\nolimits^0(\operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X_u)) \times \operatorname{J}^0(\tilde X_u)$).
    Thus $T_{p_{P,u}} \cong T_{({\mathbb{P}}^1)^k} = a_1^* T_{{\mathbb{P}}^1} \oplus \cdots \oplus a_k^* T_{{\mathbb{P}}^1}$ and
    $$\operatorname{td}^{top}(T_{p_{P,u}}) \cong \otimes_i \operatorname{td}^{top}(a_i^* T_{{\mathbb{P}}^1}) = \prod_{i=1}^k a_i^*(1 + H_i),$$
    where $a_i: \operatorname{PMod}_{P,u} \to {\mathbb{P}}^1$ is the projection onto the $i^{\mathrm{th}}$ factor and $H_i$ the corresponding hyperplane class. On the other hand, note that $c_1^{top}(\mathcal V_{P,u}^{\otimes 2}) = c_1^{top}(\omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_{P,u}})$ by the relative Euler sequence (see \cite[Lemma 3.8]{FHHO}) and the fact that each factor ${\mathbb{P}}_i$ is the projectivization of a topologically trivial vector bundle. Since 
    $$c_1^{top}(\omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_{P,u}}) = \sum_{i=1}^k a_i^*(-2H_i)$$
    we conclude that (always in $H^*_{\mathbb{C}}$)
    $${\mathrm{ch}}^{top}(\omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_{P,u}} \otimes \mathcal V_{P,u}^\vee) = \exp\left(\frac{1}{2} \sum_{i=1}^k -2a^*_i(H_i)\right) = \prod_{i=1}^k (1 - a_i^* H_i).$$
    Thus
    $${\mathrm{ch}}^{top}(\omega_{\operatorname{PMod}_{P,u}} \otimes \mathcal V_{P,u}^\vee) \cap \operatorname{td}^{top}(T_{p_{P,u}}) = \prod_{i=1}^k(1- a_i^* H_i) \cap \prod_{i=1}^k(1 + a_i^* H_i)$$
    $$= \prod_{i=1}^k a_i^*(1 - H_i^2) = 1 \in H^*(\operatorname{PMod}_{P,u}).$$
<!-- end proof-56 -->
<!-- cor-8: body_md -->
\label{cor: Gi vs Fi}
    For each $i \in {\mathbb{Z}}$, recalling the homological realization isomorphism (\ref{eq: BM = sheaf Hom}) and the degree conventions of Definition \ref{def: G and p}, we have
    $$cl(\mathfrak G^{-1}_{\gamma,i+h-h_\gamma})|_V = \pm cl(\tilde{\mathfrak G}^{-1}_{\gamma,i})_V \circ cl(\Sigma)_V \in \operatorname{Hom}(\pi_{V*} {\mathbb{C}}_{M_V}, \pi_{V*}{\mathbb{C}}_{M^{\gamma, \vee}_V}[2(i-h)])$$
    and
    $$cl(\Sigma)|_V \circ cl(\mathfrak G_{\gamma,i})|_V = \pm cl(\tilde{\mathfrak G}_{\gamma, i-h+h_\gamma})|_V \in \operatorname{Hom}(\pi_{V*} {\mathbb{C}}_{M^{\gamma, \vee}_V}, \pi_{V*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}(\tilde X_V/V)}[2(i-h)]).$$
<!-- end cor-8 -->
<!-- proof-57: body_md -->
The first part is Proposition \ref{prop: comparison on V} taken one degree at a time. (Recall that $\Sigma = [\operatorname{PMod}_P]$ is of pure dimension $\dim \operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U)$.)
                                                                                                
                                                           
                         

    For the second part, recall from Proposition \ref{prop: G and G-1 inverse} that
    \begin{equation*} 
        \mathfrak G^{-1} \circ \mathfrak G = [\Delta_{IM}] \implies \mathfrak G^{-1}_\gamma \circ \mathfrak G_\gamma = [\Delta_{M^{\gamma, \vee}}].
    \end{equation*}
    It follows that
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: G PMod}
       cl(\tilde{\mathfrak G}_\gamma)|_V = cl(\tilde{\mathfrak G}_\gamma)|_V \circ cl(\mathfrak G^{-1}_\gamma)|_V \circ cl(\mathfrak G_\gamma)|_V
    \end{equation}
    $$ = \pm cl(\tilde{\mathfrak G}_\gamma)|_V  \circ cl(\tilde{\mathfrak G}^{-1}_\gamma)|_V \circ cl(\Sigma)|_V\circ cl(\mathfrak G_\gamma)|_V $$
    by the first part. We can rewrite the last expression as follows: first, by Corollary \ref{cor: Ggamma triv on other pieces}, we see that
    $$cl(\mathfrak G_{\gamma,i})|_V: \pi_{V*} {\mathbb{C}}_{M^{\gamma, \vee}_V} \to (\pi_{V*} {\mathbb{C}}_{M_V})_\kappa[2(i-h_\gamma)] \subset \pi_{V*} {\mathbb{C}}_{M_V}[2(i-h_\gamma)].$$
    Next, recall from Proposition \ref{prop: PMod = Sigma} that $ \Sigma \in \operatorname{Corr}_U^{h_\gamma - h}(\operatorname{\overline{\operatorname{Prym}}}(X/U), \operatorname{Prym}(\tilde X/U))$ can be defined as the closure of the graph of the $\Gamma$-equivariant pullback map $\nu^*: \operatorname{Prym}(X/U) \to \operatorname{Prym}(\tilde X/U)$, it is stable under the diagonal action of $\Gamma$ and so preserves isotypic components, i.e., we have
    $$cl(\Sigma)|_V: (\pi_{V*} {\mathbb{C}}_{M_V})_\kappa[2(i-h_\gamma)] \to (\pi_{V*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}(\tilde X_V/V)})_\kappa[2(i-h)].$$
    Finally, recall from Proposition \ref{prop: (ii) smooth} that
    $$\tilde{\mathfrak G}_\gamma \circ \tilde{\mathfrak G}_\gamma^{-1} \in \operatorname{Corr}^0_U(\operatorname{Prym}(\tilde X/U), \operatorname{Prym}(\tilde X/U))$$
    induces the projection
    $$\pi_{U*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}(\tilde X/U)} \to (\pi_{U*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}(\tilde X/U)})_\kappa$$
    and in particular acts trivially on the $\kappa$ component. Thus, as a composition we have
    $$cl(\tilde{\mathfrak G}_\gamma)|_V  \circ cl(\tilde{\mathfrak G}^{-1}_\gamma)|_V \circ cl(\Sigma)|_V\circ cl(\mathfrak G_\gamma)|_V =  cl(\Sigma)|_V\circ cl(\mathfrak G_\gamma)|_V.$$
    The statement then follows by taking degree pieces of (\ref{eq: G PMod}).
<!-- end proof-57 -->
<!-- proof-58: body_md -->
Fix $\gamma \in \Gamma$ and $k \in {\mathbb{N}}$. We only consider $\mathfrak p^{\mathfrak G}_k$; the proof for $\mathfrak q^{\mathfrak G}_k$ is identical. Recall from Corollary \ref{cor: Ggamma triv on other pieces} that $\mathfrak p^{\mathfrak G}_k$ is trivial on all isotypic components $(\pi_* {\mathbb{C}}_M)_{\kappa'}$ with $\kappa' \ne \kappa$, so it suffices to understand the image of $(\pi_* {\mathbb{C}}_M)_\kappa$. Exactly as in the proof of \cite[Theorem 2.6(ii)]{MSY}, by the condition that $(\pi_* {\mathbb{C}}_M)_\kappa$ has full support on $B_\gamma$, it suffices to show that $\mathfrak p_k^{\mathfrak G}$ has image $\prescript{\mathfrak p}{}{\tau}_{\le k + \dim B} (\pi_* {\mathbb{C}}_M)_\kappa$ after restricting to an analytic open subset $V \subset B_\gamma$.

    Over $V$, it follows from Corollary \ref{cor: Gi vs Fi} and the definition of $\mathfrak p_k^{\mathfrak G}$ that we have
    $$cl(\Sigma)|_V \circ cl(\mathfrak p_k^{\mathfrak G})|_V = \pm cl(\mathfrak p_{k-d_\gamma}^{\tilde{\mathfrak G}})|_V \circ cl(\Sigma)|_V \in \operatorname{Hom}(\pi_{V*} {\mathbb{C}}_{M_V}, \pi_{V*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}(\tilde X_V/V)}[-2d_\gamma]).$$
    Since $\Sigma$ is identified with Ng\^o's endoscopic correspondence by Proposition \ref{prop: PMod = Sigma}, it follows from \cite[Lemma 3.4.1]{Yun}, as in \cite[Proof of Theorem 3.10]{MS}, that $cl(\Sigma)|_V$
    induces an isomorphism of $\kappa$ components
    $$(\pi_{V*} {\mathbb{C}}_{M_V})_\kappa \xrightarrow{\sim} (\pi_{V*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}(\tilde X_V/V)})_\kappa[-2d_\gamma].$$
    Combining this with Proposition \ref{prop: (ii) smooth}, we conclude that
    $$cl(\mathfrak p_k^{\mathfrak G})|_V = \pm cl(\Sigma)|_V^{-1} \circ cl(\mathfrak p_{k-d_\gamma}^{\tilde{\mathfrak G}})|_V \circ cl(\Sigma)|_V$$
    is given by
    $$(\pi_{V*} {\mathbb{C}}_{M_V})_\kappa \xrightarrow{\sim} (\pi_{V*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}(\tilde X_V/V)})_\kappa[-2d_\gamma] \rightarrow (\prescript{\mathfrak p}{}{\tau}_{\le k-d_\gamma + b_\gamma}(\pi_{V*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}(\tilde X_V/V)})_\kappa)[-2d_\gamma] $$
    $$= \prescript{\mathfrak p}{}{\tau}_{\le k+d_\gamma + b_\gamma}((\pi_{V*} {\mathbb{C}}_{\operatorname{Prym}(\tilde X_V/V)})_\kappa[-2d_\gamma]) \xrightarrow{\sim} \prescript{\mathfrak p}{}{\tau}_{\le k+d_\gamma + b_\gamma}(\pi_{V*} {\mathbb{C}}_{M_V})_\kappa.$$
    It now suffices to note that $d_\gamma + b_\gamma = b$ by Corollary \ref{cor: h-hgamma}.
<!-- end proof-58 -->
<!-- lem-25: body_md -->
\label{lem: Kn KnJ}
    We have
    $$(p \times 1)^*\mathcal F^n = (1 \times p)_*\mathcal F^n_J \in D^b\mathrm{Coh}(M_J \times M^\vee).$$
<!-- end lem-25 -->
<!-- proof-59: body_md -->
We have
    $$(p \times 1)^*(\mathcal P^{-1} \circ (j_* \mathcal P)^{\otimes n}) := (p \times 1)^* p_{13*} (p_{12}^*(j_* \mathcal P)^{\otimes n} \otimes p_{23}^* \mathcal P^{-1})$$
    $$ = p_{13*}(p \times 1 \times 1)^* (p_{12}^*(j_* \mathcal P)^{\otimes n} \otimes p_{23}^* \mathcal P^{-1})$$
    since $(p \times 1)$ is flat
    $$ = p_{13*}((p_{12}^*(p \times 1)^*j_* \mathcal P)^{\otimes n} \otimes p_{23}^* \mathcal P^{-1}) = p_{13*}((p_{12}^* j_*' (p \times 1)^* \mathcal P)^{\otimes n} \otimes p_{23}^* \mathcal P^{-1})$$
    again since $(p \times 1)$ is flat (where here $j'$ is the inclusion $M_J \times_B M \hookrightarrow M_J \times M$)
    $$ = p_{13*}((p_{12}^* j_*' (1 \times i)^* \mathcal P_J)^{\otimes n} \otimes p_{23}^* \mathcal P^{-1})$$
    by definition of $\mathcal P$ (noting that there is no difference between derived and underived pullbacks because $p$ is flat, $i$ is a regular embedding, and $\mathcal P_J$ is maximal Cohen-Macaulay)
    $$ = p_{13*}((p_{12}^*(1 \times i)^* j_{J*} \mathcal P_J)^{\otimes n} \otimes p_{23}^* \mathcal P^{-1})$$
    by Lemma \ref{lem: Tor indep}(b), since $j', j_J$ are both flat base changes of the regular embedding $\Delta_B: B \hookrightarrow B \times B$
    $$= \mathcal P^{-1} \circ (1 \times i)^*(j_{J*} \mathcal P_J)^{\otimes n} = \mathcal P^{-1} \circ (\mathscr O_{\Gamma_i^T} \circ (j_{J*} \mathcal P_J)^{\otimes n})$$
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: Kn J}
        =(\mathcal P^{-1} \circ \mathscr O_{\Gamma_i^T}) \circ (j_{J*} \mathcal P_J)^{\otimes n} = (\mathscr O_{\Gamma_p} \circ \mathcal P^{-1}_J) \circ (j_{J*} \mathcal P_J)^{\otimes n}
    \end{equation}
    $$= \mathscr O_{\Gamma_p} \circ (\mathcal P^{-1}_J \circ (j_{J*} \mathcal P_J)^{\otimes n}) = (1 \times p)_* (\mathcal P^{-1}_J \circ (j_{J*} \mathcal P_J)^{\otimes n}).$$

    Note that the second equality of (\ref{eq: Kn J}) holds because
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: P-1 i}
        \mathcal P^{-1} \circ \mathscr O_{\Gamma_i^T} = \mathcal P^{-1} \circ \mathscr O_{\Gamma_i^T} \circ \mathcal P_J \circ \mathcal P_J^{-1} = \mathcal P^{-1} \circ \mathcal P \circ \mathscr O_{\Gamma_p} \circ \mathcal P_J^{-1} = \mathscr O_{\Gamma_p} \circ \mathcal P^{-1}_J
    \end{equation}
    where for the middle equality we again used that $(1 \times i)^* \mathcal P_J = (p \times 1)^* \mathcal P$.
<!-- end proof-59 -->
<!-- prop-22: body_md -->
\label{prop: Fn supp ineq}
    For any $\gamma, \beta \in \Gamma$ and $n \ge 1$, we have
    $$\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F^n) \cap M^{\gamma, \vee} \times M^{\beta, \vee}) \le b-h+h_\gamma+h_\beta.$$
<!-- end prop-22 -->
<!-- proof-60: body_md -->
Let $M^\gamma_J$ be the fixed locus of $\gamma$ acting on $M_J$, i.e., $p^{-1}(M^{\gamma,\vee})$. Then
    $$\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F^n) \cap M^{\gamma, \vee} \times M^{\beta,\vee}) = \dim(\operatorname{Supp}((p \times 1)^* \mathcal F^n) \cap M^\gamma_J \times M^{\beta, \vee}) -g$$
    $$= \dim(\operatorname{Supp}((1 \times p)_*\mathcal F^n_J) \cap M^\gamma_J \times M^{\beta,\vee}) -g$$
    by Lemma \ref{lem: Kn KnJ}
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: Fn support}
     \implies \dim(\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F^n) \cap M^{\gamma, \vee} \times M^{\beta,\vee})  \le \dim(\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F^n_J) \cap M^\gamma_J \times M^{\beta}_J) -g. 
    \end{equation}

    Now, by \cite[Proof of Proposition 3.3]{MSY}, we have
    $$\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F^n_J) \subset \{(\mathcal G_1, \mathcal G_2) \in \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_u)^{\times 2}: (\mathcal G_1|_{X_u^{\operatorname{sm}}})^{\otimes n} \cong \mathcal G_2|_{X_u^{\operatorname{sm}}}\} =: Z \subset M_J \times_B M_J \subset M_J \times M_J.$$
    We note that, for each $u \in B$, the restriction $Z_u \cap (M^\gamma_{J,u} \times_B M^\beta_{J,u}) \subset M^\gamma_{J,u} \times_B M^\beta_{J,u}$ is a countable union of closed subsets of codimension $g(\tilde X_u)$, as multiplication by $\operatorname{J}^0(X_u)$ preserves the fixed loci $\operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_u)^\gamma, \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_u)^\beta$ and so the argument of \cite[Proposition 7.4]{Arinkin} applies. Then
    $$\dim (\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F^n_J)|_u \cap (M^\gamma_{J,u} \times M^\beta_{J,u})) \le h_\gamma + g + h_\beta+g - g(\tilde X_u).$$
    Recall from Remark \ref{rmk: Severi/Ngo} that by the Severi inequality
    $$\dim \overline{\{u \in B: g(X_u) - g(\tilde X_u) \ge n\}} \le b - n$$
    and so we have (using that $g(X_u) = \dim M_J - b = h+g$)
    $$\dim (\operatorname{Supp} \mathcal F^n \cap M_J^{\gamma} \times M^{\beta}_J) \le b + 2g +h_\gamma + h_\beta - (h+g).$$
    Combining this with (\ref{eq: Fn support}), we obtain the needed result.
<!-- end proof-60 -->
<!-- prop-23: body_md -->
\label{prop: K on M and MJ}
    We have
    $$(p \times p \times 1)^* \mathcal K = (1 \times 1 \times p)_* \mathcal K_J \in D^b\mathrm{Coh}(M_J \times_B M_J \times_B M^\vee).$$
<!-- end prop-23 -->
<!-- proof-61: body_md -->
We have
    $$(p \times p \times 1)^* \mathcal K = \mathcal K \circ (\mathscr O_{\Gamma_p} \boxtimes \mathscr O_{\Gamma_p})$$
    $$:= \mathcal P^{-1} \circ \mathscr O_{\Delta^s_{M}} \circ (\mathcal P \boxtimes \mathcal P) \circ (\mathscr O_{\Gamma_p} \boxtimes \mathscr O_{\Gamma_p}) = \mathcal P^{-1} \circ \mathscr O_{\Delta^s_{M}} \circ (\mathscr O_{\Gamma_i^T} \boxtimes \mathscr O_{\Gamma_i^T}) \circ (\mathcal P_J \boxtimes \mathcal P_J)$$
    since $(p \times 1)^* \mathcal P = (1 \times i)^* \mathcal P_J$
    $$ = \mathcal P^{-1} \circ (i \times i \times 1)_*\mathscr O_{\Delta^s_{M}} \circ (\mathcal P_J \boxtimes \mathcal P_J)$$
    $$= \mathcal P^{-1} \circ (1 \times 1 \times i)^*\mathscr O_{\Delta^s_{M_J}} \circ (\mathcal P_J \boxtimes \mathcal P_J)$$
    by Lemma \ref{lem: Deltasm base change}
    $$= \mathcal P^{-1} \circ \mathscr O_{\Gamma_i^T} \circ \mathscr O_{\Delta^s_{M_J}}  \circ (\mathcal P_J \boxtimes \mathcal P_J)$$
    $$= \mathscr O_{\Gamma_p} \circ \mathcal P^{-1}_J \circ \mathscr O_{\Delta^s_{M_J}}  \circ (\mathcal P_J \boxtimes \mathcal P_J) =: \mathscr O_{\Gamma_p} \circ \mathcal K_J = (1 \times 1 \times p)_* \mathcal K_J$$
    where for the first equality we use (\ref{eq: P-1 i}).
<!-- end proof-61 -->
<!-- lem-26: body_md -->
\label{lem: Deltasm base change}
    We have
    $$(i \times i \times 1)_*\mathscr O_{\Delta^s_{M}} = (1 \times 1 \times i)^*\mathscr O_{\Delta^s_{M_J}} \in D^b\mathrm{Coh}(M_J \times_B M_J \times_B M).$$
<!-- end lem-26 -->
<!-- proof-62: body_md -->
Consider the Cartesian square
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        M \arrow[d, "i"] \arrow[r, "i \times i \times 1"] & M_J \times_B M_J \times_B M \arrow[d, "1 \times 1 \times i"] \\
        M_J \arrow[r, "1 \times 1 \times 1"] & M_J \times_B M_J \times_B M_J
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    Since $i: M \hookrightarrow M_J$ is an embedding of regular varieties, this and the flat base change $1 \times 1 \times i$ are regular embeddings of the same codimension $g$, and so by Lemma \ref{lem: Tor indep}(b) the square is $\operatorname{Tor}$-independent and
    $$(i \times i \times 1)_* \mathscr O_{\Delta^s_{M}} = (i \times i \times 1)_* i^* \mathscr O_{M_J}$$
    $$=(1 \times 1 \times i)^* (1 \times 1 \times 1)_* \mathscr O_{M_J} = (1 \times 1 \times i)^* \mathscr O_{\Delta^s_{M_J}}.$$
<!-- end proof-62 -->
<!-- prop-24: body_md -->
\label{prop: supp K endoscopic}
    For any $\gamma, \beta, \alpha \in \Gamma$, we have
    $$\dim(\operatorname{Supp} \mathcal K \cap M^{\gamma, \vee} \times_B M^{\beta, \vee} \times_B M^{\alpha, \vee}) \le b-h+h_\gamma + h_\beta + h_\alpha.$$
<!-- end prop-24 -->
<!-- proof-63: body_md -->
The proof is analogous to that of Proposition \ref{prop: Fn supp ineq}. By \cite[Proof of Proposition 3.2]{MSY}, over each point $u \in B$, the closed subset $\operatorname{Supp} \mathcal K_J|_u \subset \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_u)^{\times 3}$ is contained in the locus
    $$Z :=\{(\mathcal F_1, \mathcal F_2, \mathcal F_3): \mathcal F_1|_{X_u^{\operatorname{sm}}} \otimes \mathcal F_2|_{X_u^{\operatorname{sm}}} = \mathcal F_3|_{X_u^{\operatorname{sm}}} \} \subset \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_u)^{\times 3}.$$
    As before, $Z \cap \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_u)^\gamma \times \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_u)^\beta \times \operatorname{\overline{J}}^0(X_u)^\alpha$ is a countable union of closed subsets of codimension $ g(\tilde X_u)$. Then by the Severi inequality
    $$\dim (\operatorname{Supp} \mathcal K_J \cap M_J^{\gamma} \times_B M^{\beta}_J \times_B M^{\alpha}_J) \le b + 3g+ h_\gamma + h_\beta + h_\alpha - (h+g).$$
    Finally, by Proposition \ref{prop: K on M and MJ} we have
    $$\dim(\operatorname{Supp} \mathcal K \cap M^{\gamma, \vee} \times_B M^{\beta, \vee} \times_B M^{\alpha, \vee})  \le \dim(\operatorname{Supp} \mathcal K_J \cap M_J^{\gamma} \times_B M^{\beta}_J \times_B M^{\alpha}_J) - 2g.$$
<!-- end proof-63 -->
<!-- prop-25: body_md -->
\label{prop: psi support}
    The class
    $$(j_{u*}^T(1 \times u)^*(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P^{-1}_\gamma))) \circ (j_{u*}\psi^n((u \times 1)^*(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P_\gamma)) \in K_0(M^{\gamma, \vee}_\Gamma \times M_\Gamma^{\gamma, \vee})$$
    has support of dimension $\le 2 \dim u + b-h+2h_\gamma$, where
    $\mathcal F_\gamma := \iota_{\gamma *}^{-1} \circ \pi_\gamma(\mathcal F)$ is the localization defined in (\ref{eq: pi}) and (\ref{eq: iota}).
<!-- end prop-25 -->
<!-- proof-64: body_md -->
We have
    \begin{multline*}
        \operatorname{Supp} (j_{u*}^T(1 \times u)^*(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P^{-1}_\gamma)) \circ (j_{u*}\psi^n(u \times 1)^*(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P_\gamma)))) \\ \subset \operatorname{Supp} (j_{u*}^T(1 \times u)^*(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P^{-1}_\gamma)) \circ (j_{u*}(u \times 1)^*(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P_\gamma)))^{\otimes n})
    \end{multline*}
    since $j_{u*} \psi^n(\mathcal F)$ was defined inductively as a sum of products of exterior powers of $j_{u*} \mathcal F$ of degrees adding up to $n$, each of which is an $S_n$-isotypic component (and thus direct summand) of $(j_{u*} \mathcal F)^{\otimes n}$
    $$= \operatorname{Supp} ((1 \times u)^*(j_*^T(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P^{-1}_\gamma))) \circ (u \times 1)^*(j_*(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P_\gamma)))^{\otimes n})$$
    since $u$ is flat
    $$= (u \times u)^{-1} (\operatorname{Supp} (j^T_{\gamma *}(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P^{-1}_\gamma)) \circ (j_{\gamma *}(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P_\gamma)))^{\otimes n}))$$
    using the usual compatibility of flat pullback with proper pushforward and Gysin morphisms \cite[Lemmas 3.1, 3.2]{Anderson-Payne}, and using $j_\gamma: M^{\gamma,\vee} \times_B M \hookrightarrow M^{\gamma,\vee} \times M$ for the inclusion 
    $$ = (u \times u)^{-1} (\operatorname{Supp} (\rho_\gamma(j_{\gamma *}^T\mathcal P^{-1}_\gamma) \circ \rho_\gamma((j_{\gamma *}\mathcal P_\gamma)^{\otimes n})))$$
    since $j_\gamma$ is $\Gamma$-equivariant
    $$= (u \times u)^{-1} (\operatorname{Supp} ((j_{\gamma *}^T\mathcal P^{-1}_\gamma) \circ (j_{\gamma *}\mathcal P_\gamma)^{\otimes n}))$$
    since $\rho_\gamma(\mathcal F) \circ \rho_\gamma(\mathcal G) = \rho_{(\gamma, \gamma)}(\mathcal F \circ \mathcal G)$ and $\rho_{(\gamma, \gamma)}$ is an isomorphism of $K_0(M^{\gamma, \vee} \times M^{\gamma, \vee})$ compatible with $(\Gamma \times \Gamma)$-equivariant pushforward, thus respecting supports
    $$\subset (u \times u)^{-1}(\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal P^{-1} \circ (j_* \mathcal P)^{\otimes n}) \cap (M^{\gamma, \vee} \times M^{\gamma, \vee}))$$
    by Lemma \ref{lem: gamma loc vs intersect}. Thus it follows from Proposition \ref{prop: Fn supp ineq} that
    $$\dim \operatorname{Supp} (j_{u*}^T(1 \times u)^*(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P^{-1}_\gamma)) \circ (j_{u*}\psi^n(u \times 1)^*(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P_\gamma)))) \le 2\dim u + b-h+2h_\gamma.$$
<!-- end proof-64 -->
<!-- lem-27: body_md -->
\label{lem: gamma loc vs intersect}
    We have
    $$\operatorname{Supp}((j_{\gamma *}^T\mathcal P^{-1}_\gamma) \circ (j_{\gamma *} \mathcal P_\gamma)^{\otimes n}) \subset \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal P^{-1} \circ (j_*\mathcal P)^{\otimes n}) \cap (M^{\gamma, \vee} \times M^{\gamma, \vee}) \subset M^\vee \times M^\vee.$$
<!-- end lem-27 -->
<!-- proof-65: body_md -->
First, by (\ref{eq: pushforward loc}), we have $j_{\gamma *} \mathcal P_\gamma = (j_*\mathcal P)_\gamma$. Since $M^\vee \times M$ is smooth, recall from Lemma \ref{lem: localization inverse} that
    $$(j_* \mathcal P)_\gamma = \lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N_{\iota_\gamma}^\vee)^{-1} \cdot \iota_\gamma^!(j_*\mathcal P) \in K_0(M^{\gamma, \vee} \times M),$$
    where $\iota_\gamma: M^{\gamma, \vee} \times M \hookrightarrow M^\vee \times M$ is the inclusion of the fixed locus. In particular, we conclude that
    $$(j_{\gamma *} \mathcal P_\gamma)^{\otimes n} = (\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N_{\iota_\gamma}^\vee)^{-1} \cdot \iota_\gamma^!(j_*\mathcal P))^{\otimes n}$$
    $$= \lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N_{\iota_\gamma}^\vee)^{-n} \cdot \iota_\gamma^!((j_*\mathcal P)^{\otimes n}) = \lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N_{\iota_\gamma}^\vee)^{-n+1} \cdot ((j_*\mathcal P)^{\otimes n})_\gamma.$$
    Thus, with another application of (\ref{eq: pushforward loc}) we have
    $$(j_{\gamma *}^T\mathcal P^{-1}_\gamma) \circ (j_{\gamma *} \mathcal P_\gamma)^{\otimes n} = (j_{*}^T\mathcal P^{-1})_\gamma \circ (\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N_{\iota_\gamma}^\vee)^{-n+1} \cdot ((j_*\mathcal P)^{\otimes n})_\gamma)$$
    $$= p_1^*\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal N_{M^{\gamma,\vee}/M^\vee}^\vee)^{-n+1} \cdot ((j_*^T\mathcal P^{-1})_\gamma \circ ((j_*\mathcal P)^{\otimes n})_\gamma)$$
    by the projection formula, and so
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: move loc}
        \operatorname{Supp} ((j_{\gamma *}^T\mathcal P^{-1}_\gamma) \circ (j_{\gamma *} \mathcal P_\gamma)^{\otimes n}) \subset \operatorname{Supp}((j^T_*\mathcal P^{-1})_\gamma \circ ((j_*\mathcal P)^{\otimes n})_\gamma).
    \end{equation}

    Next, we claim that
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: composition loc}
        (j_*^T\mathcal P^{-1})_\gamma \circ ((j_*\mathcal P)^{\otimes n})_\gamma = ((j_*^T\mathcal P^{-1}) \circ (j_*\mathcal P)^{\otimes n})_{(\gamma,\gamma)} \in K_0(M^{\gamma, \vee} \times M^{\gamma, \vee}).
    \end{equation}
    Indeed, we have
    $$((j_*^T\mathcal P^{-1}) \circ (j_*\mathcal P)^{\otimes n})_{(\gamma,\gamma)} := (p_{13*}\delta_M^! ((j_*\mathcal P)^{\otimes n} \boxtimes (j_*^T\mathcal P^{-1})))_{(\gamma, \gamma)}$$
    $$ = p_{13*}((\delta_M^! ((j_*\mathcal P)^{\otimes n} \boxtimes (j_*^T\mathcal P^{-1})))_{(\gamma, \gamma)})$$
    by (\ref{eq: pushforward loc}), applied to both the (proper) inclusion $M^{\gamma,\vee} \times_B M \times_B M^{\gamma,\vee} \hookrightarrow M^{\gamma,\vee} \times M \times M^{\gamma,\vee}$ and the (proper) projection map $M^{\gamma,\vee} \times_B M \times_B M^{\gamma,\vee} \to M^{\gamma,\vee} \times M^{\gamma,\vee}$
    $$ = p_{13*}\delta_M^! (((j_*\mathcal P)^{\otimes n} \boxtimes (j_*^T\mathcal P^{-1}))_{(\gamma, \gamma)})$$
    by the first equality in Lemma \ref{lem: pullback first step}
    $$ = p_{13*}\delta_M^! (((j_*\mathcal P)^{\otimes n})_\gamma \boxtimes (j_*^T\mathcal P^{-1})_\gamma) \,\,\,\,\, \mathrm{by}\,\, (\ref{eq: boxtimes loc})$$
    $$ =: (j_*^T\mathcal P^{-1})_\gamma \circ ((j_*\mathcal P)^{\otimes n})_\gamma.$$

    Finally, we note that
    $$(j_*^T\mathcal P^{-1}) \circ (j_* \mathcal P)^{\otimes n} = \mathcal P^{-1} \circ (j_* \mathcal P)^{\otimes n}$$
    by compatibility of proper pushforward with Gysin morphisms \cite[Lemma 3.1]{Anderson-Payne}, and so, combining with (\ref{eq: move loc}) and (\ref{eq: composition loc}), we obtain
    $$\operatorname{Supp} ((j_{\gamma *}^T\mathcal P^{-1}_\gamma) \circ (j_{\gamma *} \mathcal P_\gamma)^{\otimes n}) \subset \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal P^{-1} \circ (j_* \mathcal P)^{\otimes n})_{(\gamma,\gamma)}$$
    $$ \subset \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal P^{-1} \circ (j_*\mathcal P)^{\otimes n}) \cap (M^{\gamma, \vee} \times M^{\gamma,\vee})$$
    because in general, given $\mathcal X = [X/G]$, since $\iota_{g *}^{-1} \circ \pi_g$ commutes with $G$-equivariant proper pushforward by (\ref{eq: pushforward loc}), in particular $\iota_{g*}^{-1} \circ \pi_g(\mathcal F)$ is supported on $(\operatorname{Supp} \mathcal F)^g$.
<!-- end proof-65 -->
<!-- prop-26: body_md -->
\label{prop: sheaf to tau supp}
    We have
    \begin{multline*}
        \dim ((1 \times u)^* \mathfrak G_\gamma^{-1} \circ ({\mathrm{ch}}^{loc}(\psi^n((u \times 1)^*(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P_\gamma)))) \cap [M^{\gamma, \vee}_\Gamma \times M])) \\ \le \dim \operatorname{Supp} (j_{u*}^T(1 \times u)^*(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P^{-1}_\gamma)) \circ j_{u*}\psi^n((u \times 1)^*(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P_\gamma))))
    \end{multline*}
    where by dimension of a class of $\operatorname{CH}_*(M^{\gamma,\vee} \times_B M^{\gamma,\vee})$ we mean the highest $k$ such that the $\operatorname{CH}_k$ component is nonzero.
<!-- end prop-26 -->
<!-- proof-66: body_md -->
By the standard properties of the (schematic) $\tau$ functor \cite[Theorem 18.2, Example 18.3.1]{Fulton}, and again using that $p_{13}$ is proper on the support of the element of $K_0(M^{\gamma,\vee}_\Gamma \times M \times M^{\gamma,\vee}_\Gamma)$ under consideration, we have
    $$\tau(j_{u*}^T(1 \times u)^*(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P^{-1}_\gamma)) \circ j_{u*}\psi^n((u \times 1)^*(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P_\gamma))))$$
    $$= p_{13*}(\operatorname{td}(-p_2^* T_M) \cap \delta_M^!(j_{u*}\tau(\psi^n((u \times 1)^*(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P_\gamma)))) \times j_{u*}^T\tau((1 \times u)^*\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P^{-1}_\gamma))))$$
    $$= p_{13*}(\operatorname{td}(-p_2^* T_M) \cap \Delta_M^!(\tau(\psi^n((u \times 1)^*(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P_\gamma)))) \times \tau((1 \times u)^*\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P^{-1}_\gamma))))$$
    since $\delta_M$ is a flat base change of $\Delta_M$, and by compatibility of proper pushforward with Gysin morphisms and pushforward
    $$ = p_{13*}\Delta_M^!((\operatorname{td}(-p_2^* T_M) \cap \tau(\psi^n((u \times 1)^*(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P_\gamma))))) \times \tau((1 \times u)^*\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P^{-1}_\gamma)))$$
    $$ = \tau((1 \times u)^* \rho_\gamma(\mathcal P^{-1})) \circ (\operatorname{td}(p_1^*T_{M^{\gamma,\vee}_\Gamma}) \cap {\mathrm{ch}}^{loc}(\psi^n((u \times 1)^* \rho_\gamma(\mathcal P_\gamma))) \cap [M^{\gamma,\vee}_\Gamma \times M])$$
    $$ = (1 \times u)^*\tau^{EG}( \rho_\gamma(\mathcal P^{-1})) \circ (\operatorname{td}(p_1^*T_{M^{\gamma,\vee}_\Gamma}) \cap {\mathrm{ch}}^{loc}(\psi^n((u \times 1)^* \rho_\gamma(\mathcal P_\gamma)))\cap [M^{\gamma,\vee}_\Gamma \times M])$$
    by definition of $\tau^{EG}$
    \begin{multline*}
        = \operatorname{td}(p_1^* T_{M^{\gamma,\vee}_\Gamma} + p_2^*\pi_{B_\gamma}^* T_{B_\gamma}) \cap p_2^* u^* \operatorname{td}^I(-T_{\iota_{M^\vee}})_\gamma \\ \cap  ((1 \times u)^*\mathfrak G^{-1}_\gamma \circ ({\mathrm{ch}}^{loc}(\psi^n((u \times 1)^* \rho_\gamma(\mathcal P_\gamma)))\cap [M^{\gamma,\vee}_\Gamma \times M])).
    \end{multline*}
    In particular, we conclude that
    \begin{multline*}
        \dim \tau(j_{u*}^T(1 \times u)^*(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P^{-1}_\gamma)) \circ j_{u*}\psi^n((u \times 1)^*(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P_\gamma)))) \\ = \dim ((1 \times u)^*\mathfrak G^{-1}_\gamma \circ ({\mathrm{ch}}^{loc}(\psi^n((u \times 1)^* \rho_\gamma(\mathcal P_\gamma)))\cap [M^{\gamma,\vee}_\Gamma \times M])).
    \end{multline*}
    Thus, it suffices to note that in general
    $$\dim \operatorname{Supp} \mathcal F \ge \dim \tau(\mathcal F)$$
    by compatibility of $\tau$ with proper pushforward.
<!-- end proof-66 -->
<!-- prop-27: body_md -->
\label{prop: FV}
    (Fourier vanishing) We have
    $$\mathfrak G_{\beta,i}^{-1} \circ \mathfrak G_{\gamma,j} = 0 \,\,\, \mathrm{if} \,\, \begin{cases}
        \beta \ne \gamma \\
        \beta = \gamma, i+j<2h.
    \end{cases}$$
<!-- end prop-27 -->
<!-- proof-67: body_md -->
The first part is Proposition \ref{prop: FV for different chars}. As for the second, we start by noting that by construction of $u$ we have
    $$\mathfrak G_{\gamma,i}^{-1} \circ \mathfrak G_{\gamma,j} = 0 \iff (u \times u)^*(\mathfrak G_{\gamma,i}^{-1} \circ \mathfrak G_{\gamma,j}) = ((1 \times u)^* \mathfrak G_{\gamma,i}^{-1}) \circ ((u \times 1)^* \mathfrak G_{\gamma,j}) = 0 $$
    (where the second equality is because Gysin pullback $\Delta_M^!$ and projective pushforward $p_{13*}$ commute with flat pullback). By definition and the projection formula, we have
    \begin{multline*}
        ((1 \times u)^* \mathfrak G_{\gamma,i}^{-1}) \circ ((u \times 1)^* \mathfrak G_{\gamma,j}) \\ = \sum_{a \ge 0} \operatorname{td}^a(\pi_{B_\gamma}^* T_{B_\gamma}) \cap \left( (1 \times u)^* \mathfrak G_{\gamma, i}^{-1} \circ ({\mathrm{ch}}^{loc, j-a+b_\gamma}((u \times 1)^*(\rho(\mathcal P_\gamma))) \cap [M^{\gamma, \vee}_\Gamma \times M]) \right).
    \end{multline*}
    It therefore suffices to show that
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: FV with chloc}
        (1 \times u)^* \mathfrak G_{\gamma,i}^{-1} \circ ({\mathrm{ch}}^{loc,k}((u \times 1)^*(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P_\gamma))) \cap [M^{\gamma,\vee}_\Gamma \times M]) = 0
    \end{equation}
    for $i + k < 2h+b_\gamma$.

    Now, combining Propositions \ref{prop: psi support} and \ref{prop: sheaf to tau supp}, for each $n \ge 1$ and $a < b_\gamma - b + h = h_\gamma$ (Remark \ref{rmk: h-hgamma}) we have
    $$\left[(1 \times u)^* \mathfrak G_\gamma^{-1} \circ ({\mathrm{ch}}^{loc}(\psi^n((u \times 1)^*(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P_\gamma)))) \cap [M^{\gamma, \vee}_\Gamma \times M])\right]_{\operatorname{codim} = a} = 0$$
    $$ = \sum_{j \ge 0} (1 \times u)^* \mathfrak G_{\gamma,a+h+b-j}^{-1} \circ {\mathrm{ch}}^{loc, j}(\psi^n((u \times 1)^*(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P_\gamma)))) \cap [M^{\gamma, \vee}_\Gamma \times M]$$
    $$ = \sum_{j \ge 0} n^j (1 \times u)^* \mathfrak G_{\gamma,a+h+b-j}^{-1} \circ {\mathrm{ch}}^{loc, j}((u \times 1)^*(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P_\gamma))) \cap [M^{\gamma, \vee}_\Gamma \times M]$$
    by (\ref{eq: Kurano-Roberts}). Since this is true for all $n \ge 1$, we conclude that each term
    $$(1 \times u)^* \mathfrak G_{\gamma,a+h+b-j}^{-1} \circ {\mathrm{ch}}^{loc, j}((u \times 1)^*(\rho_\gamma(\mathcal P_\gamma))) \cap [M_\Gamma^{\gamma, \vee} \times M] = 0$$
    In other words, this is true for $j \ge 0$ and $a <h_\gamma$ and so for
    $$i+k = a+h+b = a + h + (b_\gamma + h - h_\gamma) < 2h + b_\gamma.$$
<!-- end proof-67 -->
<!-- proof-68: body_md -->
We have
    $$\mathfrak p_{\gamma,k}^{\mathfrak G} = [\Delta_M] \circ \mathfrak p_{\gamma, k}^{\mathfrak G} = \sum_{i \ge 0} \mathfrak G_i \circ \mathfrak G^{-1}_{2h-i} \circ \mathfrak p_{\gamma,k}^{\mathfrak G}$$
    by Proposition \ref{prop: G and G-1 inverse} and the fact that $[\Delta_M] \in \operatorname{Corr}^0_B(M,M)$
    $$ = \sum_\beta \sum_{i \ge 0} \mathfrak G_{\beta,i} \circ \mathfrak G_{\beta,2h-i}^{-1} \circ \sum_{j \le k} \mathfrak G_{\gamma,j} \circ \mathfrak G_{\gamma, 2h-j}^{-1}$$
    $$= \sum_{i \ge 0} \mathfrak G_{\gamma,i} \circ \mathfrak G_{\gamma,2h-i}^{-1} \circ\sum_{j \le k} \mathfrak G_{\gamma,j} \circ \mathfrak G_{\gamma, 2h-j}^{-1}$$
    by Proposition \ref{prop: FV for different chars}
    $$= \sum_{i \le k} \mathfrak G_{\gamma,i} \circ \mathfrak G_{\gamma,2h-i}^{-1} \circ\sum_{j \le k} \mathfrak G_{\gamma,j} \circ \mathfrak G_{\gamma, 2h-j}^{-1} = \mathfrak p_{\gamma,k}^{\mathfrak G} \circ \mathfrak p_{\gamma,k}^{\mathfrak G}$$
    by Proposition \ref{prop: FV}. Moreover, for any $\beta \ne \gamma$ we note that
    $$\mathfrak p_{\beta,j}^{\mathfrak G} \circ \mathfrak p^{\mathfrak G}_{\gamma,k} = 0 = \mathfrak p^{\mathfrak G}_{\gamma,k} \circ \mathfrak p_{\beta,j}^{\mathfrak G} $$
    by Proposition \ref{prop: FV for different chars}, and so any sum $\sum_\gamma \mathfrak p_{\gamma, k_\gamma}^{\mathfrak G} = \mathfrak{p}^{\mathfrak{G}}_{(k_\gamma)_\gamma}$ is a projector. It follows immediately that the difference
    $$[\Delta_M] - \sum_\gamma \mathfrak p_{\gamma,k_\gamma}^{\mathfrak G} = \sum_\gamma \mathfrak q_{\gamma, k_\gamma+1}^{\mathfrak G} = \mathfrak{q}^{\mathfrak{G}}_{(k_\gamma+1)_\gamma}$$
    is a projector orthogonal to $\mathfrak{p}^{\mathfrak{G}}_{(k_\gamma)_\gamma}$.
<!-- end proof-68 -->
<!-- prop-28: body_md -->
\label{prop: C identity}
    We have
    $$\mathfrak G \circ \mathfrak C \circ (\mathfrak G^{-1} \times \mathfrak G^{-1}) = [\Delta_M^s] \in \operatorname{CH}_*(M \times_B M \times_B M).$$
<!-- end prop-28 -->
<!-- proof-69: body_md -->
First, from the definition of $\mathcal K$, we obtain
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: C before tau}
        \mathcal P \circ \mathcal K \circ (\mathcal P^{-1} \boxtimes \mathcal P^{-1}) = \mathscr O_{\Delta^s_M}
    \end{equation}
    since $\mathcal P \circ \mathcal P^{-1} = \mathscr O_{\Delta_M}$, composition is associative, and $(\mathcal A \boxtimes \mathcal B) \circ (\mathcal C \boxtimes \mathcal D) = (\mathcal A \circ \mathcal C) \boxtimes (\mathcal B \circ \mathcal D)$. As usual, we apply $\tau$ to both sides of (\ref{eq: C before tau}), using the properties established in Theorem \ref{thm: tau properties}. (We will use these properties without comment, and whenever we are applying Corollary \ref{cor: part e}, we take $\mathcal Z_i$ to be $\mathcal Y_i$ with all $\times_B$ replaced by $\times$.) 

    On the left, we start by calculating
    $$\tau(\mathcal K \circ (\mathcal P^{-1} \boxtimes \mathcal P^{-1})) := \tau(p_{125*} \delta_{M^\vee_1}^* \delta_{M^\vee_2}^*(\mathcal P^{-1} \boxtimes \mathcal P^{-1} \boxtimes \mathcal K))$$
    $$ = Ip_{125*} \tau(\delta_{M^\vee_1}^* \delta_{M^\vee_2}^*(\mathcal P^{-1} \boxtimes \mathcal P^{-1} \boxtimes \mathcal K))$$
    $$= Ip_{125*}(\operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(-p_3^*T_{M^\vee}) \cap I\Delta_{M^\vee_1}^!\tau(\delta_{M^\vee_2}^*(\mathcal P^{-1} \boxtimes \mathcal P^{-1} \boxtimes \mathcal K)))$$
    $$= Ip_{125*}(\operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(-p_3^*T_{M^\vee}) \cap I\Delta_{M^\vee_1}^!(\operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(-p_5^* T_{M^\vee}) \cap I\Delta^!_{M^\vee_2}(\tau(\mathcal P^{-1} \boxtimes \mathcal P^{-1} \boxtimes \mathcal K))))$$
    $$= Ip_{125*}(\operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(-p_3^*T_{M^\vee}-p_4^* T_{M^\vee}) \cap I\Delta_{M^\vee_1}^! I\Delta^!_{M^\vee_2}(\tau(\mathcal P^{-1}) \times \tau(\mathcal P^{-1}) \times \tau(\mathcal K)))$$
    \begin{multline*}
        = Ip_{125*}I\Delta_{M^\vee_1}^! I\Delta^!_{M^\vee_2}((\operatorname{td}^I(-\pi_{IB}^* T_{IB} + p_2^* T_{\iota_{M^\vee}}) \cap  \tau(\mathcal P^{-1})) \times (\operatorname{td}^I(-\pi_{IB}^* T_{IB} + p_2^* T_{\iota_{M^\vee}}) \cap  \tau(\mathcal P^{-1})) \\ \times
    (\operatorname{td}^I(p_1^*(\pi_{IB}^* T_{IB} - T_{IM^\vee}) + p_2^*(\pi_{IB}^* T_{IB} - T_{IM^\vee})) \cap \tau(\mathcal K)))
    \end{multline*}
    $$ = Ip_{125*}I\Delta_{M^\vee_1}^! I\Delta^!_{M^\vee_2}(\mathfrak G^{-1} \times \mathfrak G^{-1} \times (\operatorname{td}^I(p_3^*(\pi_{IB}^* T_{IB} - T_{\iota_M^\vee})) \cap \mathfrak C))$$
    $$ = \operatorname{td}^I(p_3^*(\pi_{IB}^* T_{IB} - T_{\iota_M^\vee})) \cap Ip_{125*}I\Delta_{M^\vee_1}^! I\Delta^!_{M^\vee_2}(\mathfrak G^{-1} \times \mathfrak G^{-1} \times \mathfrak C)$$
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: C 1}
        \implies \tau(\mathcal K \circ (\mathcal P^{-1} \boxtimes \mathcal P^{-1})) = \operatorname{td}^I(p_3^*(\pi_{IB}^* T_{IB} - T_{\iota_M^\vee})) \cap (\mathfrak C \circ (\mathfrak G^{-1} \times \mathfrak G^{-1})).
    \end{equation}
    
    Then
    $$\tau(\mathcal P \circ \mathcal K \circ (\mathcal P^{-1} \boxtimes \mathcal P^{-1})) := \tau(p_{124*} \delta_{M^\vee}^*((\mathcal K \circ (\mathcal P^{-1} \boxtimes \mathcal P^{-1})) \boxtimes \mathcal P))$$
    $$ = Ip_{124*} \tau(\delta_{M^\vee}^*((\mathcal K \circ (\mathcal P^{-1} \boxtimes \mathcal P^{-1})) \boxtimes \mathcal P))$$
    $$ = Ip_{124*}(\operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(-p_3^* T_{M^\vee}) \cap I\Delta_{M^\vee}^!\tau((\mathcal K \circ (\mathcal P^{-1} \boxtimes \mathcal P^{-1})) \boxtimes \mathcal P))$$
    $$ = Ip_{124*}(\operatorname{\widetilde{td}}(-p_3^* T_{M^\vee}) \cap I\Delta_{M^\vee}^!(\tau(\mathcal K \circ (\mathcal P^{-1} \boxtimes \mathcal P^{-1})) \times \tau(\mathcal P)))$$
    \begin{multline*}
        = Ip_{124*} I\Delta_{M^\vee}^!((\operatorname{td}^I(-p_3^* \pi_{IB}^* T_{IB} + p_3^* T_{\iota_{M^\vee}}) \cap  \tau(\mathcal K \circ (\mathcal P^{-1} \boxtimes \mathcal P^{-1}))) \\ \times (\operatorname{td}^I(\pi_{IB}^* T_{IB} - p_1^* T_{IM^\vee}) \cap \tau(\mathcal P)))
    \end{multline*}
    $$ = (\operatorname{td}^I(p_2^* T_M) \cap \mathfrak G) \circ (\operatorname{td}^I(-p_3^* \pi_{IB}^* T_{IB} + p_3^* T_{\iota_{M^\vee}}) \cap  \tau(\mathcal K \circ (\mathcal P^{-1} \boxtimes \mathcal P^{-1})))$$
    $$ = (\operatorname{td}^I(p_2^* T_M) \cap \mathfrak G) \circ (\mathfrak C \circ (\mathfrak G^{-1} \times \mathfrak G^{-1}))$$
    by (\ref{eq: C 1})
    $$ = \operatorname{td}^I(p_3^* T_M) \cap (\mathfrak G \circ \mathfrak C \circ (\mathfrak G^{-1} \times \mathfrak G^{-1}))$$
    by the projection formula. Thus, applying $\tau$ to (\ref{eq: C before tau}) we obtain
    $$\operatorname{td}^I(p_3^* T_M) \cap (\mathfrak G \circ \mathfrak C \circ (\mathfrak G^{-1} \times \mathfrak G^{-1})) = \tau(\mathscr O_{\Delta^s_M}) = \operatorname{td}(p_3^* T_M) \cap [\Delta_M^s]$$
    and as $\operatorname{td}^I(p_3^* T_M) = \operatorname{td}(p_3^* T_M)$ is invertible, we are done.
<!-- end proof-69 -->
<!-- proof-70: body_md -->
By Proposition \ref{prop: C identity} we have
    $$\mathfrak{q}^{\mathfrak{G}}_{k+l+1} \circ [\Delta_M^s] \circ (\mathfrak{p}^{\mathfrak{G}}_k \times \mathfrak{p}^{\mathfrak{G}}_l) = \mathfrak{q}^{\mathfrak{G}}_{k+l+1} \circ  \mathfrak G \circ \mathfrak C \circ (\mathfrak G^{-1} \times \mathfrak G^{-1})\circ (\mathfrak{p}^{\mathfrak{G}}_k \times \mathfrak{p}^{\mathfrak{G}}_l)$$
    $$ = (\mathfrak{q}^{\mathfrak{G}}_{k+l+1} \circ  \mathfrak G) \circ \mathfrak C \circ ((\mathfrak G^{-1} \circ \mathfrak{p}^{\mathfrak{G}}_k) \times (\mathfrak G^{-1} \circ \mathfrak{p}^{\mathfrak{G}}_l)).$$
    Now, by Fourier vanishing (Proposition \ref{prop: FV}) we note that
    $$\mathfrak G^{-1}_\gamma \circ \mathfrak{p}^{\mathfrak{G}}_k = \mathfrak G^{-1}_\gamma \circ \mathfrak{p}^{\mathfrak{G}}_{\gamma,k} = \sum_{i\ge 0} \mathfrak G_{\gamma,i}^{-1} \circ \sum_{j \le k} \mathfrak G_{\gamma,j} \circ \mathfrak G_{\gamma,2h-j}^{-1} = \sum_{i \ge 2h-k} \mathfrak G_{\gamma,i}^{-1} \circ \mathfrak{p}^{\mathfrak{G}}_{\gamma,k} \in \operatorname{Corr}_B^{\ge h_\gamma-k}(M, M^{\gamma,\vee})$$
    and similarly for $\mathfrak G^{-1}_\beta \circ \mathfrak{p}^{\mathfrak{G}}_k$ and
    $$\mathfrak{q}^{\mathfrak{G}}_{k+l+1} \circ  \mathfrak G_\alpha =\mathfrak{q}^{\mathfrak{G}}_{\alpha, k+l+1} \circ \sum_{a\ge k+l+1} \mathfrak G_{\alpha,i} \in \operatorname{Corr}_B^{\ge k+l+1 - h_\alpha}(M^{\alpha,\vee},M) .$$
    Note as well that
    $$\mathfrak C_{(\gamma,\beta,\alpha)} \in \operatorname{Corr}_B^{\ge h_\alpha - h_\beta -h_\gamma}(M^{\gamma,\vee}, M^{\beta,\vee}; M^{\alpha,\vee})$$
    as by definition of $\mathfrak C$ we have
    $$\dim \mathfrak C_{(\gamma,\beta,\alpha)} = \dim \tau(\mathcal K)_{(\gamma,\beta,\alpha)} \le \dim (\operatorname{Supp} \mathcal K) \cap M^{\gamma,\vee} \times_B M^{\beta,\vee} \times_B M^{\alpha,\vee} \le b-h+h_\gamma+h_\beta+h_\alpha$$
    by Proposition \ref{prop: supp K endoscopic}.
    Putting this all together, we have
    $$\mathfrak{q}^{\mathfrak{G}}_{k+l+1} \circ [\Delta_M^s] \circ (\mathfrak{p}^{\mathfrak{G}}_k \times \mathfrak{p}^{\mathfrak{G}}_l) = \sum_{\gamma,\beta,\alpha \in \Gamma} \mathfrak{q}^{\mathfrak{G}}_{k+l+1} \circ  \mathfrak G_\alpha \circ \mathfrak C_{(\gamma,\beta,\alpha)} \circ ((\mathfrak G^{-1}_\gamma \circ \mathfrak{p}^{\mathfrak{G}}_k) \times( \mathfrak G^{-1}_\beta \circ \mathfrak{p}^{\mathfrak{G}}_l))$$
    $$\in \operatorname{Corr}_B^{\ge h_\gamma -k + h_\beta - l + h_\alpha - h_\beta - h_\gamma + k+l+1 - h_\alpha}(M,M;M) = \operatorname{Corr}_B^{\ge 1}(M,M;M).$$
    But since the composition
    $$\mathfrak{q}^{\mathfrak{G}}_{k+l+1} \circ [\Delta_M^s] \circ (\mathfrak{p}^{\mathfrak{G}}_k \times \mathfrak{p}^{\mathfrak{G}}_l) \in \operatorname{Corr}_B^0(M,M;M)$$
    we conclude this must be 0.
    
    Finally, since the homological realizations of $\mathfrak{p}^{\mathfrak{G}}_k, \mathfrak{p}^{\mathfrak{G}}_l, \mathfrak{q}^{\mathfrak{G}}_{k+l+1}$ are the perverse truncations described in Theorem \ref{thm: main sec 2}(ii) and the homological realization of $[\Delta_M^s]$ is the cup product, after taking cohomology we obtain the statement that
    $$P_kH^*(M) \cup P_lH^*(M) \xrightarrow{\cup} H^*(M) \twoheadrightarrow H^*(M)/P_{k+l}H^*(M)$$
    is trivial, i.e., the perverse filtration is multiplicative.
<!-- end proof-70 -->
